Enforced: 4,000,000 points a line, now 24 GPU bytes a point (16 for the point, 8 for its neighbour indices), 96,000,000 bytes at most, under the 128 MiB default storage binding. | A segment instance sees only its own points and one neighbour on each side, so it needs the index of the nearest distinct one; the CPU finds it once per change in one pass. | 8 more GPU bytes a point and one more buffer write when points or the mode change; steady frames write nothing more. | Remove repeats yourself to save the bytes; use `LineBatch` for independent segments. |
| Trails (`Trail` in `@margoengine/lines/trail`) | Enforced: 2 to 65,536 points (`maxPoints`, default 256); past that the oldest point goes and the far end jumps. By method: a trail is a line, so it faces the camera unless `normal` lays it flat (2026-11-07), and a flat trail is one strip with a per-point `normal` it does not have: it lies in a plane facing that one direction, so it does not follow a hill, and its segments are not joined at a corner; a flat trail takes no dashes; a dashed trail ignores `tailWidth`, because dash distances use the value widths are stored in. | One line keeps joins, antialiasing, fog, clipping and picking for free. | A tyre track seen from low down looks like a tube, not a flat strip. | Raise `maxPoints`; build a flat strip as a mesh with `@margoengine/splines/mesh`. |
| Massive line batches (`LineBatch` in `@margoengine/lines/batch`) | Enforced: 67,108,864 segments a batch; one draw per 8,388,608 segments at the default 256 MiB `maxBufferSize`. By method: independent segments with square ends: no joins, round caps, dashes, fog, clipping planes, depth writing or picking; colours at 8 bits a channel; a CPU copy of 32 bytes a segment stays for device loss. | Six vertices and 32 bytes a segment, where `Line` draws 78 vertices and reads a storage buffer whose binding size limits it. | Translucent corners are darker where segments overlap; memory is 64 bytes a segment across CPU and GPU. | Use `Line` where those features matter. |
| Hidden lines (`HiddenLine` in `@margoengine/lines/hidden`, `behind` and `depthBias` on `LineMaterial`) | By method: the test is against scene depth, so surfaces that write no depth hide nothing; `depthBias` (default 0.001 of the distance) decides what counts as on a surface, so an edge closer behind a surface than that shows as seen. Dashes run in world units. Hidden lines do not pick. | A depth test is one draw with no mesh analysis, on any scene; exact CAD hidden-line removal would need the geometry on the CPU. | A very thin wall can show an edge behind it as seen. | Lower `depthBias`, or raise it if a far model flickers. |
| Alpha to coverage on lines (`alphaToCoverage` on `LineMaterial`) | By method: works with MSAA only and falls back to blending without it; opacity comes in steps of one sample, four at 4x MSAA; lines of equal opacity use the same samples, so the later replaces the earlier at a crossing. | MSAA hardware turns alpha into a sample mask, which is what makes it independent of draw order. | Fine opacity changes band at low sample counts. | Leave it off and blend, or raise the sample count. |
| Filled helpers (`solidHead` on `ArrowHelper`, `fillOpacity` on `PlaneHelper`) | By method: a fill is flat colour with no lighting and does not pick. An opaque fill writes depth; translucent fills blend in the order added. | Helpers are guides, so they stay readable in any light and need no material or mesh. | A solid head has no shading, so its shape reads from its outline. | Use a mesh from `@margoengine/core` where lighting matters. |
| Video output (`@margoengine/headless/video`, `/ffmpeg`, 2026-11-05) | `encodeVideo` builds the whole file in memory and needs WebCodecs: browsers and workers have it, Node does not. WebM takes VP8, VP9 and AV1; MP4 takes H.264, H.265 (`hvc1` or `hev1`, 2026-11-15; ISO/IEC 14496-15 8.4.1), VP9 and AV1. H.265 is never picked by default, as many runtimes cannot encode it. The default bitrate is `width * height * fps / 10` and at least 100,000 bits a second (2026-11-25); at 16 x 16, AV1 in Edge 158 then reads a solid colour within 5 of 255 at any bitrate tried up to 2 Mbit/s. WebM times are whole milliseconds, as its default timestamp scale gives. Alpha is dropped unless `alpha` keeps it (2026-11-15): WebM with VP9 or VP8 only, since MP4 and the AV1 WebM mapping have no binding for it (code `'unsupported'`; `streamVideo` keeps it with `format: 'webm'` and refuses it for its default MP4 the same way). `encodeVideo` then runs a second encoder of the same codec and settings over each frame's alpha as luma (flat chroma), roughly doubling the encode work and adding the alpha stream's bytes, and writes each frame as a BlockGroup with BlockAdditions (BlockAddID 1) and a ReferenceBlock on frames that are not key, AlphaMode 1 and MaxBlockAdditionID 1 on the track (RFC 9559 5.1.3.5, 5.1.4.1.16, 5.1.4.1.28.4; Matroska codec mappings V_VP8 and V_VP9). A frame is a key frame, and gets a cluster and cue, only when both encoders made it one, so a seek never lands on alpha that needs an earlier frame. Colour under full transparency is the frames' own (black from `readPixels`), and 4:2:0 chroma at an edge mixes it in. `encodeWithFFmpeg` keeps alpha as VP9 `yuva420p` for `.webm` with the default arguments. `streamVideo` `format: 'webm'` (2026-11-15) writes a live WebM (RFC 9559 6.2): the Segment's size is unknown and the header states no duration and has no SeekHead, since it goes out before the end is known, so the joined file reports no duration (ffprobe N/A, a Chromium `<video>` Infinity until it has read to the end) and a reader finds the Cues at the end only by walking the file; `encodeVideo`, or a remux (`ffmpeg -i in.webm -c copy out.webm`), gives a file with both. Clusters are whole when written, so each states its size. Frames are 8-bit RGBA, so no HDR video. `encodeVideo` converts each frame on the CPU to limited-range BT.709 4:2:0 (one pass over the pixels, 1.5 bytes a pixel held per frame) and states BT.709 primaries and matrix, sRGB transfer and limited range in the file, since encoders that convert RGBA themselves misreport their range (WebKit and Chromium on macOS, 2026-11-14). Chroma is made on the even luma columns between rows (ITU-T H.273 chroma_sample_loc_type 0, the H.264 and H.265 default; a 1/4, 1/2, 1/4 weighting across columns) and stated so in VP9 `vpcC` and CodecPrivate (chroma 0) and Matroska ChromaSiting (left, half), 2026-11-15; an AV1 file states what its encoder wrote in the sequence header. `encodeWithFFmpeg` states the same sRGB transfer (H.273 code 13) and left chroma as `encodeVideo` (2026-11-15; it said BT.709 transfer before), since both take sRGB-encoded renders. H.264 and H.265 4:2:0 state picture sizes in steps of two (ITU-T H.264 7.4.2.1.1 CropUnitX and CropUnitY; H.265 7.4.3.2.1), so both video paths give an odd frame one repeated last column or row for those codecs and report the even size (2026-11-15; before, the encoder refused it); VP8, VP9 and AV1 keep odd sizes. Frames may carry their own times (`timestamp`, 2026-11-15): MP4 then states each frame's length in `stts` at the fps x 1000 time unit, and WebM states none by default, so block times are whole milliseconds and the last frame's length lives only in the segment duration. Sound is Opus in WebM and AAC or else Opus in MP4, one or two channels, and comes as plain samples held in memory. The containers follow their codec bindings (2026-11-15): AV1 units are stored without temporal delimiter and padding OBUs and an AV1 MP4 lists the `av01` brand (AV1 Codec ISO Media File Format Binding 2.1 and 2.4; Matroska AV1 mapping); Opus in MP4 counts time at 48 kHz, states 48000 in its sample entry, cuts the OpusHead pre-skip with an edit list and carries `roll` groups for 80 ms of pre-roll (Encapsulation of Opus in ISO Base Media File Format 0.6.8, 4.3 and 4.4); WebM Opus states the OpusHead input rate and WebM VP9 the codec feature CodecPrivate (Matroska codec mappings A_OPUS and V_VP9); each MP4 track header holds its own length (ISO/IEC 14496-12 8.3.2). The AV1 record (`av1C`, and the WebM CodecPrivate) is read from the sequence header the encoder wrote, which follows it as its config OBU, since WebCodecs gives no AV1 description and the codec string can name another level than the encoder chose (AV1 ISOBMFF binding 2.3.3; AV1 specification 5.5). | A file built whole has every size known up front, so nothing is patched afterwards and the MP4 index can sit first for playback before the download ends. WebCodecs is the only encoder a page has; shipping one would be a large download. | A very long capture must fit in memory, as compressed bytes only. In Node, `encodeWithFFmpeg` streams to a file instead, and needs ffmpeg installed. The H.264 and VP9 arguments and the rawvideo input ran on real ffmpeg 9.0.2 (`npm run test:real-ffmpeg --workspace @margoengine/headless`): 12 frames each, BT.709 tags read back, colours within 2 of 255 levels. That run needs ffmpeg, so the unit tests keep a stand-in program for failures and aborts. | Render in a browser or worker for `encodeVideo`, or use `/ffmpeg` in Node. Pass `args` to choose other ffmpeg settings. |
| Finished video files (`@margoengine/headless/ffmpeg-files`, `encodeWithFFmpeg` `layers`, 2026-11-16) | Node only, through the ffmpeg the app has. `checkSpan` and `copySpan` read MP4 and MOV (ISO/IEC 14496-12: sample tables, movie fragments, the first media edit of an edit list) and copy H.264 only; a span must start on a key frame and hold exactly its frames, so a variable-rate or open-GOP recording, MKV (whole-millisecond times) or HEVC is refused with the reason. `joinVideos` needs inputs of one codec, size and rate. `encoderArguments` writes H.264 4:2:0 8-bit; a hardware encoder needs its device and driver (an encoder ffmpeg lists can still fail with no device). Layers assume square pixels; an untagged layer file is read as BT.709 at 720 lines or more and BT.601 below, at TV range (an untagged JPEG as JFIF, BT.601 full range), each file read once with `ffmpeg -i` before the encode, whose stream line is parsed (KB-FILM-LAYERS2). A layer `crop` is in even pixels (4:2:0 chroma). Each clip frame starts on the film frame nearest its own time; there is no blending between clip frames. | Stream copy cannot change frames, so a span that is not exactly the frames is refused rather than shifted; edit lists past the first media edit are rare in recordings. | A refused span is re-encoded by the caller (the reason says why); a recording with non-square pixels is scaled first. | Record MP4 with a fixed rate and closed GOPs to copy spans; probe hardware encoders with a short encode before offering them. |
| Subsurface scattering blur (`SSS` in `@margoengine/post/sss`, 2026-11-07) | By method: screen space, so only what is on screen scatters; one Gaussian per channel stands in for a measured profile's sum of Gaussians (no long red tail); the kernel stops at 64 px each side, so a surface filling the screen close to the camera scatters less than `radius` asks; taps across a depth step larger than `radius`, off the mask or on the background count as the centre colour. The mask is the user's: a material's `subsurface` value does not mark pixels by itself. One `rgba16float` texture at the frame size; GPU cost not measured (LIM-434). | A separable blur costs two passes of `2 x taps + 1` reads, where a 2-D kernel would cost its square. | Soft skin, wax and marble on marked pixels; red bleeds farthest into shadow edges with the default profile. | Raise `taps` for wide kernels; mark pixels with a `SceneTargets` output or a selection mask. |
| Material decals (`MaterialDecals` in `@margoengine/post/material-decals`, 2026-11-07) | By method: a screen-space relight in a PostStack, not a G-buffer write before lighting. The surface comes from a `SceneTargets` capture (one more scene pass); the change is core's lit model (sun plus ambient) for the new surface minus the old, so gltf/pbr and materials models get the sun and ambient part only, not their image-based light; the sun's share is read back per pixel from the lit image, so a pixel the unshadowed sun gives nothing (facing away) is treated as lit; transparent effects drawn over the surface are relit with it; the atlas is read at mip 0; 64 decals, no culling; GPU cost not measured (LIM-441). | Engines that write decals into a deferred G-buffer change the surface before any light; Margo's forward renderer has no such buffer, so the relight works from a capture. | Normal, roughness, metalness and base-colour decals on any surface core or the capture draws, with shadow kept. | Keep decals on core meshes for an exact relight; give the atlas texels as wide as the decal's screen size. |
| Rough reflections (`SSR` with `stochastic: true` in `@margoengine/post/ssr`, 2026-11-08) | By method: one GGX-sampled ray per pixel per frame on surfaces rougher than half of `maxRoughness`, averaged over frames by a history reprojected with the surface's motion and clamped to this frame's 3x3 neighbourhood (mean plus or minus one standard deviation), blend floor 1/16; only what is on screen reflects, as for the mirror path. One history per SSR (a second view in the same frame reprojects against it); a moving camera smears rough reflections for a few frames; some noise stays on a still view (mean frame-to-frame change 0.15/255 against 1.28/255 at the second frame); three more `rgba16float` targets; GPU cost not measured (LIM-446). | One ray per pixel keeps the cost of the mirror path; the frames do the averaging. | Rough floors and brushed metal reflect what is on screen instead of keeping only the environment. | Leave `stochastic` off for deterministic frames (screenshots, tests); pair with TAA for a moving camera. |
| Multi-bounce screen GI (`SSGI` with `multiBounce: true` in `@margoengine/post/ssgi`, 2026-11-08) | By method: each frame adds one bounce by reading the light at ray hits from the previous frame's result, reprojected through the previous camera; only what is on screen bounces; the extra bounces trail a moving camera or light by a few frames; a hit hidden in the previous frame takes the light of what covered it for a frame; one history per SSGI (a second view in the same frame shares it); two more `rgba16float` targets and a display pass when SSGI ends the stack; GPU cost not measured (LIM-455). | Bounces accumulate over frames for the cost of one bounce per frame. | Indoor scenes fill with bounced light on a still or slow camera. | Keep it off for a fast-cutting camera, or accept a few frames of build-up after each cut. |
| Anamorphic streaks (`Anamorphic` in `@margoengine/post/anamorphic`, 2026-11-07) | By method: streaks are horizontal only (no rotation); they are built at half width and a quarter of the height, so a streak is about 4 px tall and a light smaller than a pixel still draws one; each streak is the light's own colour times `tint`, with no spectral split; reach is 2 (3^passes - 1) half-width texels each side; two quarter-size and one full-size `rgba16float` targets; GPU cost not measured (LIM-459). | A chain of sparse 9-tap passes reaches far for a few reads per pixel, where one wide kernel would read hundreds. | Bright points and highlights draw thin tinted lines across the frame. | Lower `passes` for short streaks, raise `threshold` so only lights streak. |
| Blur (`Blur` in `@margoengine/post/blur`, 2026-11-08) | By method: 2 radius + 1 texture reads per pixel per pass, so cost grows with the radius (64 at most, 129 reads a pass); the kernel is cut at 3 sigma for the Gaussian; edges clamp to the nearest pixel, so a bright border bleeds inward; `region` is a rectangle with a hard edge; one or two full-size `rgba16float` targets; GPU cost not measured (LIM-472). | A plain separable loop is exact for every radius and needs no mip chain. | Menus behind glass, focus pulls and custom chains blur by any whole-pixel radius. | Keep the radius small on weak GPUs, or chain two Blurs of half the radius for a wider, cheaper look. |
| Lens model (`Lens` in `@margoengine/post/lens`, 2026-11-08) | By method: one radial distortion term (k r^2), no tangential or chromatic part; distortion resamples the frame bilinearly, so it softens it slightly; the dirt is lit by its own glow at an eighth of the frame size (reach about 50 px), not by the glow of `Bloom`; the built-in dirt is a fixed pattern; two eighth-size and one full-size `rgba16float` targets; GPU cost not measured (LIM-474). The Panini projection is a camera (`WideAngle` in `@margoengine/cameras/panini`), not part of this effect. | One term covers the usual barrel and pincushion look; a small glow keeps the dirt cheap. | Wide lenses bulge, and smudges on the glass light up around bright lights. | Pass your own `dirt` texture; set `dirtIntensity` 0 for distortion alone. |
| Billboards (`BillboardLayer` in `@margoengine/sprites/billboard`, 2026-11-08) | `capacity` 256 billboards before a buffer grows; at most the device's `maxStorageBufferBindingSize` / 64 per view. | One instanced draw per view, each view with its own sorted buffer, so its memory is 64 B per billboard per view. | By method: blended billboards sort by the pivot's distance, so two that cross draw one over the other whole; pixel-sized ones take their depth from the pivot; `lockY` applies to world sizes only; texels are read with no filtering. | Multiply sprites and skeletal triangles (`BlendLayer` in `@margoengine/sprites/blend`, `SkeletalLayer` `blendMode`, 2026-11-15) | Two draws per multiply sprite and per multiply triangle; other modes one draw per run of adjacent sprites or triangles. Counted (packages/sprites/tests/blend.test.js): 4 screen then 3 multiply sprites, 7 draws; a two-triangle multiply mesh, 4 indexed draws. | The W3C multiply over a destination that may be transparent, co = cs(1 - ab) + cb(1 - as) + cs cb (premultiplied), needs the source scaled by both 1 - ab and the destination colour; one fixed-function blend offers one source factor, so a first draw adds the 1 - ab share and a second multiplies. | Smooth sprites (`SpriteLayer` `filter: 'linear'` in `@margoengine/sprites`, 2026-11-08) | One copy of the atlas per layer, `rgba8unorm-srgb` with a full mip chain: 4/3 of the atlas size again. | Filtering straight alpha bleeds a transparent texel's colour into edges, and filtering sRGB bytes darkens averages, so the layer keeps a premultiplied, linear-light copy. | By method: mip levels below the first average across neighbouring cells; the copy is made once, so a changed `GPUTexture` atlas needs `setAtlas` again; normals stay exact-pixel; premultiplied 8-bit storage loses colour precision at low alpha. | Live grading (`Grade` in `@margoengine/tonemap/grade`, 2026-11-08) | By method: display-referred, on 0..1 colour after the tone curve; under an HDR `ColorOutput` what lies above white passes ungraded; curves are sampled 33 times and read linearly; the wheels are additive offsets with fixed luminance masks (no pivot or range controls); one uniform of 608 B, 656 B while lift, gamma, gain or saturation is set (2026-11-16: the primaries, compiled only then, so a `Grade` without them is the program and data it was; `@margoengine/tonemap/grade` 1,552 to 1,877 B and `/hue` 2,165 to 2,596 B min+gzip); GPU cost not measured (LIM-477). | Grading after the curve keeps the controls in the 0..1 range artists know from grading tools. | Wheels, lift, gamma and gain, saturation, curves and hue against saturation move live with no LUT to bake. | Bake a LUT with `setLUT` for a look outside these controls. |

| Palette cycling and ramps (`@margoengine/pixel/palette`, 2026-11-08) | `cyclePalette` and `mixPalettes` run on the CPU per call; `setSwap` writes one 256 x 1 row at most each frame. | Rotating the drawn colours animates water and fire without repainting a pixel, and the matching stays. | By method: cycles rotate the colours drawn, not the matching (a pixel keeps its index); one rate per run, no ping-pong or easing; mixing is linear in Oklab between two palettes. | Extruded 3D text (`@margoengine/text/extrude`, 2026-11-08) | Enforced: nonzero fill, complete cap triangulation or a coded error; steps/curveSegments integers 1..256, bevelSegments 0..64; the font is parsed by `@margoengine/loaders/font` since 2026-11-16 (Margo's one font parser), with its budgets: composites 16 levels deep, 4,096 components over the tree and 1,000,000 points per glyph; Type 2 depth 10, 48 operands, 96 stems and 100,000 executed operations; malformed fonts throw its `LoaderError`. | Limit | Starts at | Why | What you see | Escape hatch |

| Download reader memory (`readResponse` in [loading.js](../packages/shared/loading.js), used by every loader that fetches, 2026-11-19) | Measured ([shared-read-bytes.test.js](../tests/shared-read-bytes.test.js), counts, not timings): a response with a plain `Content-Length` within the budget is read straight into one buffer of that size and handed back as is, so a 100 MiB file makes 104,857,600 B in the reader and never holds more than the file and one chunk; a body with no length, or a coded one (`Content-Encoding` other than `identity`), keeps each chunk once as it arrived and copies it once into the result, 104,857,600 B made for 100 MiB. Before 2026-11-19 (KB-LOADBYTES1) every chunk was copied as it arrived and again into the result: 209,715,200 B made and twice the file held at the end. | A declared length lets the reader skip the join; without one the result has to be joined from the chunks. | A body with no length still holds its chunks and the result together for the moment of the join (2x, briefly). A server that declares more than it sends costs a buffer of the declared size (within `maxBytes`) until the read ends, then one copy of what arrived; a chunk that views part of a larger or shared buffer is copied when held. | Serve files with `Content-Length`; set the loader's byte budget to what the app expects. |
| glTF download budget | Enforced: gltf/pbr reads at most `maxDownloadBytes` (default 512 MiB, 536,870,912 B: `assetLimit`, 64 MiB before 2026-11-11) of JSON, buffers and images per load, and decoded accessors, packed geometry and decoded images may each use 4x that (2 GiB by default); one image decodes to at most 8192 x 8192 pixels (67,108,864, the side every WebGPU device supports; 4096 x 4096 before 2026-11-17, which refused a film's 8192 x 4096 maps) and a side over the device's `maxTextureDimension2D` is refused at upload ([image-limit.ts](../packages/gltf/src/image-limit.ts), [async-images.test.js](../packages/gltf/test/async-images.test.js)); a Draco primitive takes up to 16,777,216 vertices and 50,331,648 indices (1,000,000 each before), and `@margoengine/decoders` outputs at most 384 MiB (402,653,184 B) per Draco decode (256 MiB before 2026-11-11), the most whose measured peak Wasm memory fits 90% of the prebuilt decoder's 2 GiB ([draco-output-limit.test.js](../packages/decoders/tests/draco-output-limit.test.js)): a 9,999,392-triangle grid with normals and UVs (a 5.8 MB stream, 280,126,112 B decoded) peaks at 1,035,534,336 B of Wasm memory in the prebuilt decoder and 812,449,792 B in the clean-room one, 3.7x and 2.9x its output; positions only, the worst measured mix, takes 4.5x (`node packages/decoders/scripts/draco-scale.mjs [side] [--positions]`). Draco connectivity can be a few KB for millions of regular triangles, so input size cannot bound decode memory: a 4 KB cut of that grid claims 666 MB (clean-room) or 795 MB (prebuilt) before it fails with `MargoError failed`, within the ceiling; the stage's `addGLTF` reads up to 512 MiB and sends a file over 64 MiB to gltf/pbr; `@margoengine/gltf` reads at most 64 MiB ([asset.ts](../packages/gltf/src/asset.ts), [loading.js](../packages/shared/loading.js); [accessors.test.js](../packages/gltf/test/accessors.test.js), [gltf-draco-limits.test.js](../tests/gltf-draco-limits.test.js), [gltf-routing.test.js](../packages/stage/tests/gltf-routing.test.js)). Khronos ABeautifulGame (a 43 MB GLB whose 33 2048x2048 textures decode to 528 MiB) fits the default image budget. | Bounds memory for any URL an app is handed, at a size where a 10M-triangle scan (about 300 MB raw, or about 800 MB decoded from a 40 MB Draco file) loads with no options; the decoded budget does not shrink with compression. | gltf/pbr names the option for the download and packed-geometry budgets, e.g. `RangeError: glTF exceeds download budget (536870912 bytes; raise the maxDownloadBytes option)`; decoded accessors and images over 4x throw `RangeError: Decoded glTF exceeds byte budget` or `RangeError: glTF images exceed decoded size limit`; the light loader refuses with `MargoError` code `unsupported`, `glTF download is over the light loader's 64 MiB; use @margoengine/gltf/pbr` (or `glTF buffers are ...`), so `loadAuto` moves on to gltf/pbr (KB-GLTFA B5, 2026-11-19). | gltf/pbr's `maxDownloadBytes` option, which also lowers the budget for apps that load untrusted URLs on small devices; for the light loader, use gltf/pbr. |
| Malformed and hostile files | Enforced at each parser's trust boundary (glTF, gltf/pbr with its parse worker and progressive stream, `.margo`, Draco, KTX2, meshopt, HDR, EXR, UltraHDR, FBX), checked by seeded fuzzers (`npm run fuzz`, [targets-formats.js](../scripts/fuzz/targets-formats.js); regressions in [fuzz-formats-regressions.test.js](../tests/fuzz-formats-regressions.test.js)): every input ends in a result or the package's own error. Limits added with them: a gltf/pbr document nested deeper than 256 levels ([asset.ts](../packages/gltf/src/asset.ts)); an EXR chunk that decodes to more than 256 MiB, or chunks too small to hold the image ([exr.ts](../packages/environment/src/exr.ts)); a Draco or KTX2 decode running longer than 10 s plus 4 s per MiB of input ([pool.ts](../packages/decoders/src/pool.ts)). How long large valid Draco and KTX2 files take to decode: not measured. | Files from a URL are untrusted: a malformed one must fail with an error the app can show, not crash, hang, read outside its bytes or claim memory its size cannot justify. | `TypeError: Invalid glTF JSON: nested deeper than 256 levels`, `RangeError: Unsupported EXR: a chunk decodes to more than 256 MiB`, `RangeError: Invalid EXR: chunks are too small for the image size`, `MargoError: Draco decode timed out after <limit> ms (corrupt data?); the decoder worker was restarted`. | The decoders' `timeout` option (`Infinity` turns the limit off). No real glTF comes near 256 levels; EXR: fewer channels per file. |
| Vertices per primitive | Enforced: gltf/pbr takes up to 16,777,216 vertices per primitive (2^24), loaded as parts of at most `maxPartVertices` (default 262,144, 1,024 to 1,048,576) each, skinned and morphed ones included (each part reads `JOINTS_n`, `WEIGHTS_n` and morph deltas through `part.vertexMap`, and deforms bit for bit as the mesh split by hand and as the whole primitive: [split-skin.test.js](../packages/animation/tests/split-skin.test.js), [test-skinned-parts-browser.mjs](../packages/gltf/scripts/test-skinned-parts-browser.mjs), natively and on the WebGL2 layer, RTX A6000 2026-11-17); `loadGLTFProgressive` streams them part by part, each part drawn as it arrives ([progressive.test.js](../packages/gltf/test/progressive.test.js)); the light `@margoengine/gltf` loader takes up to 1,000,000 vertices in total ([parts.test.js](../packages/gltf/test/parts.test.js), [accessors.test.js](../packages/gltf/test/accessors.test.js)). Packed geometry is still bounded by the decoded budget (4x `maxDownloadBytes`; 80 B a vertex, 4 B an index). Measured (Node 26, busy machine, diagnostic): a 1,001,000-vertex grid loads as 4 parts with 0.37% of its vertices copied onto the cuts, packed in about 240 ms. At 10M triangles ([test-parts-browser.mjs](../packages/gltf/scripts/test-parts-browser.mjs), native and WebGL2 layer; RTX A6000 and Radeon 680M 2026-11-11, Apple M6 2026-11-14): a 2,237 x 2,237-vertex field (5,004,169 vertices, 9,999,392 triangles, one primitive, a 240,093,656 B GLB) loads with no options through `loadGLTF` and `loadGLTFProgressive`, and with `maxPartVertices` 65,536 and 1,048,576, and in a far, a low and a close view draws exactly what the field pre-split at export into the same parts in the same order draws (the test splits it itself as parts.ts documents: same multisample samples, draws and triangles, and the parts hold the reference primitives' vertices and indices bit for bit; the reference with a part dropped, two parts' index lists swapped or a part drawn twice fails), and covers exactly the samples the field pre-split into 20 row bands covers. Until 2026-11-14 the split was compared exactly with the row bands, which passed on the A6000 and the 680M but never on the Apple M6, whose samples depend on the order of the draws at this triangle count ([known-bugs](known-bugs.md), "Apple M-series: multisample values of a multi-million-triangle frame depend on draw order"); the row bands, drawn in another order, are now compared by coverage only, which no draw order changes; Node's `prepareGLTF` peaks at 782,875,020 B of ArrayBuffers, 3.26 bytes per input byte. Work counts with `CulledModels`, close view (far view: every part): `maxPartVertices` 65,536: 78 parts, 12 drawn, 1,550,309 triangles; 262,144 (default): 20 parts, 9 drawn, 4,683,190 triangles; 1,048,576: 5 parts, 4 drawn, 8,363,067 triangles. Without `CulledModels` the draw loop tests each part's bounding sphere against the camera frustum on the CPU (one test per primitive per draw, 2026-11-11, [parts.test.js](../packages/gltf/test/parts.test.js)), so a part out of view issues no draw; instanced, rigged, deformed, own-shader and displaced primitives are drawn untested. The default stays 262,144 rather than the largest part a device binds: larger parts save at most 15 draws and submit 1.8x the triangles close up. | Each part's vertex buffer is also bound as a storage buffer, so 262,144 vertices (20 MiB) stays inside the WebGPU default binding (128 MiB) and the WebGL2 layer's 2048-context one (64 MiB); indices pass through float32, exact up to 2^24. Parts follow Hoppe 1999, Sander et al. 2007, Yoon et al. 2005, Isenburg and Lindstrom 2005, Cignoni et al. 2005, Kerbl et al. 2018 and Karis et al. 2021 (cited in [parts.ts](../packages/gltf/src/parts.ts)). | Over 2^24: `MargoError` code `unsupported` naming 16777216; a part over a device's binding: `RangeError` naming its bytes and `maxPartVertices`; the light loader: `RangeError: glTF exceeds one million vertices`. | Split a primitive over 2^24 vertices at export; lower `maxPartVertices` for a device with a small storage binding. |
| Dash caps (`dashCap` on `LineMaterial`) | By method: a cap reaches half the line width past its dash in pixels while dashes stay in world units, so a gap narrower than the width closes up. A cap stops at the line's own ends, and picks count gaps as line. | Ends are drawn in the fragment, with no extra geometry per dash. | Dotted lines keep the dot width on screen while their spacing follows perspective. | Widen `gapSize`, or use `worldUnits` widths. |
| Adaptive point size (`adaptiveSize` on `OctreeCloud` in `@margoengine/points/octree`) | By method: density is per node and assumes a surface (points per cube face), so a volume of points gets smaller points than its gaps need. Sizes are written on the CPU, at most 500,000 points a selection, when the nodes drawn under a node change. A random sample still leaves gaps: 98 percent of the pixels covered at the default `scale` of 1.5 in the browser check. | Point sizes already have a channel, so this needs no second shader. | Far parts look solid, with larger and softer points. A big camera jump takes a few frames to settle sizes. | Raise `scale`; set `maxPixelSize` to cap the growth. |
| Surfels (`SurfelPlugin` in `@margoengine/points/surfels`) | Enforced by method: opaque, always tests and writes depth, no textures, no `PointsPlugin.pick`; WebGPU only. Scene depth holds each disc pushed back by up to `blendDepth` radii. Each point draws twice, plus one full-screen pass. Extra targets take 12 bytes a sample: about 100 MB at 1920 x 1080 with 4x MSAA. On the WebGL2 layer's half-float tier the front depth is packed into `rgba8unorm` (2026-11-11; the tier stores `r32float` as `r16float`), pixel-equal to its full tier at 4x; its LDR tier is refused. The entry grew 16,742 to 17,028 B for it. Speed is not measured. | Weighted colour needs a sum and a divide, so it cannot be one blended draw; pushing the scene's own depth keeps meshes in the same test. | About twice the point cost of `PointsPlugin`. Something drawn later that lies within the push of a surface can show through it. | `PointsPlugin` where speed matters more; a smaller `blendDepth` for thin layers close together. |
| View offset (`CameraProjection.setViewOffset`, 2026-11-05) | By method: the frustum is built for the full image and the view shows one rectangle of it, so each tile or monitor must be rendered as its own frame at the rectangle's size. Effects that read the whole image (bloom, SSAO, TAA history, DOF blur) see only the tile, so seams can show where they reach across a tile edge. `fit` still frames the canvas, not the full image. | Core builds one matrix per view; the offset remaps that matrix, so culling, picking and every pass read the same view, with 0 core bytes. Screen-space passes cannot see pixels the frame does not contain. | Tiles of a screenshot match the full render for geometry; a wide blur or screen-space shadow can differ by a few pixels near a tile edge. | Render tiles with overlap (offset the rectangle outward, crop after) or keep post effects off for the tiles. |
| Focal length and film gauge (`CameraProjection.focalLength`, 2026-11-05) | By method: the lens sets the field of view only. It models a pinhole camera with a rectangular sensor, so no lens distortion, no crop of the sensor to the image beyond `sensorFit`, and no sensor shift. `camera.fov` is overwritten each frame while a focal length is set. | A projection matrix has one field of view; distortion and shift belong to wide-angle and off-axis projections in their own entries. | Setting `camera.fov` by hand while a focal length is set has no lasting effect. | Clear `focalLength` (set it to `undefined`) to drive `camera.fov` again. |
| Potree folders (`PotreeSource` in `@margoengine/points/potree`) | Enforced: reads 2.0 with encodings `DEFAULT` and `BROTLI`, and 1.4 to 1.8; other encodings and older versions throw `unsupported`. By method: hierarchy pages read when `load` reaches them (`hierarchy: 'eager'` reads all at open); 1.4 has no pages, its hierarchy is in `cloud.js`. The layout of a `BROTLI` node was measured on real folders, as no public text gives its bit order: every point of 3,954,696 fell in its node and the colour range matched the metadata's. `OctreeCloud` draws position and colour; other attributes reach the caller through `load`, or draw through `colorBy`. | Each node is its own request, and a page costs one more request on the way down. A leaf of 1.7 states 0 points, so its `count` is 0 until its file is read and the point budget cannot count it before that. | A `BROTLI` node decodes on the calling thread, measured at 3,954,696 points in 1.7 s (whole folder, local files, busy machine, diagnostic). | Pass a `brotli` that runs in a worker, or convert with encoding `DEFAULT`; older versions need converting. |
| Brotli decoding (`@margoengine/decoders/brotli`) | Enforced: output stops at `maxBytes`, 1 GiB by default. By method: a stream decodes whole, on the calling thread; large-window Brotli, which RFC 7932 does not define, is refused. | The output buffer doubles as the sliding window, so nothing streams out early. | A stream takes its whole output in memory. | Split data into several streams, as Potree does per node. |
| bzip2 and xz decoding (`@margoengine/decoders/bzip2`, `/xz`, 2026-11-07) | Enforced: output stops at `maxBytes`, 1 GiB by default. By method: a stream decodes whole, on the calling thread. `.xz` reads LZMA2 with any Delta filters before it (since 2026-11-15); the branch/call/jump (BCJ) filters are `unsupported`, as *The .xz File Format* 1.2.1 lists their IDs and alignments but no algorithm and Margo is written from public specifications only. bzip2's randomised blocks are `unsupported`. Speed is not measured. | Browsers offer neither format; two file formats store them inside a file. | A damaged `.lzma`, or an `.xz` written with no check, shows only if the stream breaks. | Pass a low `maxBytes` for untrusted files. |
| Off-axis and oblique projection (`@margoengine/cameras/offaxis`, 2026-11-05) | By method: one flat screen per camera, and the eye must be in front of it. The canvas aspect is ignored. An oblique near plane keeps the frustum sides and moves only the near plane, so depth precision can drop as the plane turns edge-on to the view (not measured), and the camera must stay on the clipped side. | Core builds one matrix per view. A curved or multi-panel display is several flat screens, each its own view. Putting the plane into the matrix needs no clip plane in any shader. | Wrong or stretched pictures if the canvas shape differs from the screen. Z-fighting at long range with a strongly slanted plane. | Give each panel its own camera and view; keep the plane as square to the view direction as the effect allows. |
| Octrees under a moving transform (`OctreeCloud`) | Enforced: `matrix` or `attach(mesh)` places every node, and `select` takes a world view; the size test uses the longest stretch of the matrix. By method: a skewed matrix gets that same single stretch, so node sizes on screen may be high, never low. | Node selection runs in cloud space with the view and planes brought across. | A squashed octree may load more nodes than its look needs. | Keep the scale even, or raise `minNodePixels`. |
| Physical exposure (`@margoengine/cameras/physical`, 2026-11-05) | By method: exposure is relative, in stops against `referenceEV`, because the engine's light is not calibrated in photometric units. Depth of field and motion blur are those of the `DOF` and `MotionBlur` effects, so their limits apply (a maximum blur radius, WebGPU only for `DOF`). The thin-lens formulas assume a circle of confusion on the sensor, a pinhole lens elsewhere. | A scene lit with arbitrary intensities has no absolute luminance to meter, so the honest unit is the stop. | Changing ISO or shutter changes only the brightness (no sensor noise), and a very open aperture is capped by `DOF`'s `maxRadius`. | Set `referenceEV` to the setting that should look as the scene was lit; raise `maxRadius` for a wider aperture. |
| GPU picking of points (`PointPicking` in `@margoengine/points/pick`) | Enforced: picks what the view last drew, through the Picking overlay of `@margoengine/selection`, so meshes in front block a point and clipping planes, discs and alpha cuts apply. By method: a transparent point in front of an opaque one wins the pick when it was drawn. | The pick pass reuses the drawn view and the shared ID tile. | A cloud that has not been drawn yet cannot be hit. | Pick after a frame. |
| Wide-angle projections (`@margoengine/cameras/panini`, 2026-11-05) | By method: one rectilinear picture is resampled, so the source must be drawn at a wide field of view first (about 120 to 150 degrees across at most) and the rest of the sphere is not available. The stage runs after tone mapping, on display colour, and needs WebGPU and a perspective camera. Picking and screen-space overlays still use the source picture: map them with `WideAngle.map`. | A matrix cannot do these projections, because they bend straight lines. | A fisheye or Panini wider than the source shows black or is cropped (`crop`). Pixels at the far edge of a very wide source are stretched before they are resampled, so the sides are softer than the middle. | Draw the source wider, or use `crop: true`; for a full circle render a cube map with `@margoengine/environment` and sample it yourself. |
| Triangle order at import (`optimize` on `loadGLTF` and friends, `reorder` in `margo-convert`, 2026-11-07) | By method: `BLEND` primitives keep the file's triangle order, points and lines are skipped, and a primitive with one vertex per corner gains nothing (Fox: ACMR 3.0 before and after). `optimize` reorders indices only, as a load's vertices are shared with skins and morphs; it needs `@margoengine/geometry` and keeps `loadGLTFInWorker` on the main thread. `margo-convert` also moves the vertices. Measured on a shared machine, diagnostic, Node: BoomBox's 6,036 triangles ACMR 0.874 to 0.769 in 9.0 ms, Corset's 18,324 triangles 0.865 to 0.763 in 9.2 ms. No frame time is measured on any GPU (gap C14). | Off by default in a load, on in every preset: a model built once should not pay at each load. | A file that is already well ordered pays the load time for little. | Run `margo-convert` once, offline. |
| Wide-angle projections from a cube (`@margoengine/cameras/wide-cube`, 2026-11-07) | By method: up to 360 degrees across for equidistant and equisolid, below 360 for stereographic, 180 for orthographic, and below Panini's own fold (`acos(-d)` from the centre for `distance` d up to 1, `acos(-1/d)` above). Needs WebGPU, `@margoengine/post` and `@margoengine/environment`. Not measured: the cost, or sharpness against a flat picture. | Each direction reads a cube, so the sphere is complete, at six scene draws a frame on top of the main draw the stage replaces. | Faces run the scene passes only, so HDR effects ahead of the stage do not reach the picture. Picking still uses the plain main picture: map a pointer with `WideAngleCube.map`. Each face is drawn apart, so screen-space looks can show at the seams. | `facesPerFrame` below 6 spreads the capture, and the picture then lags. |
| HDR point colours (`colorFormat: 'float'`) | Enforced: 16 bytes a point against 4; a colour must be finite and 0 or more, or `RangeError`. By method: an 8-bit canvas still clips above 1 at the end. | Four float32 a point keep the values through the shader. | Colour memory and upload are four times RGBA8. | Keep the default `'rgba8'` for colours inside 0..1. |
| Mipmaps on point and sprite maps (`mipmaps`) | Enforced: an uploaded image gets a full chain, default on for points, off for sprites. By method: sprite atlases are left without mips as levels bleed between cells; `alphaTest` tests the filtered alpha. | One chain a map, made at upload. | An atlas sprite drawn small still shimmers, and a video map pays for a chain per upload. | Use a gutter around atlas cells with `mipmaps: true`, or `mipmaps: false` on a video. |
| Materials per part (`CulledParts` in `@margoengine/culling/parts`) | By method: a batch is one geometry, and each part's record holds its own colour, roughness, metalness and sidedness. No textures per part. | Core's `PbrMaterial` has no textures, and the record is what the draw reads, so colours cost no extra batch or draw. | A CAD assembly with hundreds of colours stays one batch per shape. A batch mixing single-sided and double-sided parts leaves the back-culled pipeline. | Build batches with `groupParts`; keep sidedness uniform inside a batch where the back-culled pipeline matters. |
| Occlusion for core meshes (`CulledMeshes`, `occlusion: true`, `@margoengine/culling`) | By method: occluders are last frame's kept instances of at least `occluderSize` pixels (default 8), redrawn with this frame's camera; only core's own batches occlude; a frame whose shader moves or discards surfaces (section planes) culls by frustum alone. | Hi-Z needs a depth the package can read, and core's depth target has no texture binding, so occluders are drawn a second time. | Hidden instances stop drawing from the second frame; the image matches core's. Each frame pays one depth pass and one pyramid. On the WebGL2 compatibility layer `occlusion` culls by frustum and screen size only (2026-11-10, measured): the full Hi-Z kernels do run there, but WebGL2 has no indirect draw, so each GPU-written draw record is read back to the CPU (7 stalls a frame), and 9 of the 23 kernel dispatches a frame fall to the layer's CPU tier. With a wall hiding a crowd of n boxes on an RTX A6000 (`node packages/culling/test/gpu/compat-cost.mjs --compat`), the full kernels cut the triangles submitted to 234 a frame against 18,109, 144,109 and 202,069 for the frustum route at n = 1,500, 12,000 and 48,000, but raise GL draws from 4 to 37 and the median frame from 10.5, 11.2 and 15.1 ms to 28.9, 46.1 and 79.1 ms (diagnostic times, CPU about 13% busy); native WebGPU took 4.9 ms at 48,000 with occlusion. The frustum route keeps 0 stalls and 0 extra dispatches. | Leave it off on open layouts, where the pass costs more than it saves. On the WebGL2 layer `WebGL2Culling` (`@margoengine/culling/webgl2`) culls occluded core meshes against a CPU depth buffer with no readback (1,609 and 7,453 triangles a frame), but in the same run its median frame was 16.5, 77.3 and 391.7 ms at n = 1,500, 12,000 and 48,000: use it only for a few thousand meshes (speed phase list). |
| GPU culling of models (`CulledModels` in `@margoengine/culling/models`) | By method: covers instance rows and plain primitives, against the frustum, screen size and, with `occlusion`, the occluders you add (Hi-Z). Skinned and morphed primitives are not culled, and neither is a primitive gltf/pbr joined into an instanced batch; a displacing shader needs `padding`; the WebGL2 layer culls nothing. | Bounds of a deformed primitive are only known on the GPU. WebGPU has no multi-draw, so a plain primitive keeps its indirect draw call even when culled. | Rows cost no CPU per frame; each instanced primitive costs one uniform write and three dispatches. A plain primitive costs 96 bytes of upload a frame and one draw call: the GPU work goes, the CPU cost still grows with primitives. Each occluder draws depth-only every frame. Not timed. | Give repeated objects `instances`; give `addOccluder` only the large surfaces. |
| Occluders that are not parts (`addOccluder` on `CulledInstances` and `CulledParts`) | By method: takes core meshes, gltf/pbr models, materials meshes and `Terrain`, drawn whole each frame. Back faces, cut-outs, blended, transmissive, displaced and clipped primitives do not occlude; a material extension that moves vertices cannot be detected. Not on `CulledMeshes`, which runs before the frame's deformers. | Core's depth has no texture binding, so an occluder is drawn a second time, and it must be a surface the frame really shows. | Parts behind a building stop drawing; the image is unchanged. Each occluder costs its triangles again every frame. | Add large things only, and never a model whose extension moves vertices. |
| Hi-Z with `bounds: 'box'` on slanted occluders | Any long part behind a surface seen at an angle | The test compares the part's nearest corner with the farthest occluder depth in its screen rectangle, and a slanted surface spans a range of depth | The part draws though it is hidden: extra work, never a wrong pixel | Split long parts, or accept it |
| `CascadeParts` and `CascadeInstances` lists | One u32 per slot per cascade, up to the GPU's storage binding size | Each cascade's list can hold every caster | Past the binding size, or on the WebGL2 layer, every cascade draws every caster, as the plain classes do | Use fewer cascades, or split the parts |
| `LodInstances` | 1 to 4 levels; 96 bytes per instance per level, plus the 96-byte source record and 8 bytes of scan state | Each level's list can hold every instance; a scan keeps each list in instance order | Shadows: not cast, as `shadows.add` takes no `LodInstances`. WebGL2 layer: every shown instance draws the first level. Instances of a level draw in instance order, so an unchanged frame repeats to the byte | Use `CascadeInstances` for casters of the first level |
| `MeshletMesh` | One mesh, up to 65,535 parts (instances), each with its own matrix. The mesh's indices once, then one shared pool of kept indices for the camera and one per shadow cascade, each of `maxKeptTriangles` (default every triangle of every part, up to 4,194,304, 48 MiB) and lowered to the device's storage binding size; a word per cluster and part per list, 40 bytes per cluster, 20 bytes of draw arguments per part and list | Parts are placed in the pool in slot order, so the kept clusters sit in cluster order every frame. A part whose clusters do not fit draws its whole mesh: more triangles, the same image | One indirect draw per shown part (WebGPU has no multi-draw, and an indirect `firstInstance` needs a feature), so CPU cost grows with the parts. Two-pass Hi-Z: the occluders are the clusters each part drew last frame, at this frame's matrices, so a cluster that comes into view is still drawn that frame; the first frame has none. A pick draws the whole mesh. On the WebGL2 layer the frustum and cone tests run on the CPU (the same tests in double precision, so the same clusters: `meshlets-check` counts match native), one `drawIndexed` per run of neighbouring kept clusters; no Hi-Z there, as for every culling class | Use `CulledParts` for many small copies; split more than 65,535 parts, or a mesh whose indices pass the storage binding size, into several `MeshletMesh` |
| Attributes in generated LOD levels (`autoLOD`, `hierarchicalLOD`, `simplifyAttributes`) | Per primitive: mesh-edit's limit of 200,000 vertices or faces. A level is a subset of the source's vertices, so a position can only be one the source has. Triangles mesh-edit cannot take (a third face on an edge, a flipped neighbour) simplify as separate sheets, up to 4, then alone. | Vertex-subset collapses keep every attribute exact with no interpolation; the price is less accuracy per triangle than placing new vertices. Primitives simplify one at a time, so an open edge between two primitives can slide apart a little. | A core mesh's levels hold positions and normals only, as core geometry does. A materials mesh's levels do not follow a material swapped on the source later, and `shadows.add` takes each level on its own. | Give the source's borders the same vertices in one primitive, or use `Imposter` for the farthest level. |
| Generated levels of loaded models (`autoLOD`, `hierarchicalLOD` on a `loadGLTF` model) | `hierarchicalLOD` refuses skinned and morphed models; `autoLOD` levels them and needs WebGPU for that. Per primitive: mesh-edit's 200,000 vertices or faces. Vertex memory of the default three levels: about 0.875 of the source's, on top of it; GPU textures are shared. | A level is a model of the same file, so shadows, picking and materials work as on any model, at the cost of a model per level. | A level of a file with animations follows the source's drawing nodes in plugin order, so an `Animation` attached after `autoLOD` shows a frame late there; a file with no animations keeps the transforms of the call. Simplifying ignores bone influence: a collapse keeps one end's weights exactly, but a thin joint can lose shape in a deep pose. A flat-shaded level has new normals, the one thing in a level that is not the source's. Points and lines stay on level 0, and out of a far model. `selectVariant` on the source does not reach its levels. | `MSFT_lod` levels in the file (`LOD.fromModel`), or an `Imposter`, for hand-made levels. |
| Baked LOD levels (`bake` on `autoLOD`, 2026-11-07) | Enforced: a materials mesh or loaded model only, a core mesh throws. By method: a map the source has of its own stays, and that kind is not baked; a primitive whose UVs leave the unit square or overlap on over 2% of its texels gets no maps; `'normal'` and `'ao'` only, so colour detail lost by a level stays lost. Each lower level's maps have half the last one's size, down to 32. The bake runs on the calling thread. Maps hold CPU copies with every mip: about 1.4 MB per primitive at the default 512. | Baking on the primitive's own UVs needs no new layout and draws through the same material. | A tiled or mirrored model gets nothing from `bake` until `unwrapMesh` gives it a clean layout. `hierarchicalLOD` does not bake. | Lower `size`, or bake once and save the model. |
| Dithered level cross-fade (`LODFade`, `@margoengine/lod/fade`) | WebGPU only: instant on WebGL2. Instant to or from an `Imposter` and for `hierarchicalLOD`. One transition per `LODSystem`. | Each pixel comes from one level by a fixed noise threshold: no blending, no sorting, depth stays right, at the cost of both levels drawing for `duration` (default 0.25 s) and a storage read per core-mesh pixel while attached. | Shadows see both levels during a fade. A model's first fade compiles its pipelines unless `prepare` ran. | Default of `LODFade` off: levels pop. |
| Fuller imposters (`LODOptions.color`, `emissive`, `frame`; `ImposterOptions.emissive`, `pose`, `margin`; `ImposterFrames`; `shadows.add(lods)`) | Instance record 96 bytes (was 64). `ImposterFrames`: `count` atlases, at least 2, a draw per frame in use. Baked emissive stops at 1 (RGBA8). Lighting effects: the `direct` hook only. | Colour and emissive ride on the one instanced draw, and shadows use the atlas instead of a mesh. | An imposter loses self-shadow within `r*(2/(frames-1)+4/frameSize)`. Casters are not culled per cascade. A skinned source needs `margin` for poses past its bind-pose bounds. | Keep a mesh level at the range where these matter. |
| Streamed levels (`LevelStream`, `@margoengine/lod/stream`) | Default 4 fetches at once and 256 MiB kept; a level on show is never freed, so `resident` can pass `maxBytes`. The default count holds vertices and indices, not textures. | A wish for a level that is not there holds the level on show, so nothing pops out, at the cost of a coarse level per object. | A fetch unasked for over two frames is aborted and starts over when wanted: partial bytes are not kept. No automatic retry: a failed level waits for `retry()`. | `bytes` per level to count textures; load up front for scenes that fit. |
| Moving sources of a far mesh (`HierarchicalLOD.update`, `follow`) | A cell keeps its meshes and centre. A rebuild merges the whole cell again, and simplifies it with a `ratio` below 1. | Far meshes stay plain meshes, so nothing is paid per frame for what stands still beyond comparing matrices. | `follow` runs a frame behind the sources and only for cells on their far mesh; a cell coming into range shows its old far mesh for one frame. | `update()` when you know something moved. |
| Selection outlines on imposters (`LODSystem.drawSelectionMask`, `SelectionMaskSource`) | An object counts as selected through its anchor or a level; a part of a model level does not. | The mask redraws only selected imposters, from a buffer of their own, with the imposter's own shader, so the outline sits on the imposter's pixels. | The mask pass runs the full imposter fragment shader for the selected objects. | Select the anchor or the model. |

## Geometry

| Limit | Starts at | Why | What you see | Escape hatch |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| NURBS surfaces (`@margoengine/geometry/nurbs`) | Enforced by method: no trimming curves, knot insertion or degree elevation; `NurbsCurve.tessellate` halves a span at most 12 times. | Trimming needs a boundary representation, which this engine does not carry; revolves, control nets and whole patches do not. | A trimmed patch meshes untrimmed. | Cut the mesh with `@margoengine/mesh-edit`. |
| Mesh surface sampler (`@margoengine/geometry/sample`) | Enforced by method: points are independent random draws, so they can clump; there is no minimum spacing. Vertex weights are linear across each triangle. | Independent draws cost one search each and need no neighbour lookups. | Two points can land close together. | `@margoengine/scatter` for spaced placement on terrain. |
| Mesh optimisation (`@margoengine/geometry/optimize`) | Enforced by test ([optimize.test.js](../packages/geometry/tests/optimize.test.js)): shuffled grids, spheres and knots end under 0.8 cache misses per triangle on a 16-vertex first-in first-out cache (3 before); nested shells lose over 40 percent of their overdraw while the miss ratio stays within 6 percent. Those are stand-ins for a GPU: frame time on a real one is not measured. | The cache model is a simulation; real GPUs differ in cache size and batching. | Triangle order changes, so a transparent mesh that relied on it can look different. | `overdraw: false` keeps the sort off; leave the mesh out to keep its order. |
| Bending along a curve (`@margoengine/geometry/flow`) | Enforced by method: frames are sampled `segments` times (default 256) and interpolated, and only vertices move. A shape wider than the radius of a bend folds over itself. | Sampling once makes each vertex a table lookup. | A coarse mesh cuts corners; a tight bend pinches the inner side. | Add segments along the axis; raise `segments`. |
| Extrusion UVs (`uvGenerator` of `@margoengine/geometry/extrude`) | Enforced by method: the generator runs once per triangle corner on the CPU, and wall `u` comes from the outline before the bevel widens it. | Walls and caps are separate triangles, so a corner can differ per surface. | A texture on a wide bevel stretches a little across `u`. | Use `distance` and your own `u` from `shape`. |
| Split tangents (`splitTangents`, `computeTangents` with `split`) | Enforced by method: checked against Blender's MikkTSpace on two meshes, to a dot product above 0.9995 per corner with matching signs. It follows the published grouping and is not a port of the reference library, so a mesh with unusual degenerate triangles may group differently. `w` assumes v up. | Clean room: written from the paper. | A rare corner could differ from a bake on degenerate geometry. | Remove zero-area triangles first; flip v on glTF UVs. |
| Baked poses (`bakeMorphTargets`, `bakeSkin`) | Enforced by method: four joints per vertex, linear blend skinning, Float32 output. | One pose on the CPU for picking, physics or export; the same mix glTF defines. | Linear blending collapses at sharp twists, as it does on the GPU. | Bake several poses, or split the joint. |
| Delaunay triangulation (`@margoengine/geometry/delaunay`) | Enforced by method: adds no points of its own, so thin outlines keep thin triangles; crossing constraints and self-crossing rings are refused. Exact tests fall back to whole-number arithmetic, which is slower on grids and other exactly cocircular input. | Keeping the input points is what stops T-junctions; refinement would add vertices. | Cocircular input costs more time. | Add inner points with `points`; split crossing edges. |
| Colour conversion (`@margoengine/math/color-space`) | Enforced: four named spaces (`srgb`, `srgb-linear`, `display-p3`, `display-p3-linear`), D65 white only; any other name throws `TypeError`. Results are not clamped. | Those are the spaces WebGPU canvases and CSS `color()` share, and unclamped values convert back unchanged. | A colour outside the target space has channels below 0 or above 1. Below 0 the transfer curve runs on as its straight segment, not mirrored. | Call `clipToSRGB` on linear sRGB to bring a colour inside sRGB. |
| Ray and box slabs (`Ray.intersectBox`, `OBB.intersectRay`, scatter `InstancePicker`, 2026-11-10) | By method: hit or miss is decided on the box grown by 8 machine epsilons (about 1.8e-15) of its farthest corner from the ray origin; the distance returned is the exact entry. An empty box (max below min) is a miss; an unbounded box keeps the plain test. | The three slab entry times of a ray through a corner or a point box round apart, so without the allowance an inclusive hit could be lost (126 of 512 point-box rays missed an OBB before). | A ray passing outside a box by less than about 1.8e-15 of its distance counts as a hit at the box. | Test the exact distance when a hair-wide miss must stay a miss. |
| Unbounded box centre (`Box3.getCenter`, `Box3.getBoundingSphere`, 2026-11-15) | By method: an axis with an infinite bound (either side, or both at the same infinity) has centre 0; the other axes give the midpoint. The bounding sphere of such a box has that centre and radius `Infinity`. An empty box keeps centre (0, 0, 0) and radius -1. | The midpoint of an infinite bound is not a number (NaN), and a NaN centre or radius poisons every later sum it enters. | The centre of an unbounded axis is a convention, not a point of the box's own; a half-open box from 5 to Infinity reports 0 there. | Read `min` and `max` directly when the finite side of a half-open box matters. |
| Oriented boxes (`@margoengine/math/obb`) | Enforced: non-finite values, a negative half size, a matrix that is not a rotation and a negative or non-finite `epsilon` throw. `applyMatrix4` throws `RangeError` for a projective matrix, a zero scale axis or a scale that would shear the box. `intersectsOBB` pads the axis cosines by `epsilon`, 1e-6 by default. | A sheared box is no longer a box. Near-parallel edges have a cross product close to zero, and the pad stops them reporting a false separation. | Two boxes closer than about `epsilon` times their size can report an overlap; a real overlap is never missed. | Pass 0 as `epsilon` for an exact test on boxes with no near-parallel edges, or bound a sheared object with `Box3`. |
| Segments and triangles (`@margoengine/math/line3`, `/triangle`) | Enforced by method: two directions count as parallel, and a triangle as degenerate, when the sine squared of their angle is below 1e-14 (float64 rounding). `Triangle.containsPoint` tests the point's projection on the plane, not its height above it. | Below that angle the closed forms lose all their digits, so the parallel and collapsed cases take their own paths. | A sliver thinner than about 1e-7 radians gets null barycentric weights. | Use `closestPointToPoint`, which still answers for a degenerate triangle; check `distanceToPoint` when height off the plane matters. |
| Polygon booleans and offsets (`@margoengine/geometry/polygon`) | Enforced by method: all points go onto one grid of about 2^26 steps across the input. A vertex at a crossing moves up to half a step, edges closer than a step touch, and parts under two steps wide are dropped. | One exact grid is what makes every test safe: no epsilon to tune, and no failed or crossing output at any scale. | Two features 1e-8 of the input's width apart merge. Very large plans with very fine detail lose the detail. | Run distant parts separately, or scale up the part that needs the detail. |
| Project and unproject (`@margoengine/math/project`) | Enforced by method: core's `camera.matrix` is Float32 and holds zeros until the first frame; a point at or behind the camera plane returns null; a matrix with no inverse throws `RangeError`. | One matrix serves every camera, orthographic included; null keeps a point behind the camera from showing up mirrored on screen. | Results carry float32 precision, not float64, and depth z follows the camera (WebGPU near = 1, far = 0; WebGL near = -1, far = 1). | Pass your own `{matrix}` as a Float64Array for float64 results. Take depth from `projectPoint` instead of hard-coding it. |
| Spherical harmonics (`@margoengine/math/sh`) | Enforced by method: three bands, 9 RGB coefficients, CPU only. No rotation of a coefficient set. | Three bands hold diffuse light to within a few percent, and match the layout `@margoengine/environment` reads. | A single point of light overshoots: a distant light reads 17/16 of its irradiance facing it and 1/16 facing away, where the truth is 1 and 0. Results are not clamped. | For sharp light use a real light and keep SH for the soft part. To turn a probe, project it again from rotated samples. |
| Sweep and loft (`@margoengine/geometry/sweep`) | Enforced by method: sections stay flat and are matched by their share of the way round, with no point-to-point control. Holes of a loft pair by their order, so every section has the same number. | One rule fits any pair of outlines and keeps every corner. | A twisted quad is two flat triangles, so a twisted solid loses volume in proportion to the step (0.4 percent at 128 steps for a quarter turn). A sharp bend in a path pinches the profile. | Raise `steps`, round the path, or pass 3D rings with matching points and `align: false`. |
| Capsules (`@margoengine/math/capsule`) | Enforced: a negative or non-finite radius and any matrix beyond rotation, translation and uniform scale throw `RangeError`. `pushOutOfTriangle` resolves one triangle at a time, and returns null for an axis lying in a degenerate triangle. | Under other matrices the shape stops being a capsule. One triangle at a time keeps the type a shape, not a physics solver. | Several triangles at once (a corner) need repeated passes in the caller, and a push out of one triangle can move into the next. | For a full character controller with sliding and stepping use `@margoengine/physics`. |
| Tessellation (`@margoengine/geometry/tessellate`) | Enforced by method: `maxTriangles`, 5,000,000 by default, stops a tiny limit. Edges are measured in the mesh's own units, not on screen. | Plain edge length needs no camera and keeps neighbours in agreement. | Long thin triangles add many vertices along their length. Flat areas are split as finely as curved ones. | Pick the limit for the deformation, or tessellate only the part that bends. |
| GPU geometry (`@margoengine/geometry/gpu`) | Enforced by method: WebGPU only, `attach` throws `unsupported` on WebGL2; 1,000,000 vertices per item (core's own cap was the same until 2026-11-10 and is 11,184,810 now). Tube and ribbon frames are walked by one GPU invocation, so that step grows with `segments`. Speed is not measured. | Each frame depends on the one before it. | CPU raycasts and exports see zeros until `read()`. Control points written by your own compute pass are lost with the device. Default bounds are never culled. | Pass `bounds`; keep `segments` to what the curve needs; call `setPoints` again after a restore if you drive points on the GPU. |
| Exact booleans (`@margoengine/mesh-edit/boolean-exact`) | Enforced by method: every side test and all topology are exact, then corners round to float64. Faces thinner than about 4e-9 of their length, or a few float64 steps, fold away; `collapsedFaces` counts them. A single surface must not cross itself; overlapping shells of one input are joined first. Only faces in the box where the two bounds overlap go through the exact trees, and work there grows with their number squared: measured on two spheres of 10,224 triangles, one operation takes 7 to 11 s at half overlap, 2 to 3 s with a cutter a fifth the size, under 1 s when only the edges overlap (it was 40 to 75 s on 10,368 faces). A surface with nothing in that box, such as a cutter wholly inside a solid, takes the whole-mesh path. | `PolygonMesh` stores float64 corners and every face must pass the validity check, so a true result thinner than that has no valid float64 face. | A closed valid mesh that can differ from the exact solid by about 4e-9 of a face length; `MargoError` `failed` for a surface that crosses itself. | `booleanMeshes` in `/modeling` is faster on clean inputs; scale thin features up, or split large meshes. |
| Modifier stack (`@margoengine/mesh-edit/modifiers`) | Enforced: array `count` 1 to 4096, screw `steps` up to 4096, lattice 2 to 16 controls per axis. Not checked: walls thicker than a concave radius fold over themselves, and a screw profile is a surface because `PolygonMesh` has no loose edges. | The stack stays pure CPU work on valid polygon meshes; those limits bound one evaluate. | `RangeError` or `TypeError` from `evaluate`; a folded wall has faces that cross, with no error. | Thin the wall, or run `booleanMeshesExact` on the parts. |
| Smoothing (`smoothMesh` in `@margoengine/mesh-edit/modeling`) | Enforced: 1 to 10,000 passes; a Taubin factor whose filter magnitude at the top frequency, the absolute value of (1 - 2 factor)(1 - 2 mu), is above 1 (about 0.7 at the default pass band) throws, since it would amplify noise. By method: neighbors weigh equally, so uneven triangles drift along the surface. | Equal weights need no angle data and are what Taubin's method describes; cotangent weights fail on the thin triangles scans have. | Volume stays within 2% on a noisy sphere over 20 passes; very uneven meshes change shape slightly along the surface. | Run `remeshMesh` first. |
| Remeshing (`@margoengine/mesh-edit/remesh`) | Enforced: voxel grids stop at `maxCells`, 16,777,216 by default, and need a closed input. By method: isotropic output is triangles, or with `quads` mostly quads from a greedy matching with an augmenting search, with triangles left where seams and creases leave them no partner: on a rounded cube at `targetLength` 0.15, measured, 81.5% of triangles pair with seams kept (503 quads, 228 of 1,234 triangles alone) and 100% with `preserveSeams: false` (627 quads, none alone); a warped quad of either remesher is stored as two triangles (`quads` keeps the topology), parity counts an overlap of two parts as outside, and UVs do not carry through voxels. | Faces must be planar, and a grid has no link back to corner UVs. | `RangeError` above `maxCells`; `TypeError` for open input; `nonManifoldEdges` above 0 where two sheets pass within a voxel. | Raise `voxelSize` or `maxCells`; `fillMeshHoles` closes input; `booleanMeshesExact` unions overlapping parts first. |
| Sculpting (`@margoengine/mesh-edit/sculpt`, `/sculpt-view`) | Enforced: `undoLimit` 0 to 1,000; 200,000 vertices and faces in, like every mesh-edit mesh; `SculptView` up to gltf/pbr's 1,000,000 vertices. By method: output is triangles; a triangle covering more than 512 grid cells is tested by every ray. Measured (Node 26, one run, 199,712 triangles, other lanes running, diagnostic): a pick 10 ms before, 0.01 ms now; a dab of radius 0.08 on a unit sheet 21 ms, 1.4 ms; a stroke's undo step 90 ms, 1.6 ms. In a page, a stroke on 62,208 triangles uploaded 75,120 of 2,870,320 bytes. | A hash grid changes only where something crosses a cell, while a BVH needs a whole-tree refit per dab and a rebuild per split. Same output as testing everything: compared byte for byte over 1,273 checks. | With dynamic topology each change of triangles rewrites the whole mesh on the GPU, because gltf/pbr's ranged write keeps the indices. A vertex dragged so far that a ray crosses more cells than the mesh has triangles falls back to testing every triangle. | Sculpt a part of a mesh per session above 200,000 faces; use fixed topology while the mesh is large. |
| Dissolve border (`dissolveMeshComponents` in `@margoengine/mesh-edit/modeling`, 2026-11-15) | Enforced: a merged region's border has at most 4096 corners, the most the convex splitter takes ([large-boundary.test.js](../packages/mesh-edit/tests/large-boundary.test.js)). | Ear clipping is quadratic in the corner count, so a merged polygon past that is refused instead of split. | `MargoError` `unsupported` naming the border's corner count. | Dissolve the region in parts. |
| Hole filling (`fillMeshHoles` in `@margoengine/mesh-edit/modeling`) | By method: holes above 256 edges start from a center fan, not the lowest-cost search; a grid needs an even edge count and warped grid quads are stored as two triangles; new faces get planar UVs of their own. | The search costs edges cubed, and faces must be planar. | A long border fills from its center; an odd one in grid mode gets triangles. | `maxEdges` leaves large holes open for manual work. |
| High-to-low baking (`@margoengine/mesh-edit/bake`) | By method: one ray per texel at the texel center, no supersampling; overlapping UVs share texels, first triangle wins; colour reads the nearest texel; the bake runs on the calling thread. | Antialiasing would multiply ray cost, and a bake is an offline step. | Hard detail edges alias at low resolutions; `missed` counts texels whose ray found nothing. | Bake at twice the size and downscale; raise `distance` when `missed` is above zero. |
| Vertex groups (`@margoengine/mesh-edit/weights`) | By method: a brush reaches by straight-line distance, not along the surface; `skinAttributes` keeps at most 8 joints per vertex and drops the weakest; `remap` needs every edit in order. | Straight-line distance needs no surface walk per dab, and 4 influences is what glTF skinning takes. | A brush can touch both sides of a thin part; a vertex with more groups than influences loses the weakest. | Paint with a smaller radius; raise `influences` up to 8. |
| Closest point and frames (`closestPointOnSpline` in `@margoengine/splines/closest`, `SplineFrames` in `@margoengine/splines/frames`) | By method: the search samples the curve (`samples`, default the spline's `divisions`) and refines the best sample only, so passes closer together than one sample can be confused; frames are stored at `samples` steps (default 256) and blended between them; the tangent is a finite difference. | Sampling plus bisection keeps a query at `samples` curve evaluations with no per-curve setup. | A tight spiral can return a nearby pass instead of the nearest; frames drift from true rotation-minimising by less than the step size. | Raise `samples`. |
| Knot paths (`KnotPath` in `@margoengine/splines/knots`) | Enforced: 2 to 1,000,000 knots (3 minimum when closed); every knot carries the same number of data values. By method: a closed path builds an open Bezier whose last point is its first; a segment is straight only when both its knots are `linear`. | Bezier handles express auto, linear and broken tangents in one form. | `Spline.closed` is false for a closed path, so frames do not spread loop twist. | Build the curve with `Spline` and `closed: true` when you do not need broken tangents. |
| Place and deform along splines (`@margoengine/splines/mesh`) | Enforced: at most 1,000,000 instances. By method: a mesh bends in straight chords between its own vertices; normals are rotated with the frame, not re-derived; one frame lookup per distinct position along the axis. | Rotating normals needs no mesh connectivity. | A coarse mesh facets on a tight bend and a very sharp bend leaves normals slightly off. | Subdivide the mesh along its axis first. |
| Springs by duration and bounce (`Spring` in `@margoengine/tween`, 2026-11-06) | By method: `duration` is the period with no damping, so a spring settles later than `duration`, and a `Spring` keeps only the `stiffness` and `damping` worked out from it. | By method: `bounce` runs from above -1 to below 1, as 1 would never settle. | A spring settles later than `duration`, because `duration` is the period with no damping. | Read `spring.settled` to know when it has come to rest, or give `stiffness` and `damping` directly. |
| Custom ease curves (`@margoengine/tween/custom-ease`, 2026-11-06) | By method: x must run forward from exactly 0 to exactly 1, so a curve that loops back in time is refused. `easeFromStroke` needs a stroke that ends at another y than it began, and drops samples that go back in x. | The ease is a function of x, so x cannot go back in time. | A bezier is solved to about 1e-7 in x, as `cubicBezier` is. | Split a motion that loops back in time into two tweens in a `Timeline`, each with its own ease. |
| Scroll-linked timelines (`@margoengine/tween/scroll`, 2026-11-06) | By method: follows the main thread's `scroll` event, so it trails a compositor-driven scroll by up to a frame, where a CSS `animation-timeline` does not. `Timeline.call` callbacks do not run, as for any seek. | Selection masks (`PointCloud.setMask`, `Line.setMask`, sciviz `bindSelection`, 2026-11-11) | Enforced: one value a point in stored order, selected when true or above 0 (binary; fractional membership stays with bar and histogram bindings); a line segment is selected when both its points are; one mask style per cloud or line (fade, highlight or filter; fade and highlight amount in [0, 1], highlight colour and amount stored as 8-bit sRGB). | Fitting (`fitSpline` in `@margoengine/splines/fit`) | Enforced: 2 to 10,000,000 points, a `tolerance` above 0. | Tile metadata and Draco points (`@margoengine/tiles/metadata`, 2026-11-07) | Property tables proved on real Cesium samples (LIM-359); Draco pnts on real Draco data in a stand-in pnts (LIM-360). Feature ID textures, property textures, property attributes and a glTF `schemaUri` are not read; 64-bit integers become doubles; Draco pnts decode in Web Workers in a browser and in the calling thread in Node (since 2026-11-16, GAP-FILM-DRACO-NODE); another runtime without workers needs a decoder argument. | Written from the 3D Tiles Metadata binary table format and the EXT_structural_metadata, EXT_mesh_features and 3DTILES_draco_point_compression specifications; textures need an image decode this entry does not do. | `readStructuralMetadata` lists a texture feature ID set with no `ids`; integers past 2^53 lose low digits; `dracoPoints` in a runtime with neither Web Workers nor Node rejects without a decoder argument. | Sample the feature ID texture yourself; pass your own `decode(bytes)` as the third argument of `dracoPoints`. |
| Gaussian splat tiles (`@margoengine/tiles/splats`, 2026-11-07) | Proved on CesiumJS's real sh_unit_cube tileset on a real GPU (LIM-361). | Splat depth (`@margoengine/splats/depth`, 2026-11-07) | Proved on a Radeon 680M with a real capture (LIM-444). By method: a pixel takes the centre depth of the nearest splat whose own opacity there reaches `threshold` (default 0.5); depth is written after the cloud draws. | Splats blend far to near and the colour pass cannot write depth without hiding the splats behind; accumulated (median) depth needs a front-to-back pass. | Thin captures of many faint splats get depth only where one splat is solid (1,514 of 4,463 covered pixels on the raccoon fixture at 0.5); a mesh drawn before the cloud is not hidden by splats in front of it beyond the normal blend; transparent meshes (drawn before) are covered by the blend. | Lower `threshold`; draw glass with the cloud through `@margoengine/oit/vfx`. |
| Streamed splat level of detail (`@margoengine/splats/lod`, 2026-11-07) | Proved on a Radeon 680M with a real capture (LIM-453); the past-3,000,000 case on a procedural stand-in.
