Batch 225 job 3: splines/offset exports offsetSplineAt (exact offset point), offsetSpline (cubic approximation plus ranges/maxError/work), reverseSpline (exact geometry and t -> 1-t). Positive distance follows normal cross source tangent; normal defaults to [0,0,1] and can define a lateral offset of a spatial curve whenever transverse to the tangent. Defaults: tolerance=0.001 world units, maxDepth=20 (0..30), maxSegments=16384 (1..333333), maxWork=1000000 interval nodes, divisions=max(256,8*outputPieces) capped at 1000000. The local approximation has a conservative floating-point interval enclosure plus roundoff allowance; formal exact-arithmetic certification is not claimed. maxError excludes bevel joins, whose ranges have equal endpoints. Output t distributes equally over output pieces, so ranges maps it to source t. Closed paths get a closing bevel if needed. Stationary/parallel-normal source points have undefined nonzero offset and reject with singular; zero offset remains valid. Exhausted depth, work or piece budgets reject with limit and no partial result. Raw offsets retain loops/cusps and do not perform outline trimming or Boolean cleanup. Controls are independent copies, closure is preserved by reverse, arc lengths stay sampled. No GPU implementation, GPU tests or core/stage changes.

Batch 225 /offset: new optional entry 0 -> 4005 B gzip (ceiling 0 -> 4261 B); geometry operations belong together to share polynomial calculations. Core + stage remains 24209 B gzip, below 25000 B; root sources untouched.

### BVH parallel construction (batch 221)

Optional bvh/parallel adds buildParallel(source, options). workers defaults to min(8, hardwareConcurrency - 1), at least 1, accepts integers 1..64 and counts leaf workers plus one coordinator. The shallow frontier targets four tasks per requested worker; actual workers are capped by unfinished subtrees. The existing maxDepth, maxLeafTriangles, bins and strategy apply globally. Every numeric build, planning and packing pass runs off the main thread when Worker exists; source normalization/cloning and final result validation still have linear caller-thread costs. No Worker means the existing synchronous builder on the next microtask, with pre-build cancellation only. Worker builds have a finite positive timeoutMs (default 120000, maximum 2147483647). Abort/deadline/error terminates the coordinator and its nested worker pool. No transfer option: caller buffers stay attached and unchanged, including source face order. Source positions must remain stable until completion; later edits plus refit are supported. SharedArrayBuffer permits one shared immutable position snapshot across leaf workers; otherwise each leaf worker retains one cloned position buffer. This fallback uses additional memory proportional to worker count. Subtree indices/results are transferred. Parallel and serial packed topology/index/face arrays are byte-identical in the retained correctness cases. No speed ratio claimed.

## Batch 210 job 1: animation/mixer

## Batch 265 adaptive performance

The optional @margoengine/react/performance entry exports PerformanceMonitor, AdaptiveDpr, usePerformanceMonitor and PerformanceController. Defaults: 250 ms windows, 10 windows per decision, 0.75 required fraction, factor 1, step 0.1, unlimited direction reversals, fallbackFactor 0. Bounds default to [50,57] FPS, or [50,90] when a measured window exceeds 90 Hz. A 60 Hz presentation can therefore recover quality. FPS is frames divided by summed measured milliseconds; observed refresh is a high window average, not a display capability query. It is cadence, not GPU execution time. A sample prop accepts measured milliseconds or null from an application's collector; default intervals use the monotonic performance clock without the engine's delta cap. Hidden tabs and unsampled demand frames discard incomplete windows. Active slow frames remain measurements. Snapshots retain at most 4096 frame intervals per window while all intervals count toward the average. A direction reversal beyond flipflops fixes the factor at fallbackFactor until reset.

AdaptiveDpr defaults to min 0.5, max 1, pixelated false. Fractions apply to the Canvas's native resolution, not CSS layout. A package-owned target scales scene raster dimensions; native MSAA stays intact. Reduced frames add one full-canvas presentation triangle. Scale 1 returns to the original renderer, allowing exact restored pixels. Multiple holds use the lowest scale and nearest presentation if any requests it. Named Scenes and Canvas views retain their scene, camera, layers, clear and scissor. Explicit offscreen targets and tracked XR eye targets retain their owner's resolution. Picking uses original Canvas view coordinates. Removing the last hold destroys its texture immediately and retains only logical picking until the next Canvas draw; engine disposal always releases the adapter. Resources recreate after device restore. WebGPU and the WebGL2 compatibility layer are supported; native preview reports unsupported. No timing or throughput gain is claimed during the build phase.

Adaptive performance size: optional entry 0 -> 5619 B minified gzip, ceiling 5769 B. Keeping measurement, presentation and picking in one optional entry avoids duplicate lifetime and asynchronous render boundaries. Core + stage stays 24209 B on the current main baseline.

Adaptive diagnostics use stable MargoError codes and help links. The final React root is 10259 B gzip, React XR 4159 B; the performance entry above includes coded presentation-owner diagnostics.

## Mesh repair (batch 224 job 3)
The optional mesh-edit/repair entry exports repairMesh(input, options). Input is a polygon soup with unique nonempty face IDs, xyz vertices and index loops; corner UVs are optional. Defaults: distance 0 (exact duplicates), fillHoles true, maxHoleEdges 256. Up to 200000 input vertices and faces and 4096 corners per input face; output remains within standard PolygonMesh limits. Near welding is non-chaining and keeps the earliest eligible position. Nonfinite positions and invalid-index faces are discarded and named; structural array/ID errors reject. Missing or invalid UV corners reset to [0,0] with diagnostics. Concave/warped polygons split through existing mesh editing rules; unresolved, pinched and degenerate polygons are discarded.
When more than two faces compete for an edge, descending face area then input order select the retained manifold subset. A contradictory orientation constraint removes the encountered conflicting face and reports it. Disconnected vertex fans split identities. Existing hole filling uses triangles, refine false and fair false, so it adds a closure without moving surviving scan vertices; holes above maxHoleEdges stay open and are reported. Nested closed shells orient by solid-angle containment (cavities inward). Self-intersections and intersecting-shell intent are not reconstructed or certified. readyForBoolean checks closed opposing edge incidences and positive volume, followed by the actual solid validator; it is false for empty, open or zero-volume output. It does not promise valid geometric self-intersection behavior for arbitrary damaged scans. Result fields include every removed face/vertex, flipped/filled face, weld/fan counts and source face/vertex maps. Source and output arrays are independent. Cooperative AbortSignal checks bound work between traversal steps; no interactive latency claim.
Repair entry size: 0 to 9631 gzip bytes, with a 9920-byte ceiling. The optional entry includes the established hole filler and topology validation so repair stays complete; splitting them would add API complexity without reducing bytes when closure is needed. Core plus stage remains 24209 bytes.
### Legacy VTK datasets (batch 202)
`@margoengine/loaders/vtk-legacy` adds `parseVTKLegacy` independently of the root parser. All five legacy geometric dataset types support ASCII and big-endian binary, old packed cells and explicit OFFSETS/CONNECTIVITY. Source connectivity, offsets, cell types, point/cell/global FIELD data and source cell IDs for every drawn primitive survive. Numeric arrays retain float64 precision; rendering positions remain float32. Structured coordinates are x-fastest; ORIGIN defaults to [0,0,0] and SPACING/ASPECT_RATIO to [1,1,1]. `maxCells` defaults to maxTriangles; existing vertex/triangle bounds remain. `surface: 'outer'` suppresses shared volume faces; `'all'` retains them. Both readers reject inexact 64-bit integer values. Binary native `long` is eight bytes, matching the existing legacy reader. ASCII bit arrays and MSB-first packed binary bit arrays are decoded; polyhedron type 42 retains its original face stream in connectivity. Higher-order cell drawing retains corner points and warns; intact source topology is always returned for supported cells. Global FIELD arrays with tuple counts unlike the active association are kept in fieldData. No core or stage changes.
The optional /vtk-legacy entry is 6,336 B min+gzip (new, previously absent). Its 6,592 B ceiling retains the shared reader and complete dataset metadata instead of splitting user-facing APIs. Root loaders: 52,868 to 53,022 B; existing /vtk-xml: 7,514 B. Core plus stage remains 24,209 B.
Legacy VTK texture coordinates (loaders audit, 2026-11-15): `parseVTK` and `parseVTKLegacy` return `uvs` with v = 1 - t, as `parseVTKXML` does, since VTK puts t = 0 at the image's bottom; `pointData` keeps the file's own values. All three VTK readers fan a convex polygon from its first corner and ear-clip one that is not convex on the plane of its Newell normal; a self-intersecting polygon, which VTK does not allow, gets a best-effort result.

### XML DTDs (loaders, 2026-11-15)
`@margoengine/loaders/xml` reads the DOCTYPE as XML 1.0 Fifth Edition (W3C, 2008, https://www.w3.org/TR/xml/) section 5.1 asks of a non-validating processor: the whole internal subset, parameter entities included (4.4.8, enlarged by a space either side), attribute defaults and type normalization (3.3, 3.3.3), and entities holding markup read as content (4.4.2, each holding whole elements, 4.3.2). External entities, the external subset among them, are read only from `external`, which `resolveDTD` fills through the caller's `resolve`; nothing is fetched otherwise, because a document from an untrusted source must not make the reader fetch the URLs it names. Browsers' DOMParser, which the common web 3D loaders use for COLLADA, X3D, 3MF and KML, does not fetch external DTDs either, so the default matches them and `resolveDTD` is an addition. Without `external`, an entity the unread part may declare is a `LoaderError` with code `unsupported` (4.4.3 lets a non-validating processor skip it but asks it to say so; there is no result to give without its text), and entity and attribute declarations after an unread parameter entity are skipped unless `standalone="yes"` (5.1). Limits: `maxExpansion` (default 1 Mi characters) for all entity and parameter entity text brought in, the external subset itself not counted; `resolveDTD` reads at most `maxFiles` (64) entities and `maxCharacters` (16 Mi) in all. Not done: validation (element content models are skipped, IDs are not checked), NOTATION use, and `xml:base`. Every format parser that reads XML (`parseDAE`, `parseKMZ`, `parseX3D`, `parse3MF`, `parse3MFLattice`, `parseAMF`, `parseKML`, `parseGPX`, `parseTMX` with its TSX tilesets, `parseSVG`, `parseMaterialX`, `parseVTKXML`, `openVTKXMLDataset`) takes the same optional `external` (type `XMLExternalOptions`), the result of `resolveDTD`; the parsers never fetch. The relationship parts of 3MF and the OPC `.rels` files are read without it, as they carry no DTD in any producer's output.

### G-code arcs (loaders audit, 2026-11-15)
`parseGCode` draws G2 and G3 arcs as chords no more than 0.002 mm from the arc, at least 16 per turn, so a 10 mm radius quarter turn takes 40 chords (80 vertices against `maxVertices`). Centre offsets (I, J, K) and radius (R) forms, full circles, P turns and helices are read in the G17, G18 and G19 planes. G90.1 (absolute centres: I, J and K are the centre itself, both of the plane's words required) and G91.1 (incremental, the default) follow the LinuxCNC G-code reference (linuxcnc.org/docs/html/gcode/g-code.html, G90.1 and G91.1, and G2 and G3). What P counts differs by firmware and is the `arcP` option: `'turns'` (default) is LinuxCNC's number of turns, P1 the programmed arc alone and each step above 1 one more full circle; `'circles'` is Marlin's (marlinfw.org/docs/gcode/G002-G003.html, `ARC_P_CIRCLES`, "Specify complete circles"), P full circles added to the arc, so Marlin's Pn draws LinuxCNC's P(n + 1) and P0 is allowed. Marlin's page does not say in so many words whether P counts the first turn; 'circles' reads it as full circles on top of the arc, as its wording and parameter name suggest. RepRapFirmware documents no P parameter for G2 and G3 (Duet3D, "GCode dictionary", "G2: Controlled Arc Move", docs.duet3d.com/User_manual/Reference/Gcodes, read 2026-11-15): a full circle is an end point equal to the start with the centre given by I and J, which `parseGCode` already reads as a full turn whatever `arcP` is, so `arcP` has no RepRapFirmware reading. RepRapFirmware 3.6.2 and later rejects an arc whose start and end radius differ by more than 0.0022 mm in CNC mode or 0.05 mm in FDM and laser mode; `parseGCode` keeps LinuxCNC's tolerance below, so it accepts some arcs that firmware refuses and does not model the firmware's mode. Its G90.1 behaviour is not checked. An end off its circle by more than LinuxCNC's tolerance (0.5 mm, or both 0.005 mm and 0.1% of the radius) and an R shorter than half its chord are `range` errors. Not read: G17.1 to G19.1 and the 5 to 9 axis forms.

### STL colours (loaders, 2026-11-15)
`parseSTL` reads both binary colour conventions described in the colour section of the "STL (file format)" article (Wikipedia, read 2026-11-15; neither vendor publishes a format note). VisCAM / SolidView: bit 15 of the facet attribute set marks a colour, red in bits 10 to 14. Materialise Magics: the 80-byte header holds `COLOR=` and four RGBA bytes for the whole part, optionally `,MATERIAL=` and diffuse, specular and ambient RGBA (the diffuse is used for the part colour, as Magics prefers the material), and bit 15 has the opposite meaning: clear marks a facet's own colour, red in bits 0 to 4, set takes the part colour. `colorVariant: 'auto'` picks Materialise only when `COLOR=` is in the header, so a Magics file saved without a part colour reads as VisCAM unless `colorVariant: 'materialise'` is passed; the two cannot be told apart from the bits alone. Header alpha is returned in `materialise` but `colors` holds RGB only. ASCII per-facet colours have no shared convention and are not read.

### Pixel-exact area queries (batch 199 job 3)
`@margoengine/selection/area` exports AreaPicking and AreaPickingOptions. Attach instead of Picking, retaining ordinary pick/pickMany and add(source). `rect({x,y,width,height}, view?, signal?)` accepts CSS pixels and normalizes negative dimensions; `polygon(points, view?, signal?)` accepts 3-4096 finite xy vertices and uses even-odd filling. Only included raster pixel centres count, including fractional CSS/DPR boundaries; empty/fully clipped regions return no hits. Results are unique visible triangle IDs, preserving model, primitive and instance identity, in first raster occurrence order. Fully occluded geometry, unrendered bounding spheres, approximate proxies and non-mesh overlays are excluded. Opacity, clipping, sidedness and current deformation use the same replay as point queries. With multiple views, pass the desired view; omitted view uses the engine camera/scene across the canvas. Queries honor viewport, scissor and layers.
Each area query owns one cropped r32uint target, one depth32float target and a 256-byte-pitched staging buffer. Default maxPixels is 16777216, additionally bounded by device texture dimensions and maxBufferSize. AbortSignal is checked before queued work and after mapping; pending GPU resources remain alive through completion and are destroyed in finally. Point capture defaults false and may be enabled separately. Concurrent area and ordinary point calls retain separate operations through the engine queue. New entry 15287 B min+gzip, ceiling 15719 B; selection root 21308 -> 21464 B and hit-details 15002 -> 15152 B remain inside existing ceilings. The entry includes its common picker rather than duplicating replay/resource ownership. Core plus stage stays 24209 B.
## Batch 210 job 2: animation/playback
New optional entry 1817 B min+gzip (previously 0), ceiling 2073 B. It intentionally imports the existing Animation root/model runtime; the reported size leaves shared bare package imports external. Core/stage source stays unchanged, below 25000 B.
Import Animation (alias of PlaybackAnimation) from animation/playback for plain play/pause/seek and existing deformation with loop/finished events, finished promise, loop modes and total traversal counts. Defaults inherit loop=true and speed=1; loopMode defaults LoopRepeat (LoopOnce with loop=false), repetitions=Infinity, timeScale=1, no signal. LoopOnce always uses one traversal. Negative timeScale plays backward; play starts negative-rate clips at their end. Ping-pong counts each traversal. A multi-boundary update emits one loop event with signed loopDelta, while the final boundary emits finished once after the terminal pose.
play renews completion, rejecting an interrupted run with AbortError. dispose and constructor signal abort reject pending completion; waitForFinished accepts independent cancellation without stopping playback. seek accepts nonnegative total seconds, emits no events and resets traversal counting; use play to renew a finished run. Events use on or EventTarget-style listeners; listener signal cancellation is supported. Loop counts must be safe positive integers or Infinity, and boundary jumps must be countable as safe integers. A zero-duration clip finishes once, without an infinite loop.

### Batch 243 mesh PBR channels
Optional mesh-pbr supports normals, four UV sets, RGBA vertex colours, base-colour, tangent normal, metallic/roughness and emissive RGBA8 maps, explicit affine instances and OPAQUE/MASK coverage. Mesh material ids are independent of the 255-entry voxel palette. Surface/texture/vertex packets share the existing 128 MiB geometry limit. Samplers support repeat, mirrored repeat, clamp, nearest and linear-light bilinear reconstruction at the base mip. Normal XY scale can be negative; finite UV/transform/tangent values stay within +/-1e8. Colours are linear factors; base/emissive image RGB decodes sRGB before interpolation, data maps and alpha stay linear. BLEND coverage (2026-11-25) is stochastic transparency: each traversal keeps a BLEND candidate with probability equal to its coverage, from a hash of the ray's current random state and the hit distance rounded to 13 mantissa bits (no extra random number is drawn, so scenes without BLEND trace exactly as before; triangles sharing an edge take one decision; two BLEND layers closer than about 1.2e-4 of their distance along the ray take the same decision); sampled light points on a BLEND emitter emit their coverage times the emission. Converged images are the coverage-weighted mix; single samples are binary per ray. There is no ordered compositing of layers (order-independent by construction) and no refraction: use transmission for volumes. Skinned and morphing glTF models (2026-11-25) trace the pose last drawn: `traceSceneFromGLTF` reads deformed vertices back from the GPU (`readPickingGeometry`), copies them with the materials and images, and `setScene` rebuilds the BLAS of every mesh whose content changed (a full spatial-median rebuild in the lazy Wasm kernel, not a refit) while unchanged meshes reuse theirs. Each pose therefore costs one GPU readback, one image copy per texture and one rebuild per deformed mesh; there is no in-place GPU skinning into the trace buffer and no BVH refit, which suits offline frame-by-frame renders rather than an interactive viewport at full rate. Motion blur across a pose change is not traced. The glTF adapter reads current geometry and source material definitions, with an explicit imagePixels callback for compressed/streamed images. It preserves borrowed-image ownership and rejects merged primitives without source identity. No new core or stage feature is added.

Entry size: mesh-pbr 0 to 37,233 B min+gzip, with a new 38,350 B optional ceiling. This includes the existing geometry Wasm/traversal and the material, sampler and glTF snapshot boundary; splitting the surface channels would duplicate the same packet/frame/lifetime coupling. The existing mesh entry is 32,933 B. Core plus stage remains 24,209 B, below 25,000 B.

### Optional CPU occlusion on the full WebGL2 layer

`@margoengine/culling/webgl2` supplies `WebGL2Culling` for opaque core meshes on
both the full WebGL2 layer and native WebGPU. It rebuilds a 128 by 128 CPU depth
buffer each view using actual triangles, then redirects compacted 96-byte rows.
Resolution accepts integers 1 through 2048. It uses no hardware queries, no GPU
readback and no previous-frame visibility. `readCounts()` returns the last view's
counts synchronously. Use one redirect owner per batch. Picking and shadow data
stay complete. Surface-changing core shaders disable occlusion for that frame.
The preview renderer is unsupported. Models and dynamic GPU-only geometry retain
their existing cullers; this entry culls core batches. Near-plane-crossing triangles,
triangle seams and partially covered cells can retain hidden objects. This is
conservative excess drawing, never an excuse to cull visible surfaces. CPU work
scales with occluder triangles and covered software cells; no speed claim is made.

Batch 223 job 1 size: culling/webgl2 new entry, 0 to 2442 B gzip. Its CPU depth
and upload code stay together because both implement this one optional feature.
Core plus stage remains 24,209 B gzip (under 25,000); no frozen code changed.
### FBX optional texture formats (batch 205)

`@margoengine/fbx/textures` exports `textures`, passed in `FBXOptions.extensions`. It routes embedded
and external TGA, DDS, TIFF/TIF and BMP through decoder entries, lazily, then encodes PNG. Default
FBX byte and pixel budgets still apply. DDS material images must be 2D; only the base mip is embedded
in GLB, whose runtime generates its mips. Float TIFF/DDS values clamp to 0..1 and encode to sRGB PNG. The decoder entries define
format support; damaged recognized inputs reject instead of silently dropping a texture. Unknown
formats and missing files retain the existing missing-texture record. Multiple image hooks are tried
in extension order, and the first successful conversion wins.

67,108,864. OS/2 core and Windows 40/52/56/108/124-byte DIB headers, indexed 1/4/8-bit, RGB 16/24/32-bit,

are opaque. JPEG/PNG-in-BMP, OS/2 v2 compression and embedded colour-profile transforms are not supported.

The texture-rgba decoder entry shares the existing textureFileToRGBA implementation with decoders/image, without container/transcoder imports. BMP and texture bridge defaults do not add a core/stage feature.

### Batch 243 optional learned denoiser
`voxel-pathtracer/denoise-ml` exposes DenoiseML.create(engine, {signal}), denoise(image, {signal}), whenIdle, dispose and Symbol.dispose. It requires an engine WebGPU compute device (the existing WebGL2 compatibility device is supported), finite RGB Float32 color/albedo/normal guides from renderImage with aovs:true, positive integer dimensions totaling at most 16,777,216 pixels, positive samples and optional coverage in [0,1]. Color is signed, each value within the Float32 representation of 1e16 of zero (renderImage gives few-sample pixels negative channels behind dispersive glass; the luminance features use x/(1+|x|), equal to the trained x/(1+x) on the nonnegative training data, so the weights are unchanged), albedo [0,1], normal components [-1,1]. Device binding/buffer/grid limits apply in addition. Device changes rebuild weights and the pipeline; each request snapshots every input AOV, owns its output and preserves alpha, albedo, normal, depth, instance and palette arrays. Cancellation rejects queued/active waits promptly and disposal releases owned buffers. GPU failures use coded failed errors with their platform cause.
The 321-parameter, two-hidden-layer network predicts a single 3x3 positive reconstruction kernel; it is spatial, with no temporal history, downloaded weights or external inference runtime. Input guides are required. HDR normalization and softmax preserve finite constant fields and bound reconstructed RGB by observed neighbor radiance. Synthetic training and the licensed Box holdout are narrow correctness/quality evidence, not a claim of universal image-quality superiority.
The entry measures 6,781 B min+gzip after the signed-colour fix (6,767 B before; ceiling 7,023 B), previously absent. Root/core/stage gain no code. Batch 172 job 3: optional sciviz/clip supplies scalar/plane/box/sampled-sphere cuts, iso-volume, whole-cell crinkle, point/cell threshold and Cartesian/curvilinear structured subsets. imageGrid supports 2D/3D topology and up to 1000000 samples. Sciviz threshold components (2026-11-10): `thresholdGrid` tests a component index, the Euclidean magnitude (the default for arrays wider than one) or all/any components against an inclusive range; one end may be infinite for a one-sided threshold. Region IDs follow cell count (descending by default, or ascending) or lowest cell ID; equal sizes order by lowest cell ID. Scalar connectivity tests point scalars only. Inputs are bounded by the clip entry limits (imageGrid 1,000,000 samples). Evidence: packages/sciviz/tests/clip.test.js.

Sciviz multi-volume (2026-11-10): sciviz/multivolume draws 1 to 4 channels, each 2 to 2048 samples an axis, as r16float textures (about 3 significant digits after range normalisation), with one 256-entry transfer row per channel, no lighting, clip planes, scene-depth occlusion or 2D classification, and no drawing while the camera is inside the union box (back faces are culled). ### Geospatial vector formats (batch 202)
The optional `@margoengine/loaders/geo` provides parseGeoJSON, parseShapefile, parseGPX, parseKML and parseMVT. New entry 0 -> 2339 B min+gzip, ceiling 2595 B; model data, validation, parts and shared patch evaluation belong together rather than duplicating the evaluator across part entries. Core + stage remains 24209 B. The margoengine/geometry/teapot alias is generated from the same entry.

### Headless GIF and exporter palette (batch 209)
Entry bytes (min+gzip, bare package imports external): headless/gif 118 B (new, ceiling 374 B), exporters/palette 2,597 B (new, ceiling 2,853 B), exporters/capture 6,944 -> 7,667 B (ceiling 7,241 -> 7,923 B). The 118 B wrapper requires the optional exporters peer; its codec bytes are in the capture entry, sharing palette quantization. These bytes retain one writer, stream cancellation, explicit duration/repeat policies and correct rounding. Splitting another codec would duplicate LZW and quantization or add lazy-loader plumbing. Core plus stage stays 24,209 B.
encodeGIF accepts sync/async RGBA8 frames; only one raw frame is retained plus the compressed result. fps defaults to 30, in 100/65535..50. dither defaults false; loop defaults 0 (forever), -1 plays once, 1..65535 repeats. Per-frame duration overrides fps and accepts 0.02..655.35 seconds. Sizes are consistent and <=65,535 per side; data must fit memory. Alpha <128 is transparent, otherwise opaque, as GIF supports one-bit alpha. Each frame has a local <=256-colour RGB palette (255 opaque colours with transparency). Exact colours are preserved when they fit; other frames use shared median cut and optional ordered Bayer dithering. The signal interrupts waiting for the next frame; producers must also observe it to release their own pending work. No CPU speed claim or speculative Wasm rewrite.

## Mesh convex hull and Minkowski sum (batch 224 job 4)
geometry/hull exports convexHullTriangles(points, {signal}) with outward indices into the original flat/nested xyz positions. Empty or lower-dimensional sets return empty indices. The existing Quickhull predicates use a translated unit frame and a 1e-10 coordinate-scale tolerance; this is a floating hull, not an exact predicate claim. Source coordinates are never narrowed to float32. Legacy geometry/extras convexGeometry retains its original errors and float32 rendering buffers.
mesh-edit/hull exports convexMeshHull(oneMeshOrArray, {createId, signal}) and minkowskiSumMeshes(a, b, options). Hull includes all supplied positions (including loose vertices), emits newly generated triangle IDs/planar UVs, and returns an owned empty solid for empty/flat input. Maximum hull input is 200000 positions and normal output mesh limits apply. Minkowski inputs are closed outward consistently wound solids or empty; output has mesh, cells [a,b], convexPairs, planeTriples, collapsedFaces and diagnostics. Empty operands absorb. Concavity, disconnected components and cavities are supported by BSP interior cells and union of convex pair sums. Every output face has a new ID; caller corner attributes are not meaningful under the sum and UVs are planar.
Minkowski defaults: maxCells 2048 per operand, maxPairs 65536, maxPlaneTriples 2000000 per operand. A convex pair may contribute at most 200000 vertex sums; the batch input/output limits also apply. Budgets are positive safe integers and exceeding them rejects with guidance, not partial geometry. Cell decisions/intersections use the existing exact representation, but exported cell coordinates and additions are float64 and Quickhull uses its documented tolerance; a positive cell too thin for that hull rejects explicitly. The final union's validity-preserving thin-face folds are counted. This is not exact arithmetic Minkowski output or a geometric self-intersection repair API; normalize intersecting component soups first. AbortSignal is checked throughout. Worst-case BSP decomposition and pair enumeration can be large, so no interactive or speed claim is made. Core/stage remain unchanged.
Entry sizes: mesh-edit/hull 0 to 11992 gzip bytes (12352-byte ceiling); geometry/hull 0 to 2071 bytes (2327-byte ceiling). Shared Quickhull keeps geometry/extras growth at 5570 to 5617 bytes within its existing ceiling. The optional bytes cover nonconvex and cavity-capable sums rather than a convex-only partial API. Core plus stage remains 24209 bytes.

### FBX large entry (batch 205)

`@margoengine/fbx/large` exports `largeFBX(overrides)` and `FBXImportLimits`. Pass the returned
immutable extension in `extensions` to convertFBX, parseFBX, loadFBX or their worker forms. One
limit configuration per import; unknown names and nonpositive/noninteger/unsafe values reject.
Ordinary imports keep every existing default. All figures below are caps, never reservations.

| Field | Ordinary | largeFBX default |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| inputBytes | 64 MiB | 512 MiB |
| decodedBytes | 128 MiB | 2 GiB |
| arrayBytes | 128 MiB | 512 MiB |
| nodes | 100,000 | 1,000,000 |
| properties | 2,000,000 | 16,000,000 |
| parseWork | 128,000,000 | 2,000,000,000 |
| sceneBytes | 128 MiB | 2 GiB |
| sceneWork | 128,000,000 | 2,000,000,000 |
| morphBytes | 64 MiB | 512 MiB |
| vertices | 1,000,000 | 8,000,000 |
| corners | 3,000,000 | 24,000,000 |
| geometryWork | 40,000,000 | 320,000,000 |
| textureBytes | 64 MiB | 512 MiB |
| texturePixels | 16,000,000 | 268,435,456 (1 GiB of RGBA8) |
| outputBytes | 128 MiB | 512 MiB |

MiB = 1,048,576 bytes; GiB = 1,073,741,824 bytes. `vertices` bounds control points,
expanded vertices and the cumulative scene vertices (including instances); `corners` bounds
polygon corners and triangulated indices. Allocation/work accounting remains conservative,
so dense seams/instances may need higher caps. Raising a cap cannot create available memory.
The 4,096-corner polygon, hierarchy depth, animation/key/sample limits and GLB uint32 format
limits are unchanged. Imported meshes are never decimated or truncated to meet these caps.

Measured default ceiling (2026-11-11, RTX A6000 workstation): the defaults hold a 996,004-vertex mesh with every corner
its own vertex (normals, one UV set, tangents; binary FBX with compressed arrays, 6.7 MiB): it converts, attaches with
`parseFBX` and renders on WebGPU and on the WebGL2 layer, uploading its GPU geometry once; the converted file holds
one primitive, which gltf/pbr draws as parts of at most 262,144 vertices (its default `maxPartVertices`), one draw
each, covering every vertex and every triangle once (`packages/fbx/test/large.test.js`, `test/default-scale-browser.mjs`,
`test/part-coverage.js`). What bounds it: the
1,000,000 expanded-vertex cap (a second primitive starts past 999,997 vertices and repeats the corners of a polygon
split across it). The memory caps sit just above it for this layout: the geometry build reserves 94 B per corner for
a mesh of unique vertices with normals and one UV set (each term a typed array of exactly that size; it was about
267 B, which stopped such a mesh at about 480,000 corners under the 128 MiB scene cap), decoded arrays are about 75 MiB
of the 128 MiB array cap (an inflated array is counted while it lives, not added to the total after its typed copy is
made), and an uncompressed file reaches the 64 MiB input cap first, at about 860,000 such vertices. WebGPU's default
device limits do not bind: a converted primitive holds at most 1,000,000 vertices and a drawn part 262,144 of 80 B (under the 128 MiB storage binding)
and its index buffer is far under the 256 MiB buffer size. Past the default ceiling `largeFBX` raises every cap.

Batch 205 large entry: 539 B min+gzip, new ceiling 795 B. FBX worker finished at 98,163 B, within its existing 100,703 B ceiling (before 97,769 B). Core plus stage is 24,209 B; 16,769 B was the separately reported particlesOnly build.

The large configuration also reaches GLTFAsset attachment and worker prepareGLTF: the converted GLB uses outputBytes and nodes as its downstream caps. Ordinary attachment retains the pre-existing 64 MiB glTF cap. The 2,500,002-vertex test produces a buffer above 64 MiB and attaches both directly and from prepared worker output.

Large material partitions are emitted as additional child mesh nodes at triangle boundaries, with at most 1,000,000 vertices per primitive, matching the existing PBR storage-binding safety cap. Every triangle and layer is retained; control-point maps still drive skin and morph remapping. Shared vertices on a chunk boundary may be duplicated and count against the configured vertex cap. This adds draw calls rather than reducing geometry. The 2,500,002-vertex independent-triangle fixture emits three full primitives and retains every position/index.

### Progressive splat loading (batch 238)
Optional splats/progressive reads standard vertex-only ASCII/little-endian Gaussian PLY, 32-byte splat and SPZ 2/3/4 byte streams. Captures remain limited to 3,000,000 splats and PLY headers to 64 KiB. Default batchSize is 16,384. Raw splat requires its count; other formats declare it. Available batches are sorted largest opacity-weighted volume first, with stable equal scores; server ordering controls which records arrive first. The capture's declared pool is reserved on its first drawable batch, and uploaded records share the existing GPU depth sort. Whole untransformed straight-alpha ImageBitmaps retain RGB at low/zero alpha; transformed copies still use the existing Canvas2D path. (Superseded by KB0477, 2026-11-11: every ImageBitmap copy on the WebGL2 layer is a GPU copy that keeps straight RGB, flips, crops and converts alpha as WebGPU does. A bitmap whose every copied texel is unchanged by premultiplying, and so cannot show its alpha state, is taken as premultiplied; both readings give the same bytes except where alpha is between 1 and 254 and dividing by it changes a small RGB value, which no page can tell apart either The quality size records of @margoengine/webgl2-compat grew from 111,889 B to 112,716 B gzip (full) and from 80,737 B to 81,105 B (base, without the compute runtime and read-back) for this path.)
Batch 172 calculator: /calc is optional; core/stage remain unchanged at 24209 B gzip. Up to 1000000 points/cells, 64 input tuple components, 4096 expression characters, 512 parsed expressions and nesting 64. Float32 snapshots/coefficients; per-value absolute parity bounds exclude quantisation and discretisation. Rank cutoff 1e-12; centers are vertex means; connectivity is shared-point topology; quality definitions and GPU/CPU ownership are in docs/sciviz-analysis.md. No speed claim.
Batch 172 /calc entry: new 0 to 6722 B min+gzip (ceiling 6978 B); parser, derived operators and conditioning bounds remain together to avoid public import fragmentation. Core/stage unchanged at 24209 B.


### Optional front-to-back instance ordering

`@margoengine/culling/sort` exports FrontToBack for kept core batches (including
DynamicInstances) and registered model instances, SortedInstances for the static
CulledInstances draw path, and InstanceSorter for 96-byte GPU lists. Sorting is
optional; enabled and sortEnabled default true on the respective optional
classes and can change at runtime. Core and model sorting executes after culling
and before drawing, independent of registration order. Model tint/transmission
lists and alphaMode BLEND primitives retain their existing order. Plain model
primitives keep their original draws; deformed models retain their bypass.
Each range orders by its transformed local center along the current view
forward direction, with original row indices breaking equal-depth ties. It
supports perspective and orthographic views, reflection and node transforms.
Ordering is per batch, as with specialised batched renderers, rather than across
materials or geometries. Counts, picking/caster buffers and every record field
stay unchanged. Opaque surfaces that overlap at equal surface depth but have
different center depths can resolve in the new order, the usual draw-order
consequence of sorting. Transparent geometry must never be passed to the raw
sorter. Importing ordinary cullers does not load ordering code.
InstanceSorter accepts capacity 0 through 4,194,304 within device storage limits;
its key network rounds to a power of two. It binds only the rows a range reads (from the last record at or before
`start` meeting minStorageBufferOffsetAlignment to `start + capacity`), so a core instance buffer that has doubled past
one storage binding still sorts (2026-11-11; before, it bound the whole buffer, a validation error every frame past
about 1,048,574 meshes of one geometry on a 128 MiB device). A list past one binding itself (1,398,101 records at
128 MiB) is refused by `encode` with RangeError; `InstanceSorter.fits(device, capacity, start)` tells, and
FrontToBack leaves such a list in its original order (drawn the same, unsorted). Scale check
`packages/culling/test/gpu/sort-scale-check.mjs`: 1,200,000 meshes, frames equal to core's natively and on the WebGL2
layer. O(n log-squared n) key comparisons and
one gather are encoded; no per-instance CPU work or GPU readback occurs. Each
view and stage owns distinct parameter storage. Input instance buffers require
STORAGE; supplied argument buffers require STORAGE and COPY_SRC. Software
occlusion arguments now expose those flags too. No speed claim is made.

Removed sort owners release all their view resources with InstanceSorter.forget;
FrontToBack also collects owners absent from the preceding frame and releases
registered model resources on removal. Cleanup happens before a later frame,
after the prior frame's command submission; existing view uploads stay distinct.

Batch 223 job 3 minified gzip: /sort is new, 0 to 14060 B. /webgl2 stays 3028 B while exposing storage/copy access to its argument buffer. /bounds stays 19447 B. The sort entry shares one network implementation across drawing routes and reuses the existing static culler; a split would duplicate resource state and complicate import/use. Core plus stage remains 24,209 B. firstInstance prefixes are included in capacity; their indirect word and draw offset are preserved, along with every other indirect word.

### Graph transition offsets and interruption (batch 211 job 3)

GraphTransition.offset defaults to 0, accepts finite 0..1 and sets destination entry time relative to its longest clip. Events start at that entry, including a marker exactly at the offset. Crossfades retain their own seconds clock, so a large offset cannot prematurely end an uninterruptible fade. interruptionSource is none, current, next, both (alias current-next), current-next or next-current. Each source checks transitions in declaration order, with any-state rules eligible for that source; only the selected rule consumes triggers. ## Mesh-surface scatter (batch 231 job 2)

scatterSurface(geometryData, count, options) from @margoengine/scatter/surface returns owned transforms, positions, normals, uvs and colors arrays. Defaults: seed 1; scale [1,1]; yaw [0,2*pi] radians; align 1; offset 0; source matrix identity; no weights or painted colours; no cancellation signal. Count is 0..1000000. Source triangles must have positive weighted area even with count 0. Vertex weights are nonnegative and interpolated linearly within each triangle. Areas are measured in world space after options.matrix, including nonuniform scale; normals use its inverse transpose. Arrays and source geometry are not mutated. Sources and outputs must fit finite f32 values; placements are nonsingular affine world matrices with uniform scale. Use an identity TexturedScatter model root for world placements, or convert into that root's space.

Output costs 112 bytes per placement (16 matrix, 3 position, 3 normal, 2 UV and 4 colour floats), plus the sampler's triangle CDF and transformed source copies when a matrix is supplied. Alignment is the shortest rotation from world +Y, then optional local yaw; the antipodal -Y case chooses +X as its turn axis. Offset is along the sampled normal. No mesh-to-heightmap projection: cliffs, roofs and undersides are sampled directly. Resample when source geometry or weights change. Entry gzip 0 to 1259 bytes, ceiling 1515 bytes; core plus stage remains 24209 bytes.
Batch 172 /glyph: optional instanced glyphs and scalar/vector warp, with at most 1000000 input points (images follow imageGrid's existing 2D/3D limits). Stride/mask apply to original row IDs; an all-zero instance scale is omitted, while a zero component (components scaling of a planar field) draws the glyph flattened along that axis with the plane normal. Cell centres are vertex means. Finite f32 render transforms/bounds; grid warp coordinates are f64 and surface output is f32. Line sources are thin tubes; custom meshes use +X and retain their own origin. Bounds are conservative spheres; explicit triangle normals rebuild after warp, while arbitrary field arrays remain borrowed. No tensor transport, element-inversion guarantee or timing claim. Core/stage unchanged at 24209 B gzip.

Batch 172 /glyph entry: new 0 to 4388 B min+gzip, ceiling 4644 B; optional placement, shapes, warp and ownership stay together to avoid API fragmentation. Core/stage unchanged at 24209 B.

Batch 205 job 4: `@margoengine/fbx/surfaces` exports `surfaces`, an optional extension on page and worker conversion. It tessellates Nurb/NurbsSurface and Patch geometry, including older inline Model geometry after legacyFBX normalization, independently of extension ordering. NURBS orders 2..32, positive rational weights, open/closed/periodic nets and every nonempty knot span use loaders/nurbs. FBX Step controls subdivisions per span; absent Step defaults to four times degree. Bezier cubic, BezierQuadric quadratic, Cardinal cubic, uniform cubic BSpline and Linear patch bases may differ on U and V. Open Bezier nets require 1 modulo degree control points; closed nets add their seam point; Cardinal open spans interpolate the interior controls and closed spans wrap. Closure wraps the necessary weighted rows/columns. Parametric UVs, analytic/pole normals, FlipNormals, material links, model transforms and animation remain in the ordinary FBX path. UCapped/VCapped generate flat-normal cap polygons, with the existing 4,096-corner polygon limit. All generated work and buffers charge the import budgets before allocation; vertex/corner limits include caps. Blend shapes on a surface are exact morph targets at every weight (normals exact at full weight); a skin is exact where the control points a vertex reaches share one weight set, and where they blend it is exact through four helper joints for each joint whose weight changes there (KB5330c, 2026-11-25), so two such joints fit the eight influences glTF and the engine take; three, a negative share (Cardinal patches) or a blend in an Additive or TotalOne cluster is refused with the polygon-bake remedy. Each weight set costs one more tessellation of the grid, and each changing joint two. Deformers on legacy inline Model geometry are refused.
The output is the whole parametric surface, not trimmed topology. Control-point skin deformation needs a bind position per joint, which one glTF vertex position holds only through helper joints: up to two changing joints a vertex are exact that way (KB5330c), and anything past that fails with coded unsupported/help and a polygon-bake remedy, rather than misapplying original control-point indices to generated vertices. Ordinary polygon skin/morph import is unchanged. Separate Maya ASCII/binary exports contain different near-zero control coordinates; exact front-end parity is proven by encoding the same real control net both ways, without rounding the product output.
Job 4 min+gzip: new surfaces entry 3,177 B (ceiling 3,433 B); FBX root 22,042 to 22,049 B and page worker entry 23,094 to 23,102 B. The root remains below its ceiling; the page worker ceiling rises 23,098 to 23,796 B for the shared geometry-normalization dispatch. Separating it would duplicate fallback conversion. Classic worker 100,787 to 105,877 B, ceiling 103,811 to 109,054 B, buys the shared rational evaluator, all patch bases and caps. Splitting would duplicate evaluator delivery/normalization ownership in the classic worker. Core plus stage remains 24,209 B after build:packages and measure:size.

## Batch 207 job 4: live Blender node graphs
blender/nodes is a new optional entry; entry size and ceiling are recorded with the job's size evidence below. Core and stage are untouched. Export live_nodes defaults false. When true, reachable unsupported nodes or surface lobes fail by material/node name, with the existing baked export available by disabling live_nodes. No silent baking in the live path.
Supports Value/RGB, reroutes, Math (41 scalar operations including safe divide/power/log domains), MixRGB and Mix (Float/Vector/RGBA, 19 color blend modes; Hue and Color keep A when B is grey, and Saturation keeps a grey A grey, since a grey has no hue), Color Ramp (2..32 stops, Constant/Linear/Ease/Cardinal/B-spline, RGB/HSV/HSL and four hue directions), Noise (1D..4D, Fac/Color, fractional detail 0..15, normalized fBM, multifractal, ridged, hybrid and hetero terrain, roughness/lacunarity/distortion/offset/gain), UV/Generated/Object/Normal coordinates and RGB/XYZ separate/combine. Principled live inputs: base, alpha, metalness, roughness, emission/color strength and IOR. Other shader types, groups, images, arbitrary mapping/vector nodes, custom object coordinate sources and physical surface lobes are outside this entry's common-graph row and reject explicitly. This entry does not replace the existing baked or extended-material entries.
Limits: 256 live output nodes, 1024 vec4 parameters (16 KiB), 3601 animation frames, 262144 parameter samples, file limit 256 MiB. Original metadata is cloned, cycles/forward links and shader-injection enums reject. seek(seconds) clamps to the sampled scene range without looping; per-frame samples interpolate linearly. Runtime set overrides remain through seek until reset. Blender frame/subframe and images/mesh counts are restored during export. Coordinate conversion preserves Blender Z-up, UV bottom-left and scene units. Ramp stop positions/colors remain paired and sort live when they cross.
Noise uses Margo's independent hash and gradient field, rather than Blender's private stochastic ordering: the procedural field and animation controls remain live, but exact noise texels are an accepted difference. Per-frame sampling also approximates subframe curves between samples. No speed, bandlimiting or full Blender material equivalence claim. Both are recorded for later quality work rather than hiding the difference.
Live Noise against Cycles (KB5339e, accepted difference, 2026-11-25). Cause: Cycles' lattice hash and gradient order are not in a published description (the Blender manual's Noise Texture page gives the controls only), an integer hash cannot be recovered from samples by curve fitting, and the clean-room rule bars reading Blender's source. What Margo does: the live Noise keeps Blender's controls, animated and evaluated per pixel at any resolution, on Margo's own lattice; for Cycles' exact pattern the add-on's `bake_noise` option (off by default) bakes every material a Noise Texture feeds with Cycles, and on the 32 x 32 fixture (a coloured 3D noise on base colour, a 4D noise inside a node group on roughness, Blender 5.3 Beta, CPU, 4 samples) 0 colour and 0 roughness texels differ from an independent Cycles emission bake (`tools/blender-addon/tests/blender_bake_noise.py`). Trade-off: a baked material is a still image of `bake_size` pixels per side for each mesh that uses it, needs a UV map and texture memory, and loses detail below a texel and all animation (an animated node tree is refused by name); a live one animates and has no texel limit but shows another pattern.
Socket curves (KB5339b, KB5339c): a parameter driven by plain F-curves seeks to Blender's value between frames (Bezier, constant, linear and every easing, Elastic included; constant or linear extrapolation, with linear extrapolation flat from a CONSTANT end key, along the last span from a LINEAR one and along the outer handle from any other, as Blender 5.3 evaluates it, KB-P3d). A colour wired into a float socket becomes its Rec. 709 luminance with the weights a Cycles bake gives (0.2126391, 0.7151691, 0.0721927), within 1e-6 of the bake; Geometry Nodes rounds them to 0.2126, 0.7152, 0.0722, within 1e-4. A vector wired into a float socket becomes the mean of its three components (KB5339h). Elastic matches Blender 5.3 within its single-precision rounding (under 2e-5 of the larger of 1, the value and the decaying swing, on 135 probes); a curve's keys count toward the 262144 samples. An F-curve with a Noise modifier (KB5339d) is sampled in Blender by fcurve.evaluate at an eighth of a frame or finer (finer for short noise octaves, down to 1/1024 frame) and played back as LINEAR keys: at every sampled step the value is Blender's within one float32 step; between steps it is interpolated linearly, measured at most 5.9e-4 off on the KB5339d fixture (frame + k/3 + 1/7 offsets, noise strengths 0.2 to 4). The old frame samples missed the same fixture by up to 0.078 between frames. Margo has no noise model of its own for F-curves. Drivers, other F-curve modifiers, NLA and muted curves interpolate frame samples linearly. Seeks clamp to the scene range.


Batch 207 job 4 size evidence: blender/nodes 0 to 10102 gzip bytes; ceiling 10406 B. These optional bytes keep the validated compiler, controls, animation and shader families together. A split would duplicate validation or add asynchronous graph boundaries. Blender root 4397 B; core plus stage 24209 B, unchanged.

### Immediate debug and arc lines (batch 227 job 3)
@margoengine/lines/debug exports DebugLines, ArcLine and arcPositions. DebugLines drawLine/drawLines/drawArc queue for the next rendered frame and clear on the following rendered frame, including zero delta. ### Splat interchange formats (batch 238)
splats/formats reads KSplat 0.1 compression 0/1/2, multiple sections and capacities, full and partial spatial buckets and SH degrees 0 to 2 (the supported writer's maximum). It promotes mixed section degrees with neutral missing higher bands. SuperSplat compressed binary little-endian PLY supports 256-record chunks, position/scale 11-10-11 words, smallest-three rotations, old full-range or current per-chunk RGB, and uchar SH through degree 3. Count is capped at 3,000,000, PLY header at 64 KiB; malformed schemas, lengths and bucket ranges reject before reading attributes. These are synchronous CPU readers; no worker or reduced peak-memory claim. Standard Gaussian PLY export defaults to binary little-endian and optionally writes ASCII, including normals (zero), every SH coefficient, log scales, wxyz rotations and opacity logits. Exact opacity 0/1 writes limiting IEEE infinity logits. Colour and SH use the existing display/linear first-order mapping; quaternions are normalized and covariances use the existing Float32 floor, matching other Margo readers. GPU rendering uses the existing Splats pipeline unchanged.

Batch 238 formats entry size: absent (0 B) before, 20,239 B min+gzip after. It includes shared Gaussian attribute conversion, covariance eigen decomposition and all three named format operations; separate import paths would add packaging without reducing the full capability. Named exports remain tree-shakable. Core plus stage stays 24,209 B gzip; progressive stays 30,891 B.

### Painted GI and temporal intervals (batch 247 job 2)
`GILighting2D.temporal` defaults true; false recomputes all intervals, and resetHistory() forces the next rebuild. Identical frames retain spatial/angular cascade and finite-bounce surface buffers, and their compute invocations return before tracing. Source and emission RGBA comparisons are exact on GPU. Any alpha, color, emission, source transform, cutoff or gain change invalidates painted intervals. Analytic geometry, emitters, lights (including nested masks), layer, cascade options, view camera and output dimensions are compared on CPU. No old radiance is blended into changed input. A camera move rebuilds rather than reprojecting; ambient is applied at presentation and needs no interval rebuild. Device replacement and changing painted/no-painted mode discard all GI history. One SDFScene2D snapshot per command encoder serves multiple consumers; submit a manually managed frame before starting another. GI borrows the painted scene and textures.
Painted occupied cells have four outward surface slots; internal faces are inactive. Each exposed face gathers 32 cosine-weighted directions per requested bounce from the preceding order, at its midpoint offset .001 source pixels into empty space. Painted RGB clamps to [0,1] for reflectance and multiplies the configured albedo; emission retains HDR. Finite bounce orders 0..4, source resolution, interval reach and angular quadrature limits still apply. GI is now covered by the named opaque visibility, energy, finite-bounce, painted-input and temporal correctness fixtures; no general physical-exactness, converged transport, continuous vector-outline or frame-rate claim is made. Historical README exceptions and no-history language await the README phase.
SDF adds 32 B/pixel exact RGBA history and a 16 B change flag to its previous 48 B/pixel transform storage (80 B/pixel plus 48 B fixed uniforms/flag). Painted GI surface buffers use 192 B/source pixel (two persistent fields and immutable zero order, four vec4 faces each), plus analytic patch geometry and cascade storage. Analytic surface fields use 96 B/patch including zero order, replacing the earlier 64 B/patch. Changed-input comparisons and distance generation still run every frame; presentation traces the near connectors. Reuse avoids surface gathers and upper-cascade interval traces, not every GPU operation.

Batch 247 job 2 sizes: SDF 2,667 to 2,911 B min+gzip, inside its 2,923 B ceiling; GI 9,670 to 10,348 B, ceiling raised 9,961 to 10,659 B under Scott's optional-size ruling. The bytes buy painted diffuse face transport, exact temporal change detection/reuse and owning-scene disposal. ### Batch 231 per-instance colour and custom values
`scatter/attributes` adds `AttributedScatter` over fixed `ScatterInstances` batches. `setColorAt(index,rgb,batch=0)` sets a nonnegative finite linear RGB multiplier; `getColorAt` returns a copy. `setAttributeAt(index,name,components,batch=0)` and `getAttributeAt` use the declared scalar/vector sizes 1..4. Names and declaration order are fixed by `AttributeOptions.attributes`; `attributeIndex(name)` returns its `data.custom` slot. Optional batch `colors` and `attributes` arrays supply initial values; defaults are white and zero. Call setters after attachment; they write 16 bytes per changed value without recreating resources. Live values survive device restoration at unchanged batch counts. Batch indices identify the factory's stable batch order.
`AttributeOptions.shader` defines WGSL `scatterAppearance(position:vec3f,color:vec3f,data:ScatterAttributeData)->ScatterAppearance`. Position is world space before rooted wind. Result fields are position and color; both passes call it, so translation/custom deformation keeps matching shadow geometry. Data has `color:vec4f` and (when declared) `custom:array<vec4f,N>`; scalar/vector tails are zero-padded. Default function returns its position and colour inputs. Geometry normals stay those of the batch; a position modifier does not supply a new normal. Custom data is consumed by this shader path, not merely retained on CPU. Existing vertex colour/occlusion, emission, wind, detail, translucency, roughness and metallic fields retain their bindings.
Attribute storage costs `16*(1+N)*instanceCount` bytes on GPU and the same retained CPU data, per batch, within both device maxBufferSize and maxStorageBufferBindingSize. Entry is 2063 B gzip (ceiling 2319), root scatter 19262 to 19306 B (within existing 19518 ceiling); core plus stage remains 24209 B. No timing claim.

### True MSDF rendering (batch 248 job 3)
`BitmapFont` now retains raw RGBA channels for msdf/mtsdf atlases in `GlyphBitmap.msdf`, while `data` remains the existing scalar median for consumers outside TextRenderer. ## Batch 212 job 3: mixer/fx
FX entry: 3,680 B gzip, budget 3,936 B. New optional JSON chain entry includes chorus, flanger, phaser, tremolo, vibrato, auto-filter, auto-pan, distortion, bitcrusher and authored waveshaping. Root/core/stage unchanged. Each createFX has input/output, named AudioParams, dispose and Symbol.dispose; createFXChain rolls back failures/abort and prefixes parameters by index; createBusFX inserts an owned chain after bus gating, before post sends, independently of native root effects.
Modulation defaults rate 1 Hz (0..20), depth 0.5 (0..1), sine (also triangle/square/sawtooth), initial phase 0 degrees; spread 180 degrees for chorus/tremolo, otherwise 0. Auto-pan is linked stereo. Mix defaults 0.5 for chorus/flanger/phaser, 1 for other effects. Delay centre defaults 0.02/0.003/0.005 s for chorus/flanger/vibrato, range 0..0.1, minimum actual read 1 sample, depth sweeps centre*(1+depth*LFO), linear fractional interpolation. Delay feedback default 0 (-0.95..0.95); no artificial 128-frame minimum. Phaser uses 6 allpass biquads (integer 1..32), frequency 400 Hz (10..0.45*sampleRate), octaves 3 (0..8), q 1 (0.1..40, linear quality factor); auto-filter uses one lowpass with the same exponential sweep. Sweeps clamp at 0.45*sampleRate. This models canonical digital effects, not a particular analog pedal. Wet zero copies input bits, wet one copies processed bits including signed zero.
Bitcrusher defaults bits 4 (integer 1..24), sample/hold reduction 1 (integer 1..128); nearest quantisation, no saturation. Distortion amount 0.4 (0..1) uses (1+k)*x/(1+k*abs(x)), k=100*amount, with 8193 curve samples. Waveshaper accepts 2..65537 finite float32 JSON samples. Native input lookup saturates outside [-1,1]; oversample none (default), 2x or 4x. Colour amount/curve, waveform, spread, phase, stages and channel layout are construction settings; numeric worklet controls and mix are automatable. Worklets support explicit speaker channels 1..32 (default 2); auto-pan requires 2. Requires secure AudioWorklet and blob CSP permission except native colour effects. Caller owns headroom for resonant filters/feedback and chain tails. Tests cover deterministic quantum independence and actual rendered audio on both backends; no speed, other-browser, anti-alias certification or perceptual-equivalence claim.


### Batch 218 GLSL transition import

The optional transitions/glsl entry translates user-authored GLSL ES 1.00 with vec4 transition(vec2 uv) into the custom WGSL contract. translateGLSLTransition is pure; createGLSLTransition and createLiveGLSLTransition validate asynchronously before attaching. progress and ratio are supplied, along with getFromColor/getToColor and the from/to sampler2D aliases. GLSL UVs default to bottom-left; flipY:false preserves top-left coordinates. Additional uniform values are snapshotted as constants from options.uniforms or // = JSON annotations. Vectors, column-major matrices and fixed arrays use flattened component arrays; boolean values or 0/1 are accepted for boolean components. Numbers must fit finite 32-bit values; integer uniforms must fit their signed/unsigned type. Array lengths may be integer literals, const names or constant expressions over them (folded at parse time, 2026-11-11); helper parameters may be unnamed. Since the batch 132 audit (2026-11-15) lengths fold over local constants too, decimal, octal (leading 0) and hexadecimal (0x) integer literals carry their values, a declared name comes into scope after its initializer, a precision statement may stand in a function, matrices negate and take every compound assignment and increment, a scalar constructor takes a vector's or matrix's first component, a sequence may start with a void call, the last operand of `?:` is an assignment expression and only l-values take assignments. Still refused: inverse and array equality in a GLSL ES 1.00 source (neither is in that language; `#version 300 es` sources get both), and a swizzle of a swizzle as an assignment target; each fails with an error, never a wrong image. Since 2026-11-15 a vector built from a matrix (`vec4(mat2)`), a matrix built from mixed vectors and scalars and a constructor whose last argument is partly used lower, spread into scalars in GLSL's order.

Preprocessing supports object/function macros, conditionals, define/undef, `#version 100` and `#version 300 es` (2026-11-15). Expressions use typed precedence parsing, including scalar/vector arithmetic, matrix operations and casts, struct/array access, overloads, swizzles, short-circuit boolean expressions and conditional side effects. Structured if/for/while/do control flow and copy-in/copy-out out/inout parameters are lowered to WGSL. No extra textures or arbitrary binding interface is supplied beyond the two transition images. Other GLSL versions (3.10 and up, desktop GLSL) are refused when declared, with code `unsupported`. This is a transition-function importer, not a complete vertex/fragment program or an external include loader. Source is limited to 65536 UTF-16 units, 32768 tokens, 128 nested statements/expressions, 64 macro expansion rounds and 262144 expanded units; uniform arrays have at most 16384 elements. The custom wrapper also limits emitted WGSL to 65536 units. Compiler diagnostics carry failed and a help link; GPU compilation, cancellation, exact endpoint bypass and shader trust requirements follow the custom entry. Shader execution itself is not bounded by these parser limits.

Native GLSL and WGSL may round floating-point arithmetic differently, especially at exactly-on-texel-boundary nearest samples. Pixel fixtures choose coordinates away from those ambiguous ties and compare with the existing one-byte unorm tolerance. No bit-exact arbitrary GLSL or speed claim is made.

Batch 218 job 3 glsl entry is 15718 B gzip (new entry, before 0 B), with a ceiling of 16190 B. After the batch 132 audit fixes (2026-11-15) it is 16475 B gzip, from 16167 B (+308 B), ceiling 16970 B: the bytes are the GLSL ES 1.00 forms the importer now lowers instead of rejecting. The compiler carries a real parser, preprocessor, typed aggregate/control-flow lowering, diagnostics and both validated factories. Splitting those mutually dependent stages would complicate deterministic diagnostics and lifecycle without improving shader quality. Core + stage stays 24209 B.

The GLSL front end (parser, preprocessor, emitter) moved from `packages/transitions/src` to `packages/shader/src/glsl` behind the `GLSLHost` interface (progress, ratio, from/to samplers, getFromColor/getToColor, the y flip and the entry wrapper stay in transitions), so the shader package can take GLSL input too. Transitions bundles it from source; the transitions/glsl entry measured 16519 B gzip (default zlib, `entry-sizes.mjs` method) after the move, from 16475 B (+44 B for the host object), under its 16837 B ceiling; shader root stays 18664 B and core + stage stays 24837 B. The WGSL emitted for every recorded transition source is byte-identical (`packages/transitions/test/glsl-wgsl-identity.test.js`).

GLSL ES 3.00 input (2026-11-15, The OpenGL ES Shading Language 3.00.6): `uint` and the bit operators and their compound assignments (a shift amount is converted to the unsigned type of the left operand's width, as WGSL needs), `switch` with `case`/`default` labels folded at parse time (constant integer expressions over literals and constants in scope), cases that fall into the next (each WGSL case holds its own statements and those it falls into, up to one that ends in `break`, `return`, `continue` or `discard`; WGSL cases never fall through), `matCxR` types with GLSL's product shapes and `transpose`, `outerProduct`, `matrixCompMult` and the uniform layout for them, `float[3] a` and unsized `float a[] = float[](...)` declarations, array constructors, `.length()`, array equality and arrays as parameters and results, `texture`, `textureProj`, `textureLod`, `textureProjLod`, `textureGrad`, `textureOffset`, `texelFetch` (rows counted from the bottom under the y flip) and `textureSize`, `inverse` (adjugate over the determinant; a singular matrix is undefined in GLSL and gives non-finite values here), `outerProduct`, `trunc`, `round` and `roundEven` (both round half to even, which GLSL allows for `round`), the hyperbolic functions, `isnan` and `isinf` (decided on the IEEE 754 bit pattern, so a compiler cannot fold them away), `modf`, `floatBitsToInt`, `floatBitsToUint`, `intBitsToFloat`, `uintBitsToFloat`, the 2x16 snorm, unorm and half pack functions, boolean `mix`, the `flat`, `smooth`, `centroid` and `invariant` qualifiers and skipped `layout(...)` qualifiers. A signed integer literal keeps its 32-bit pattern (0xFFFFFFFF and 3000000000 are negative), and one beyond 32 bits is refused. The transition images have one level and are read at their nearest texel, so a lookup's level, bias and gradients select nothing there. Not lowered: samplers other than the two images (no binding exists for them in this entry), integer samplers, shadow samplers, `textureGather`-style ES 3.10 functions and uniform blocks. Each of seven original GLSL ES 3.00 fixtures draws the same pixels, within one level per channel, as the browser's own GLSL compiler over 16 x 16 pixels at three progress values, natively and on the WebGL2 layer (`packages/transitions/test/glsl-es3-fixtures.js`). One fixture's reference takes a `continue` out of its `switch`: ANGLE's Direct3D 11 back end (Chrome 157, RTX A6000) cannot compile a `continue` inside a `switch` and loses the context, so the translated fixture keeps it and the layer avoids it (KB-SW1, below). The transitions/glsl entry measured 19,498 B gzip after this, from 16,519 B (+2,979 B); its ceiling rises from 16,837 to 20,083 B. The bytes are the GLSL ES 3.00 language the shared front end now reads; it is one front end for transitions and shader, and a lazy split of the ES 3.00 parts would need a second fetch on the first translation of any source that uses them. Core + stage is unchanged.

KB-SW1 (fixed 2026-11-15): a WGSL `continue` inside a `switch` inside a loop reached ANGLE's Direct3D 11 back end as a GLSL `continue` inside a `switch`, which it fails to compile ("Error compiling dynamic pixel executable", then a lost context). The WebGL2 layer's GLSL now sets a flag and breaks out of the switch, and the loop continues after it; a nested switch hands the flag outwards. Regression: `packages/webgl2-compat/test/glsl.test.js` ("a continue inside a switch leaves the switch by a flag").

Batch 244 job 3: CRT adds `colorBleed` [0,1], default 0, and `chromaticOffset`, `redOffset`, `greenOffset`, `blueOffset`, each a horizontal number or [x,y] source-pixel tuple in [-32,32], default 0. Symmetric offset adds to red and subtracts from blue; independent offsets add on top. Positive offsets select texels to the right/below, so those channel images move left/up. Effective combined offsets may reach 64 source pixels. Color bleed retains source luma and alpha, filters I with normalized 5-tap and Q with 9-tap horizontal binomials, then clips to the premultiplied gamut. Offsets use bilinear sampling with edge-repeat borders; alpha is the maximum selected channel alpha. Tube beam/mask/brightness modulate the processed color; glow still adds the unshifted raw-source 3x3 halo. Both effects default off and preserve all previous CRT pixels, including exact boundaries. This is a selectable composite-video look, not RF encoding, dot crawl, interlacing or a calibrated TV standard. No extra pass or intermediate image; no timing claim.
