### Streamed SOG (batch 238 job 3)
splats/lod-sog accepts v1 and unversioned pre-release lod-meta.json, null/omitted environments, sparse leaf levels, optional errors and relative arbitrary chunk paths. Each chunk is unbundled SOG v2/v3 with 1 to 3,000,000 records. All small metadata is fetched up front with concurrency 8 to validate runs/counts and choose a uniform SH degree; textures remain lazy. Spatial depth limit 128. Complete non-overlapping single-level chunk runs and supplied totals must agree. A referenced chunk is decoded whole, then its range is copied. cacheChunks defaults 2 (0 disables completed caching), plus active loads and the existing SplatLod node cache. Independent caller aborts share requests; disposal aborts all loads. A manifest `model` other than `antialiased` (such as `2dgs`) is refused with code `unsupported` before any chunk is fetched (2026-11-11).
SplatLod structural nodes have count 0 and refine unconditionally; the renderer never calls their load. Minimum coarse coverage must fit the fixed-slot budget, otherwise construction rejects with the required budget. Slot-count and splat-count limits both constrain refinement. Errors are used only with lodErrors true; otherwise radius * cbrt(max(0,1-count/finestCount)) estimates omitted detail. Environment stays selected regardless of camera distance. No transition blending or new training algorithm.
SOG v3 preserves exponential-map rotations, squared opacity through 1.5625, 24-bit labels and SH degree 4 (25 RGB coefficients including DC). Unused blind attributes are ignored as permitted by the format. Images use the existing lossless WebP decoder. Extended opacity is retained until the existing fragment alpha cap min(0.99, opacity*Gaussian), preserving extra off-center coverage. Colours retain the existing first-order display/linear SH conversion. encodeSog chooses v3 for extended opacity or degree 4, otherwise v2. SPZ v3, .splat and Gaussian PLY reject opacity above 1 rather than wrapping/clipping; SPZ v3 rejects degree 4. Standard PLY now carries degree 4.

Batch 238 job 3 minified gzip: lod-sog new 0 to 20,369 B (ceiling 20,981 B). Shared degree-4/v3 support takes data to 22,273 B (prior ceiling 22,135 B, raised to 22,942 B) and animate to 20,381 B (prior ceiling 20,263 B, raised to 20,993 B). The bytes retain a single validated data representation and codec instead of splitting degree/opacity formats. Root splats 32,073 B; lod 30,582 B; progressive 31,464 B; formats 20,705 B. Core plus stage remains 24,209 B.

## Lightmaps drawn at draw time (batch 54)

`@margoengine/lightmap/apply` adds the bake as indirect light (diffuse reflectance times occlusion times the bake),
the way `Material.lightMap` does; it does not turn off live lights the bake already holds. A glTF PBR material record
that already has a material extension (clearcoat, a custom one) is refused, since a record holds one extension. A core
mesh needs its lightmap UVs passed (`uv1`), is drawn by a materials stand-in in the engine's default scene, and its
stand-in copies colour, roughness, metalness and sidedness only (no core textures). A live GPU baker must share the
model's GPU device. WebGPU only for glTF PBR models. After a device restore a CPU bake on a glTF PBR model draws the
same light from the new device (uploaded again from its pixels, 2026-11-15, KB-OWN-LIGHTMAP1); a live GPU baker
lives on its device and goes with it, so the model draws no baked light until a new baker made on `engine.gpu` is
applied. That fix took `lightmap/apply` from 2,476 B to 2,442 B min+gzip (ceiling 2,634 B unchanged).

## Batch 196 non-XR stereo

Optional cameras/stereo is 3,144 B min+gzip (previously 0 B), ceiling 3,400 B. StereoOutput.render replaces the application's engine.render call in its frame loop; it uses two scene draws and one fullscreen packing pass, with one plugin update per pair. Default mode side-by-side, eye separation 0.064 world units, convergence at the camera target, source engine.camera, source camera layers, default scene, unswapped eyes, column stripes and phase 0. Infinity focus gives parallel frusta. StereoRig also preserves custom projection hooks; orthographic eyes correctly have no depth disparity. The packed output is display colour (RGBA8 eye textures); anaglyph is the published red/cyan Dubois transform in linear light. Two RGBA8 eye targets use 8 * eyeWidth * eyeHeight bytes, plus core's normal render attachments. Rows/columns refer to physical backing pixels; a physical barrier needs calibrated optics and pixel-aligned presentation. On automatic canvas resize the projection follows the new aspect immediately and eye resolution catches up on the next frame; exactSize canvases give caller-controlled physical dimensions. No XR session or automatic engine.start takeover. Dispose the output before its engine. Native WebGPU and WebGL2 compatibility work; native WebGL-only engines reject.

### Curved text (batch 248 job 4)
`@margoengine/text/curve` provides CurvedText, curvePoint and PathText. CurvedText extends Text, wrapping the entire local X/Y block around local Y at signed curveRadius (default 1; Infinity is flat). Default curveSegments is 8 horizontal subdivisions per glyph, integer 1..256. The analytic cylinder uses [r*sin(x/r), y, 2*r*sin(x/(2*r))^2]; glyph UVs and outline/shadow layers interpolate over the subdivided surface in one block draw. Anchors, lines, shaping, font styles and transform/mesh placement are preserved. Layout/caret/selection coordinates remain in the unwrapped plane; hitTestSurface maps a cylinder-local surface point back to that plane. That inverse is principal-angle only, so blocks winding more than one revolution need an application-supplied winding choice.
PathText accepts a TextPath with positive finite length and sample(distance) returning position/tangent/normal in local world units. startOffset defaults to 0; closed defaults false (out-of-range glyph midpoints hide), true wraps distances. Glyphs align rigidly to normalized orthogonal path frames as in SVG textPath align; whole shaped runs remain joined. Line baselines offset along the frame normal. Global transform and mesh attachment apply after path placement. Each visible nonspace shaped item is one Text draw. Call update after editing owned options, font state or path; addTo/removeFrom and dispose manage renderer membership, including rebuilds. Billboard is refused for PathText because the path owns glyph orientation; CurvedText supports a billboard cylinder. Arbitrary paths are supplied via the public frame interface, not parsed from SVG strings. No core or stage additions.
Batch 248 job 4 measured entries: /curve 10,487 B gzip (new), text root 16,701 to 16,860 B within its existing ceiling. The shared rendering avoids another renderer; core plus stage remains 24,209 B.
Extended dynamics entry: 2,856 B gzip, budget 3,112 B.

## Batch 212 job 4: mixer/dynamics
Extended dynamics entry: 2,856 B gzip, budget 3,112 B. New optional gate/expander/three-band compressor with explicit linked speaker channels 1..32 (default 2), fixed construction options, AudioWorklet/CSP/AbortSignal/owned bus lifecycle as the existing worklet entry. No lookahead (latencyFrames 0), automatic makeup, clipping or true-peak limiting. Crossover phase is inherent; flat magnitude does not mean sample-identical input. Use existing worklet limiting after this stage for peak safety.
Gate defaults threshold -40 dBFS (-120..0), hysteresis 3 dB (0..40), hold 0.05 s (0..10), floor -Infinity (silence, or -120..0 dB), attack 0.001 s and release 0.1 s (0..10). Peak >= threshold opens; while open, peak >= threshold-hysteresis resets hold. Exactly holdFrames below-closing-threshold samples remain open, then closing begins. Expander defaults threshold -40, ratio 2, knee 6 dB, range 80 dB (0..120), makeup 0; below-threshold slope ratio and a quadratic knee join continuously to unity. Band defaults threshold -24, knee 6 (0..40), ratio 4 (1..100), attack 0.003, release 0.1 (0..10), makeup 0 (-24..24). Attack/release are one-pole gain time constants: compressor attenuation/recovery, gate/expander opening/closing; zero jumps. Pure expanderCurve returns output dB and handles silent -Infinity.
Multiband crossovers default [250,2500] Hz, ordered 10..0.45*sampleRate; separate low/mid/high BandDynamics. Each split is two cascaded Butterworth biquads per low/high path (24 dB/octave). Low-band high-crossover phase compensation keeps the unity sum flat. Per-band detector is linked maximum absolute sample. Ratios 1 and makeup 0 retain the crossover's allpass response. Tests prove independent RBJ convolution, closed-form knees/gains and flat impulse-response magnitude across the spectrum; real renders beside both backends. Headroom, perceptual tuning, other browsers and performance remain unmeasured. No core/stage change.
## Batch 173: optional transfer classification
`@margoengine/sciviz/transfer` adds joint value/gradient histograms, rectangle, triangle and Gaussian classifiers, 1D ordered preintegration, CT/MRI/PET display presets and an owned HTML editor. LUT resolution is 2..2048 per axis; default 256 for widgets, 128 for preintegration. Colours are linear light, opacity per reference voxel. Points and widget coordinates use physical scalar units and scalar units/data unit for gradients. Histograms require 2+ samples per axis, at most 64 million samples, x fastest; NaN/nonfinite centres or derivative neighbours are excluded. Histograms own two float64 scratch arrays (16 bytes/sample) and a 4-byte count per bin. Scalar values/gradients outside the selected histogram axes clamp to the edge bins.
Volume textures retain signed normalized scalar values outside the display range so their gradients remain meaningful; binary16 limits normalized values to [-65504,65504] and rounds them. Histogram derivatives use original CPU values; render derivatives use the half-float, trilinearly sampled field. Native WebGPU and WebGL2 compatibility are supported. Bricked volumes and extracted isosurfaces do not consume this scalar VolumeLayer API. The editor can bind any existing scalar VolumeLayer without recreating its data; function points are resampled into the layer's existing range. Slice colours update with the same classifier. Slice opacity remains its independently specified opacity.
Preintegration uses 8..2048 midpoint samples (default 128), linear scalar variation over an ordered front/back segment and RGBA8 output. Generate for the layer's `step=1/quality` and density. Regenerate after changing quality/density for the most accurate colour integral. The marcher corrects opacity when step/density differ, but unpremultiplied integrated colour remains an approximation in that case, at clipped segment endpoints and in the existing 2048-sample cap. Gradient classification is evaluated at march samples, not preintegrated in 2D. MIP is scalar-maximum projection, not a 2D classification maximum.
The HTML component has no import side effects, supports add/select/delete, pointer/key translation, colour/opacity, rectangle extents, Gaussian sigma and explicit triangle vertices. Disposing the editor removes DOM/listeners and restores the layer's original classifier. Preintegration and histograms accept AbortSignal and yield during work. No timing or superiority claim. Transfer entry: 5996 bytes min+gzip (new entry, formerly 0; ceiling 6252). Sciviz root: measured parent 50597 to 52045 bytes; its optional ceiling rises from 51813 to 53607 for physical classifier hooks and safe owned-buffer PNG capture. Core + stage: unchanged 24209 bytes. The combined editor, histogram and classification contract stays together; splitting would add import/ownership complexity without reducing full-feature bytes.



### Batch 243 traced glTF extension lobes
mesh-pbr now carries clearcoat, sheen, iridescence and specular factors and all specified extension textures from loaded glTF snapshots. Clearcoat has independent roughness and tangent-space normal state, and attenuates underlying emission. Sheen uses Charlie, clamped Neubelt visibility and the existing Margo directional-albedo fit. Specular color is linear/sRGB-decoded, clamped after multiplying dielectric F0, while strength scales dielectric F0 and F90; metals retain their own Fresnel. Iridescence uses the shared two-order Fourier thin-film model and the green thickness channel, or maximum thickness without a map. Factors default to the Khronos values. Thin-film IOR is bounded to [1,10], thickness to [0,1e8] nm with minimum at most maximum; color factors allow up to 1e8 for specular and [0,1] for sheen. The existing source-definition snapshot and base-mip texture limits continue to apply. Clearcoat normal maps use the same derived/provided tangent frame logic as base normals.

One true geometry ULP beyond either boundary still rejects. The extra cache-disabled compatibility compile defect remains in known-bugs.md; no cold-cache guarantee or speed claim is made.


## Lens drops (batch 236 job 3)
Optional weather/lens is 3,601 B min+gzip, new from 0 B, ceiling 3,815 B. Core plus stage remains 24,209 B. LensDrops joins PostStack as an HDR stage, including WebGL2 compatibility at the half-float tier. Defaults: wetness 0.6, radius 0.025 image heights (0.002..0.06), speed 0.08 heights/s (0..1), distortion 0.7 (0..2), streaks 0.65 (0..1), seed 1 (integer 0..16777215), enabled true, time accumulated from frame deltas; an explicit time supports 0..1000000 s. An optional weather.wetness overrides wetness. The field considers 18 nearby cells per pixel, in stationary and moving layers. ## Batch 212 job 5: mixer/pitch
Pitch entry: 2,366 B gzip, budget 2,622 B. New optional time-domain transposer emits exactly one frame per input frame, with linked read-head phase for explicit speaker channels 1..32 (default 2). Defaults: pitch 0 semitones (-48..48, fractional), windowSize 0.1 s (0.005..1, fixed at construction), delayTime 0 s (0..1), feedback 0 (-0.95..0.95), mix 1 (0..1), antiAlias true (boolean). Pitch/mix/feedback/delayTime are native audio-rate controls; setPitch validates schedule atomically and defaults to immediate, or an exponential fade settling about 98% over seconds. Zero wet and default unison preserve bits, including initial samples. Unison with configured delay/feedback reads a fixed delay, minimum 1 sample for feedback.
Two half-cycle-offset read heads use complementary Hann weights and linear interpolation. Nonzero-pitch wet delay spans additional delay plus 1..windowFrames+1 samples; there is no single fixed latency. Source event times/duration stay on the same clock, with that bounded wet tail; keep feeding zeros to flush it. Memory per channel is ceil(sampleRate+windowFrames)+4 float64 samples plus filter state, allocated once. No per-sample allocation, FFT, offline resampling or timer. Upward antiAlias filtering is two Butterworth biquads at 0.45*sampleRate/ratio before the delay; aliases can remain and high frequencies are attenuated. Linear interpolation also rolls off high frequencies. No formant preservation, transient protection, speech-quality, polyphonic transparency or alias-free claim; this is the requested delay-line effect class and can have window coloration. Feedback is a creative transposed delay, not pitch-preserving echo. Requires secure AudioWorklet and blob CSP permission. Abort/disposal and bus-owned inserts follow the other optional worklets. No core/stage change; tested in Edge beside both backends, other browsers/listening/performance unmeasured.


### Voxel image and text generation (batch 241 job 1)
`@margoengine/voxel-edit/generate` provides `heightmapToVoxels` and `textToVoxels`. Grey8/RGBA8 row-major images produce Y columns: nearest whole-cell height, black zero, white `height` (default 32), X image columns and Z image rows. RGBA defaults to encoded BT.709 luma, with explicit red/green/blue/alpha and inversion options. RGBA alpha at or below `alphaThreshold` (default 0) is air; grey images have no alpha, so the threshold does not apply to them. `textToVoxels` crops to the ink of the lines that have ink, so a glyph's side bearing leaves no empty columns. Source RGBA is retained, with the existing deterministic reduction above 255 colours.
Text takes a required CSS `font`, default depth 1, coverage threshold 127 and opaque white colour. Native canvas shaping preserves Unicode, kerning, ligatures and holes; callers load custom fonts first. Multiline default spacing is 1.2 times measured Mg ink height. Negative bearings and descenders are included; Y is up, extrusion is positive Z. Empty text is empty storage with positive dimensions. An optional supplied context is resized and cleared; otherwise Canvas is created at call time. Fonts and platform rasterizers can differ, so font masks are not cross-platform bit-identical. There are no import-time DOM accesses. Both APIs take AbortSignal and the standard 16,777,216-cell default / 67,108,864-cell maximum budget, checked before grid allocation. Text needs a native 2D canvas; Node hosts can supply one. No new rendering backend or core code.
Entry size: /generate is new (0 to 2,479 B min+gzip, recorded ceiling 2,735 B). The bytes cover image validation, palette generation, native text bounds and extrusion together; splitting would duplicate their shared grid and validation code. Core and stage are unchanged.

### Batch 214: chain avoidance
The optional kinematics-constraints/chain entry supports CCD and FABRIK on 1..256 positive-length links, 1..256 candidate poses (default 32), and 1..1024 sweeps per candidate (default 64). The first candidate keeps the reached pose; candidate k is turned about the root to target line to that pose's swivel plus 2 pi k / candidates, so the swivel angles tried are evenly spaced and the widest gap left is 2 pi / candidates. Radius defaults to zero, required gap to zero and positional tolerance to 1e-5. The query protocol accepts capsule, convex hull, mesh and SDF obstacles. Every accepted capsule link preserves its length and target tolerance. Results certify a static pose only: use /swept for paths. Bounded local failure is not infeasibility; self collision requires caller-supplied pose acceptance. Full-body limb avoidance searches preserve the root and end and roll the entire body back when any callback rejects. Rollback restores the frame input, which is not itself certified against moving obstacles. No physics solver, rigging, core or stage change.

Batch 214 job 1 entry gzip: chain 0 (absent) to 1,904 B; animator/fbik 5,434 to 5,728 B. Optional ceilings raised in sizes.json for the new entry and atomic body rollback, which cannot be split out of the pose commit without losing atomicity. Core plus stage remains 24,209 B, under 25,000 B.

### Per-splat GPU modifiers (batch 238 job 4)
splats/modify supplies SplatModifier.create(cloud, options), attach(engine,cloud,options) and splatModifierShaders. Creation asynchronously snapshots current cloud data; signal abort rejects creation and later disposes the modifier. Already submitted readback work completes normally. One active modifier per cloud; combine hook logic into its WGSL bodies. Hooks position/opacity/color default to identity; declarations defaults empty; up to 64 parameter floats default zero, exposed as u.parameters[0..15] vec4f values. Each body has index, time and delta; position takes canonical position and returns vec3f; opacity takes the modified position and canonical opacity and returns f32; color takes modified position and evaluated linear RGB and returns vec3f.
time defaults 0, playing true, speed 1, enabled true. Clock advances once in the first view; seek with playing false. Geometry runs at -7.25 before projection/sorting, colour at -6.95 after SH/fog and before relighting. All SH degrees are evaluated at the modified centre. Covariances and SH remain the source's; this position-only warp does not deform ellipsoid axes. Geometry/opacity is written to the cloud inputs, including alpha readback, so existing geometric consumers see it. Colour changes are transient evaluated output. Opacity is clamped to 0..1.5625, colour to nonnegative HDR values. Shader/compiler errors remain visible through normal WebGPU validation.
Canonical position/opacity costs 16 bytes per splat on CPU plus 16 bytes per splat on GPU and a 288-byte uniform. Per frame: two compute passes, no canonical geometry readback. Ordinary source edits to centres/opacity must also call setRest with a full same-count SplatData; source RGB/SH/covariance edits flow normally. Disabling and disposal restore canonical centres/opacity; a fresh projection restores colour. Device restoration uploads the CPU canonical snapshot and retains clock/parameters. Composition with another position-writing animation needs an explicit canonical update; the plugin never silently stacks multiple owners.

Batch 238 job 4 minified gzip: modify new 0 to 20174 B, ceiling 20780 B. It retains canonical state, asynchronous snapshot/cancellation, typed WGSL hooks and both compute passes in one optional entry; splitting would add lifetime/ownership coordination without reducing a user's imported effect. The existing entries retain their job 3 sizes, including lod-sog 20,369 B; core plus stage remains 24209 B.

### Screen-space voxel selections (batch 241 job 2)

### Shaped and variable-font extrusion (batch 248 job 5)
`text/extrude` accepts `shapedRuns`, ordered visual glyph IDs with xAdvance/yAdvance/xOffset/yOffset in em units, optional UTF-16 cluster and zero-based line. It respects ligatures, reordered RTL runs, mark offsets, vertical advances and multiple runs per line without remapping IDs through cmap. Letter spacing applies between distinct supplied clusters; omitted clusters space each glyph. A FontLike.shape(text) provider is called once when runs are absent; without either input, the existing Unicode cmap path remains. This is a shaping-result interface, with no built-in script shaper or network dependency. Normalize shaper positions by its font scale and use the same font instance and axes as the run.
`parseFontOutlines(bytes,{variations})`, FontOutlines.withVariations(values) and extrudeText's variations option select instances; omitted axes use fvar defaults, out-of-range values clamp, unknown/nonfinite axes fail with a linked coded error. variationAxes exposes tags/min/default/max. TrueType supports gvar shared/private/intermediate tuples, sparse contour interpolation, composite offsets and phantom widths when HVAR is absent. HVAR supports index maps and short/long delta rows, including null subtables. avar version 1 piecewise remapping is supported; later avar versions reject explicitly. CFF2 supports 32-bit INDEX counts, FontDICT/FDSelect formats 0/3/4, local/global subroutines, private and charstring blend/vsindex, implicit program termination and a 513-value stack. Existing 96-hint, 10-subroutine, 100,000-token and 16,384-flattened-vertex budgets remain; malformed ranges/counts reject. CFF1 and static TrueType behavior remain covered by the existing tests. Glyphs remain unhinted; font-wide MVAR/VVAR metrics are not consumed because block line height and supplied vertical advances own placement here. Parsed instances currently reparse their source bytes; no timing claim.
The existing optional extrude entry grows from 10,834 to 14,894 B gzip; its ceiling is raised in the same commit. Those bytes add the complete font-instance and positioned-run path in one parser; a split would duplicate sfnt state or add an asynchronous stateful bridge to the synchronous extrusion API. Core/stage and the text root are unchanged by this job, at 24,209 B combined and 16,860 B root respectively.

Variable font axes (KB5472d, fixed 2026-11-11): `text/extrude` and the text outline path normalize each axis as the OpenType "Coordinate scales and normalization" section specifies (Microsoft, OpenType 1.9.1 Font Variations Overview and the avar chapter, https://learn.microsoft.com/typography/opentype/spec/otvaroverview): the user value as 16.16 Fixed, the default normalization in 16.16, the avar segment map in 16.16, then the final F2Dot14 step `(v + 2) >> 2`. wght 350 on a 200 to 900 axis gives 0.21429443359375 before avar, not the floating 0.2142857. The outline oracle (packages/text/tests/generate-variable-reference.py) draws FontTools at that spec coordinate; FontTools' own floating normalization differs at every rounded weight and is kept beside it as `floatingAdvance`. Outlines stay unhinted.

## Batch 173: labels and registered multi-component volumes
Optional `@margoengine/sciviz/labels` adds `fusionVolume`, `FusionLayer` and `labelLegend`. One drawable, one fullscreen triangle and one march combine 1..4 sources; each source is categories, RGB, RGBA or 1..4 independent scalar components. Components are interleaved, x fastest. Arrays and transfer results are snapshotted. Each source retains its own dimensions and invertible affine unit-box-to-data mapping, with no registration resampling. Bounds default to [0,nx-1,0,ny-1,0,nz-1]; transform replaces bounds. Dimension and category counts obey the device's 3D/2D texture limits (palette needs one extra transparent slot). Each dimension is at least two.
Category IDs are exact unsigned 32-bit integers, including zero and 4294967295; never interpolate them. Unlisted IDs are transparent but retain distinct boundaries. Each listed category has linear-light RGBA and an optional separate outline RGBA and integer framebuffer-pixel width 1..16 (default 1). Eight nearest-category neighbours per radius detect label-to-label and external boundaries at each ray sample. This is a projected neighbourhood outline, not a smoothed subvoxel segmentation or mesh. `setLabels` atomically validates and snapshots replacements; `labelLegend.update()` refreshes accessible HTML text after edits.
RGB/RGBA channels are linear light, default divisor 255 for byte arrays and 1 otherwise; alpha shares that divisor. RGB opacity defaults to 0.1; RGBA uses its alpha. Colour and intensity sampling is trilinear; component functions are evaluated at 256 physical scalar values into binary16 RGBA tables, and source scalar components are normalized/clamped to their declared range in binary16. No gradient or preintegrated component functions in this entry. Component and source weight default 1; zero hides them. `TransferFunction.evaluate` can supply a 1D function directly; update a snapshotted function by rebuilding the layer.
Default optical mixing sums extinction and weights colours by optical depth; over gives earlier sources/components priority at each sample; maximum selects the largest corrected opacity (earlier wins ties). All three mix before front-to-back ray compositing, never as separately sorted volume draws. Quality defaults to 1.5 samples per projected voxel; density defaults to 1. Step opacity uses distance through each source's voxel coordinates. Each ray caps at 2048 midpoint segments and terminates at alpha >0.9999. Small features thinner than a step can be missed; increase quality within the cap. No native WebGL2 fallback driver; WebGPU and WebGL2 compatibility are supported. Internal opaque-geometry termination is the separate volume-quality job, not supplied here.
Entry min+gzip: 6292 B (new, formerly 0), ceiling 6548 B. Sciviz root remains 52045 B and core+stage remains 24209 B. Palette ownership, transforms, component mixing and the one march remain together; splitting would fragment the same source lifecycle without removing full-feature bytes. The MSD demo reduction is 60x60x39, gzip 180024 B intensities and 661 B labels; see its source record for exact output sizes/hashes. Data are demo-only CC BY-SA 4.0, separate from engine source. OpenNeuro RGBA uses the existing CC0 T1.


Batch 203 JPEG entries: decoders/jpeg is a new optional 3,774 B minified gzip entry (previously absent); exporters/jpeg-read remains 3,774 B through the shared implementation. Its size baseline adds 256 B headroom. Core plus stage is unchanged at 24,209 B. No new dependency, Wasm asset or CPU loop was added.

### Batch 240 job 2: object blocks

Optional voxel/objects provides VoxelObjects(engine,world). Its define(name,source,options?) snapshots a core Mesh or the root/meshes graph of a core glTF Model. Nodes copy local TRS, names and receiveShadow, while Geometry and PbrMaterial identities stay shared. Source meshes remain caller owned and can be disposed after definition. Object geometry is centred on x/z cell centres, with the cell floor at y=0; objectState(id,turns) supports 0..3 positive Y quarter turns. Storage defaults are solid=false, opacity=0 and light=0; optional solid=true uses existing whole-cell voxel collision, not arbitrary mesh collision. Material appearance belongs to source meshes.

Call update before render. World edits reconcile only touched chunks, retaining unchanged cell handles; chunk unload/disposal releases placements and subscriptions. at(x,y,z) exposes root-first handles, and stats counts chunks/cells/mesh nodes. Core performs instanced geometry batches and per-placement frustum culling, so objects crossing chunk bounds retain correct bounds. The packed voxel mesher does not draw object cube faces. Loaded-world and engine node capacity bound memory; each placement has a transform root plus its source graph nodes, so define refuses a source graph 64 or more meshes deep (the root adds one parent and core allows 63). A placement that throws part way through a chunk leaves the placements made before it owned by the chunk (dispose releases them) and the chunk pending, so the next update finishes it. Static core glTF materials are supported; animated/skinned PBRModel graphs belong to their existing packages and are not silently converted into core meshes. No new core or stage code, new Wasm kernel or wall-clock claim.
Batch 240 job 2 optional entry gzip: objects 0 to 1,678 B, ceiling 1,934 B. Core plus stage remains 24,209 B. Existing geometry batching avoids a second instance-buffer implementation; no optional ceiling for an existing entry is raised.

### Voxel-net recording and replay (batch 242 job 2)
Optional /replay records the exact per-recipient outbound message stream using server.onSend, including welcome and spawn; attach before clients join. Default queued bytes 64 MiB, hard per-message bound 16 MiB. Overflow and I/O errors stop recording and reject flush/close. MVR1 carries protocol version 6, tick rate, recipient id, tick and raw payload; a complete-file footer is mandatory. readVoxelRecording has a default 256 MiB file limit, configurable; playback holds validated records in memory. Files include names, application messages and resume tokens and belong with private bug reports. Select one recipient and use a fresh VoxelNetClient/world with no-op send; advanceTo is forward-only, play defaults to speed 1 and a 1-hour hard bound with AbortSignal. Playback completion means packets delivered to receive; chunk decompression completes asynchronously through the normal client. Seeking backward requires a fresh client/world. This reconstructs server-visible states, not unsent predicted local inputs or deterministic server execution. No GPU work.

Voxel-net /replay entry: 0 -> 3584 B min+gzip, ceiling 3840 B. Server is 18031 B and rooms 19424 B, within existing ceilings. Core + stage unchanged at 24,209 B.

# Batch 185 job 2: volume and array storage

`@margoengine/shader/compute-volume` adds `storageVolume(width, height, depth, options)` and `ComputeVolume`. ### VFX lifetime dynamics (batch 270 job 2)

## Batch 203 standalone compression
Zstandard is an optional entry over the existing clean-room decoder: concatenated and skippable frames, checksums, a caller destination, default 256 MiB output and 128 MiB declared window. External Zstandard dictionaries remain unsupported with a coded error. LZ4 decodes standard and legacy concatenated frames, metadata, linked/independent blocks and raw blocks with an explicit decoded size. All descriptor/block/content checksums are verified. It accepts an external dictionary (last 65,536 bytes) and optional dictionaryId, rejects a missing required dictionary, caps total output at 256 MiB by default (configurable integer 0..2147483647), and yields after 8 MiB or 128 blocks for cancellation. Each call receives its complete compressed byte stream and returns all output bytes; no incremental transport API is claimed. Decoded blocks, frame assembly and final assembly may coexist, plus up to one 8 MiB legacy block and its dictionary; maxOutputSize bounds decoded bytes, not peak process memory. No timing claim.

## Batch 173 job 3: sciviz/cinematic
`cinematicVolume(figure, volume, options)` wraps an existing composite VolumeLayer, shares its scalar and classifier textures, hides the base drawable and restores its previous visibility on disposal. No core or stage imports of cinematic lighting are added. Ordinary slices remain available. Gradient and preintegrated classifiers are accepted; preintegration is treated as local diagonal extinction for secondary paths, not a claim of exact nonlocal preintegrated transport. Source gradient surface shading is replaced by scattering lighting.
All three expensive modes default off. Ambient radius defaults to 8 smallest scene voxels, 8 directions (1..64) and 8 integration steps (1..256). Shadows default to 32 steps (1..2048), toward [0.4,0.6,1]. Ambient radiance defaults [0.3,0.3,0.3], directional irradiance [8.8,8.8,8.8], scattered by the Henyey-Greenstein phase normalised over the sphere in both the march and the path tracer (an isotropic scatterer returns light / (4 pi)). Path tracing defaults g=0 (-1<g<1), 8 bounces (1..32), albedo 0.9 ([0,1]), seed 1 (uint32), 4096 accumulated samples (1..16777216). Paths converge to the chosen finite-bounce, piecewise-constant integration model, not an unbounded-bounce exact solution. Local AO applies to the deterministic march; path tracing computes ambient visibility by physical path escape instead. Each segment uses the classifier's per-voxel alpha as extinction, scaled by density and the smallest scene voxel. Both ray direction and light distance use scene metric, preserving nonuniform volume transforms. The primary/each scattering march caps at 2048 segments and widens the step to cover the box; shadow/local integral resolutions are explicit quality controls.
Accumulation uses two RGBA32float images plus an RGBA32uint work image (48 bytes per viewport pixel), one integration pass then a display triangle. Counters are always available, so even the unlit wrapper pays those passes and writes compared with ordinary VolumeLayer. `cost({signal})` reads exact last-frame scalar fetches, shadow rays, ambient rays and collisions, with a 30-second mapping deadline. Camera matrix, transform, density, quality, clips, classifier/source replacement and resize reset accumulation. Call reset() after externally updating an existing GPU source texture. configure() validates atomically, snapshots inputs and resets. Sources rebuild through VolumeLayer after device replacement; lighting clears its own history. Native WebGPU and WebGL2 compatibility are tested; native GL fallback is unsupported and fails before allocation.
Scene-depth termination is owned by batch 173 job 4; this entry currently has the same opaque-interior limitation as the ordinary volume path. Multiple translucent drawables sort as whole layers, not interleaved samples. The EMD-8117 demo contains 64^3 original density samples, reduced from 192^3 at stride 3, without intensity scaling. This is an educational view, not medical evidence.

Batch 173 job 3 measured entry sizes: cinematic 6006 B min+gzip (new entry, previous 0 B), ceiling 6262 B. One resource/accumulation owner avoids duplicate transport state across split entries. sciviz root remains 52045 B; combined core + stage remains 24209 B.

### Voxel-net native server hosts (batch 242 job 4)
Optional /server-runtimes provides serveVoxelBun and serveVoxelDeno, one owned native listener plus a normal VoxelServer, default loopback and free port. Factories reject unsupported runtimes with a coded error. Async disposal and AbortSignal close clients, worker threads and listener. Native socket APIs handle WebSocket framing; pending totals/per-address reservations, own-host origin defaults, authentication, 4096-byte input bounds, binary-only messages and all simulation/codec rules remain in voxel-net. Authentication receives method, URL, headers, rawHeaders and socket.remoteAddress through a Node IncomingMessage facade; it is not a readable native request-body stream. Bun cork/getBufferedAmount/ping/pong integrate with tick writes, slow clients and heartbeat counters; Deno uses WebSocket.bufferedAmount and ordinary message activity. Native buffers contribute to the server's existing queue bound. Deno idle native pongs are not observable by the adapter, so an idle client must keep calling update to send inputs or may be closed by clientTimeout even when reachable. Native TLS delegates to Bun or Deno; Deno requires PEM string key/cert rather than Buffer values. Runtime permissions and executable installation are application-owned. Local shared contract passed on Bun 1.4.4 and Deno 2.9.8 on Windows. No GPU or speed result. Deno answers WebSocket pings inside the runtime and shows no pong, so a Deno connection reports `livenessByRuntime`: Deno pings after floor(clientTimeout / 2000) idle seconds (at least 1) and closes a client that does not answer within as many again, and the server's byte-silence close does not apply to it (KB5545a, 2026-11-11). VoxelLobby room URLs: a used shard ticket, even past its reservation life, is let on again only while its seat's player is in the room (playing or parked), and only for a hello that resumes; a plain join on a used URL is refused with 1008 (KB5499a, 2026-11-11). `authenticate` now gets `resume: true` on such a hello.

## Batch 214 job 3: multi-goal IK
The optional @margoengine/kinematics-constraints/multi-goal entry accepts 1..256 joints and at most 256 combined goals and loop closures. Fixed, revolute and prismatic scalar joints compose into spherical and floating joints; rest/attachment quaternions use x,y,z,w and normalize nonzero inputs. Joint parents may be unordered but must form a forest; explicit attachment-frame closures join branches, trees or world anchors. World position and rotation-vector channel masks and nonnegative objective weights are supported. Hard scalar bounds apply to every returned pose, including failed solves. All active constraints must meet unweighted physical tolerances before resolved is true; conflicting weighted goals return a bounded best compromise with resolved false. Defaults: 128 iterations per seed, 4 deterministic seeds, 1e-5 metre/radian tolerances, 0.01 initial damping, 0.25 radian/metre maximum scalar step, +Z joint axes, identity rest/attachment transforms, unbounded scalars, initial value zero. Inputs and scalar bounds have magnitude at most 1e6; omitted bounds may be infinite. Weights are in 0..1e6, iterations in 1..4096, seeds in 1..64, damping in 1e-6..1e3. Point closures match position by default; orientation is opt-in. The dense local nonlinear solve is bounded and not a proof of global feasibility; iteration-limit and stalled are explicit. Returned failures are diagnostic poses, not certified closed chains. Rotation masks select world logarithm components, not Euler angles. No dynamic constraints, obstacle/path certificate, renderer, core or stage dependency is added. Use existing optional chain/swept entries for collision queries. No speed result is published.
For multi-goal IK, the numerical scalar envelope is -1e6..1e6 even when a bound is omitted, so every returned value remains valid as a warm start and for forward evaluation. It is enforced during every candidate and step.
Multi-goal entry size: 8,535 minified bytes, 3,375 gzip bytes (new entry, previously 0), ceiling 3,631 bytes. The optional bytes provide the complete coupled solver; splitting its math would complicate one isolated feature. Core plus stage remains 24,209 gzip bytes.

### Anisotropic painterly filter (batch 271 job 4)
`@margoengine/creative/paint-aniso` exports AnisotropicPainterly, an LDR PostStack effect. Defaults: radius 3 (integer 1..8), strength 1 (0..1), anisotropy 1 (0..1), sharpness 8 (1..8), enabled true. The RGB Sobel structure tensor receives separable 5-tap [1,4,6,4,1]/16 smoothing. Eight overlapping polynomial sectors follow its minor eigenvector; ellipse radii are r*(1+A) and r/(1+A), at most 2r and at least r/2. Weighted RGB variance combines means; centre alpha is preserved. The Gaussian radial weight has a Wendland C2 taper to zero at the ellipse boundary. This is a single-scale variant, not the papers' exact sampled weighting texture or a multiscale solver. All reads clamp to the current viewport. Two rgba32float intermediates cost 32 bytes per target pixel per retained view, capped at 512 MiB per view; inputs are display-space, without alpha-weighted filtering. Zero strength/disabled is an exact copy and omits both tensor passes. Native WebGPU and full WebGL2 are checked; the preview refuses. Per-view buffers/textures/groups are retained, resize replaces them, and device restoration recreates them. No speed, aesthetic or other-device claim.

Anisotropic paint entry: before 0 B, after 9827 B minified / 3746 B gzip, optional ceiling 4002 B; generated alias 67 B gzip. The tensor passes and sector filter stay together to share resources and lifecycle. Core plus stage remains 24209 B.

### Compute dense decompositions (batch 274)

The optional compute/decomp entry returns owned f32 arrays in the input context. It handles real finite matrices, arbitrary leading batches, broadcast solve RHS matrices (only 1-D RHS is a vector), strided/expression inputs, square/tall/wide/reduced/full and empty factors. Arithmetic is f64 in a lazily loaded per-call Rust SIMD Wasm instance on every backend, including native WebGPU and compatibility; GPU inputs incur a readback and results an upload. This is a correctness route, with no device-native decomposition or speed claim. Singular solve/inv, non-positive-definite Cholesky, nonsymmetric eigen/Cholesky input, nonfinite input, f32 output overflow and iteration exhaustion reject. det(singular)=0 and det(0x0)=1. SVD values descend; symmetric eigenvalues ascend. Real symmetric inputs must match across their diagonal exactly; complex/Hermitian arrays are outside compute's supported dtypes. Limits: each matrix dimension and RHS column count <=4096; 16,777,216 f64 workspace words by the checked algorithm bound, and that many f32 output elements per call; Jacobi maxSweeps 100 by default, 1..1000 configurable. Cancellation covers loading, readbacks and batch boundaries (event-loop yield each 16 matrices), not the middle of a synchronous matrix factorization. Concurrent calls own separate Wasm instances; no arena survives a call.
Batch 274 job 2 measured gzip sizes: compute/decomp 0 -> 3617 B (ceiling 3835 B); separate lazy decomp-kernel.wasm 64419 B raw / 25233 B gzip. Compute root remains 39118 B; combined core + stage remains 24209 B. ## Batch 173 job 4: volume-quality and opaque scene termination
Optional `qualityVolume(figure, volume, options)` shares the source data, classifier, clips and transform, hides the ordinary drawable and restores its previous visibility on disposal. Defaults: emptySpaceSkipping=true; blockSize=8 cells (2..32); jitter=true; adaptive={tolerance:0.01,maxStep:4}, tolerance (0,1] in normalized scalar units and maxStep [1,16]; refinement=12 (4..24). isovalue defaults absent, selecting composite or MIP from the source; a supplied isovalue must be finite within the source range and selects the first detected crossing. Optional surface color is linear RGB [0,1], otherwise the classifier at the hit. Clipped samples do not create cap surfaces.
GPU block bounds contain a one-voxel interpolation halo. A 256x256 opacity-range table conservatively includes all gradient/front-back classification rows and interpolation support; classifier replacement rebuilds it. Source/device/block-size changes rebuild min/max blocks. Call invalidate() after updating an existing GPU texture in place. Max block-texture width/height is the device's 2D texture limit; increase blockSize if needed. Each block uses 16 bytes plus a 65536-byte opacity lookup and a 2048-byte rank texture. Original source storage is shared. CPU envelope preparation is bounded by the already uploaded classifier (at most 2048x2048) plus 32896 interval unions; field reduction runs on the GPU, and the expensive noise optimization is offline, not a browser CPU loop.
Adaptive integration widens steps in low-variation blocks and corrects opacity for actual segment length. It is a quality control, not a certified error bound for arbitrarily narrow transfer functions. Steps are bounded by block exits; base spacing is at least the ray interval/2048, with a 4096-iteration traversal cap. Bisection refines the first detected crossing; multiple crossings wholly between sampled endpoints may require higher source quality. Refined isosurface values use explicit float32 trilinear interpolation; general compositing uses hardware filtering. Integration distances use the smallest scene voxel metric and sample centres map exactly to the first/last grid points.

Depth capture presents at graph order 39; custom scientific renderer orders must remain before that. A single nearest reversed-Z depth is used per pixel (maximum covered MSAA sample), so volume coverage at opaque silhouettes is conservative, not independent per-sample integration. Whole transparent layers still sort by centre, not interleaved ray samples. Native WebGPU and WebGL2 compatibility are covered; native GL fallback remains unsupported for these layers.

Changed opaque depth resets only affected pixels, even at the sample cap; unchanged saturated pixels perform no transport. Exact cost counters use RG32uint with mode-specific lossless packing. Total cinematic history/work image storage is now 56 bytes per viewport pixel (previous 48). Colour remains float32. cost() reports zero transport work for saturated pixels in a no-op frame; read it immediately after the frame to be measured, before an extra image capture render. The extra depth/count attachment and packed counters fit 32 bytes of colour attachments per sample. Camera/volume/classifier changes still clear all history.

### Demand rendering (batch 195 job 1)
quality/demand renderOnDemand stops the continuous engine loop and schedules only dirty frames. Defaults: initial true, maxDelta 0.1 seconds, browser animation-frame scheduler, no sources/update/signal. invalidate(n=1) coalesces to the maximum outstanding count; animate() holds are independent and released idempotently; loaded(promise) wakes on success and preserves rejection. sources listen to start/change/end/load. ### Adaptive events (batch 195 job 3)
quality/events adaptiveEvents(handler, options) returns run(...args), regress, setMoving, flush, moving, pending and disposable lifecycle. Defaults: interval 100 ms during motion, debounce 120 ms after start/change/end, no sources or signal, performance.now and native timeout clock. Interval/debounce are nonnegative through 2147483647 ms; interval also accepts Infinity to suppress all motion picks. Control events reset the inactivity timer; setMoving(true) remains in force until false or a later regress timeout. At rest there is no intentional throttle. Queued calls retain only the latest arguments and resolve all coalesced callers with that invocation's result; active async calls finish first, so results cannot arrive out of order. Click/drag handlers stay direct. Rest immediately flushes queued input; a stationary pointer with no queued request is not polled or repicked. flush bypasses the interval without overlapping an active call. Handler rejection reaches every corresponding caller; disposal/abort rejects queued and active result promises, cancels timers and subscriptions, and ignores late completion without cancelling the caller-owned GPU task. No idle polling and no scene/core changes. Applications pass an AbortSignal for owner disposal. Native and compatibility picks tested.

Adaptive events entry size: new 0 to 967 B gzip, ceiling 1223 B. Core plus stage remains 24,209 B. One optional entry keeps deadlines, latest-input promises and lifecycle ownership together.

### Composed physical materials on 16-unit compatibility devices
Full physical shaders and extended materials with six or more distinct extension maps pack the five base maps into one linear RGBA32F array. The remaining eight extension maps, all material lobes, transmission, shadows, clustered/local shadows and IBL remain. Packed arrays are shared by source views, dimensions, mip ranges and sampler state on each device, and released after their last model user. Float array storage per unique set uses 80 bytes per texel at the maximum base-map width/height, times its mip pyramid (roughly 4/3 for a complete square pyramid), plus a 160-byte parameter buffer. Allocation is device-limited; no reduced source images or channels are used. Mip copies run on upload/rebind; streams expose actual resident view dimensions. This correctness fix makes no speed claim.

The 360-case sampling oracle measures at most 0.0000402 absolute channel error against the continuous filtering equations on both tested backends. Native fixed-precision HDR bilinear filtering differs by up to 0.00792 (a fixture with radiance up to 2); packed RGBA32F interpolation retains the continuous reference rather than reproducing that hardware quantization. Custom shading hooks keep their original separate base-map binding contract and own their additional resource budget. No existing composed pipeline assertion changes.

## Batch 177: optional 2D contours

Entry size: 0 B before (absent), 3,802 B min+gzip after, 4,058 B initial ceiling. These bytes hold both interpolation models, exact triangulation predicates, bands, stitching and SVG export together; splitting would duplicate topology or force extra user orchestration. The core + stage root remains 24,209 B gzip. Work is bounded to 4,000,000 cell-level combinations per request; reduce either sampling or levels beyond this allocation bound.

`@margoengine/sciviz/contour2d` has no root/core/stage dependency. `contour2D` accepts strictly monotone rectilinear axes, x-fastest scalar samples, 2x2 through 1,000,000 points; `scatteredContour2D` accepts 3 through 10,000 distinct sites with a noncollinear hull. Coordinates and finite scalars have magnitude at most 1e100; NaN scalars mask incident cells. All 1 through 256 finite levels must strictly increase. Bands cover adjacent levels only; no under/over band is invented. Lines connect exact symbolic cell-edge identities; grid interpolation is bilinear with straight marching chords and the asymptotic decider, with the 0-2 diagonal for an exact saddle tie. Scattered interpolation is linear over the Delaunay convex hull; there is no extrapolation or inferred land mask. Cocircular ties follow input order. Exact dyadic predicates protect triangulation signs; exported intersections use float64 arithmetic.

Polygon rings use even-odd filling and include cell boundaries; they are exportable polygons, without a global polygon-union simplifier. SVG defaults to 800x500, 36 px padding, 1 px dark isolines, six blue-red band colours, labels on, title `Contour plot`. Labels are rotated at half the projected path length, omitted below 48 px, and use a white halo. Global collision avoidance is not claimed. Cancellation checks before snapshots and between bounded batches, with exact abort reasons. Inputs are snapshotted; results own their memory. CPU triangulation is quadratic in the worst case; no timing or Wasm acceleration claim. The demo is standalone SVG and does not mutate the existing Figure or core/stage. Known correctness defects found by this job: none open after the analytical regressions.


### Fresnel reflector floor (batch 188)

Optional environment/reflector-pbr adds PBRReflector, reflectorFresnel and reflectorBlurFraction. New entry 0 to 3,340 B min+gzip; shared reflector 11,355 B, refractor 11,312 B, cube-camera 5,756 B, prefiltered 3,693 B; core + stage stays 24,209 B. Reflection uses Schlick Fresnel (ior default 1.5, allowed 1..4, metalness default 0, allowed 0..1) mixed with baseColor (default #808080). Inherited color tints the reflection. baseColor is an artist-selected constant linear floor term, not direct-light shading. All options are live uniforms.

Inherited roughness (default 0) sets the maximum mip blur. Captured geometry at the plane stays sharp; its world normal distance / blurDistance (default 10 metres, a positive normal float32 from 2^-126 to 3.4028234663852886e38) scales the blur, saturating at the maximum. Empty depth takes maximum blur. Actual inverse oblique projection works for perspective and orthographic captures; there is no assumption of an ordinary depth projection. Up to eight existing box-filtered mips: this is mip blur, not a GGX convolution or screen-space ray tracer. Normal maps distort the lookup; Fresnel uses the geometric plane normal. The standard Reflector's visibility, passes, layer selection, transform convention, capture-only mode and lifecycle remain in effect. Native WebGPU and full WebGL2 compatibility are supported; the lightweight WebGL2 preview still refuses the capture.

### Mesh reflector (MeshReflector, MeshReflectorMaterial, 2026-11-16)

`MeshReflector` (environment/reflector-pbr) and `<MeshReflectorMaterial>` (react/materials) draw a planar reflection over a flat mesh's own surface. By method: the surface blends with one alpha, the mean of the three channel weights, so under a coloured F0 (a tinted metal) the mesh underneath keeps (1 - mean weight) of its colour while the reflection takes its per-channel weight; on a display (non-HDR) target the blend runs on display values. The weight clamps at 1, so a `mixStrength` above 1 / F0 turns into a mirror (drei users pass 40 to 80; here 1 / 0.04 = 25 already reaches a mirror at normal incidence). `blur` reads the capture's box-filtered mips (at most 8 levels) at the shorter axis' size and averages at most 16 taps along the longer axis, so a blur longer than 16 times its shorter side, or past 128 px per tap, is cut short. Depth is the reflected point's world distance from the plane times `depthScale`, not drei's depth-buffer value, so drei's threshold numbers do not carry over. `distortion` is a screen fraction per unit of the normal map (default 0.03), not drei's scale of a height map. The surface is biased 4 depth steps (slope 1) toward the eye to pass the depth test on the coplanar mesh: without it a 48 x 48 subdivided floor seen at a grazing angle out to 400 units showed the floor through 12,676 of 16,640 pixels (its triangles interpolate other depths than the surface's quad), with it 0, native and WebGL2 compatibility. The mesh's geometry must be flat in its local XY plane (within 1e-6 of its size); a box or curved geometry is reported and hides the reflection. Measured: tests/mesh-reflector-browser.js, worst 0.00048 against Schlick on rgba16float, 0 floor pixels left under mirror 1, native and WebGL2 compatibility. Sizes: react/materials 7,366 to 8,493 B gzip, environment/reflector-pbr 3,300 to 4,910 B; an app importing only MeshTransmissionMaterial from react/materials bundles none of MeshReflectorMaterial and keeps the native reflector off its initial chunks (tests/subpaths.test.js), so it does not need its own entry.

### Lightformer and Environment children (2026-11-16)

`Lightformer` (environment/lightformer) and `<Lightformer>` with `<Environment>` children (react/environment), drei's
studio lights. Accepted differences: a Lightformer is an unlit draw of its own (one uniform and one render pass per
form per view), not a mesh with an emissive material, so it does not cast shadows or appear in picking, and an
`<Environment>` capture draws only its children (the rest of the scene is excluded) over its `src` environment or
black. `ring` is open inside radius 0.25 (half the disc's radius). `frames` counts captures, not frames: a capture
waits for its background and every Lightformer inside, so `frames={1}` never misses one. The children are hidden in
the main view by setting `visible` on their meshes while the Environment is mounted; a child hidden before it mounted
stays out of every capture. With children and no `src`, the Environment adds no default sun (the scene keeps the
lighting it had). Measured: tests/lightformer-browser.js (exact `color x intensity` on rgba16float per form; captured
irradiance 1.84 toward a softbox against 0.07 away; refresh tracks intensity within 1%) and the lightformer modes of
react tests/reflections-browser.tsx, native and WebGL2 compatibility. Sizes: environment/lightformer new at 4,300 B
gzip; react/environment 5,763 to 7,105 B (the capture binding and `<Lightformer>`; splitting them into another entry
would break drei's `import { Environment, Lightformer }` path and repeat the Environment wiring). The capture binding loads with
`import()` once an `<Environment>` has children, so an app without children does not pay for it: react/environment's

### Puff clouds (vfx/clouds, react/clouds Clouds and Cloud, 2026-11-16)

`Clouds` (`@margoengine/vfx/clouds`) and `<Clouds>` / `<Cloud>` (`@margoengine/react/clouds`) draw every puff of every cloud in one instanced draw of 4 vertices per puff, sorted far to near on the CPU each frame (equal depths keep the order added, so every run draws the same). `limit` (default 200) caps the puffs drawn; later puffs, and puffs past `range`, are counted in `stats.dropped`, not drawn. Culling tests each puff's bounding circle (its quad's half diagonal) against the side and near planes only. Lighting is per puff, not per pixel: the light reaching a puff is exp(-density x sum of Gaussian overlaps with the puffs nearer the light along `lightDirection`), within one cloud only (one cloud does not shade another), times the Rayleigh phase 3/4 (1 + cos^2) plus `ambient`; it is a fixed direction and colour, not the scene's lights, and the puffs cast no shadow on the scene. Differences from drei by design: the default seed is the cloud's number in its Clouds (React: a hash of the component's place in the tree), not a random value per render, so the same scene draws the same clouds; `material` takes Margo's shading (`'scatter'` or `'unlit'`), not a three.js material; `bounds` is the full size of the box the puff centres lie in; the default texture is generated (a soft, lumpy puff), not fetched; `speed` turns puffs at up to `speed` rad/s and breathes them by up to 1 / `growth` of their size. `softness` needs the scene depth (React adds `@margoengine/post/depth`, a depth pre-pass of the core meshes). Measured on the real GPU (packages/vfx/test/clouds-check.mjs, native and WebGL2 compatibility, 1x and 4x): three clouds of 21 puffs are one draw and one engine draw call; soft alpha within 4/255 of the contrast curve over a floor; near fade within 1/255 of smoothstep(0, fade, distance); the same deltas draw identical bytes. Sizes: vfx/clouds 8,006 B gzip (new), react/clouds 3,247 B (new); core plus stage unchanged. WebGPU or the full WebGL2 compatibility layer only: the small WebGL2 preview is refused at setup (`unsupported`), never attached to draw nothing (packages/vfx/test/clouds.test.js).

### Precipitation cover (batch 236 job 2)
Optional weather/cover is 1,539 B min+gzip, new from 0 B. Core plus stage remains 24,209 B. PrecipitationCover takes an unattached WeatherFX and reuses its top-down depth map (graph order -3) for rain, core Puddles and Snow (order -0.5) and GLTFWeather (cover option). WebGPU and WebGL2 compatibility. Bias defaults to 0.02 m (finite, 0 or more). The map is the WeatherFX square of side 2 x Weather radius centred on the camera, at WeatherFX resolution (default 50 m over 256 texels): surfaces outside it count as exposed, so set radius to reach the sheltered surfaces in view. A receiver is sheltered by the highest occluder of the four texels around it: every point under an occluder at least one texel wide stays dry, and up to one texel past an edge does too. A receiver facing up (normal y 0.5 or more) adds sqrt(2) texels times its slope to the bias, so a sloped shelter's own top is not sheltered by itself; a receiver steeper than 60 degrees keeps the plain bias, and an up-facing receiver less than that rise (at most 0.16 m at 30 degrees with the default 50 m over 256 texels) under a separate shelter counts as exposed. Receivers are tested at the shaded point; with multisampling an edge pixel is shaded at its centre, which can lie up to a pixel outside its surface, so a surface that ends exactly at a shelter edge can show a one pixel exposed fringe. Give shelters a small overhang. The capture splash and lens passes are not installed.

Grid sides 16..512, default 128. Horizontal finite floor/emission aperture, all source vertices below emission plane. Static snapshots require setGeometry after edits; full compatibility supported, native preview refused. Reflected Fresnel branches, roughness, dispersion, absorption and heterogeneous/nested IOR are excluded; source bias is 1e-5 of footprint size. See staging-parity.md for complete defaults/ranges and proof.

Batch 272 job 3 measured gzip: staging/caustics 5447 B, new ceiling 5703 B, core plus stage unchanged at 24209 B. Exact device-restored maps and analytic Fresnel errors below 1.12e-6 on both GPU backends; no speed claim.

Store keys are unique finite numbers or strings; binding keys may repeat for multiple representations of the same row. History defaults to 32 snapshots and is caller-configurable; CPU membership and aggregate evaluation are linear in mapped rows. Native WebGL2 is unsupported by this entry; WebGPU and webgl2-compat are supported. Its store, binding and shader stay together so the optional API does not require coordinated sub-entry loading.

### Batch 186 job 2: shared shadow atlas
ShadowAtlas from /shadow-atlas replaces LocalShadows on one Clustered instance, retaining its maxLights (1..16, default 4), casters, PCF/PCSS, biases, receiveShadow and clipping. It allocates one depth32float array layer, resolution squared times four bytes, plus a 4096-byte uniform table of guarded rectangles. Default atlas 2048, minimum face 32, maximum face 1024, texelDensity 1. Dimensions are powers of two from 16 to 16384, minimum <= maximum <= atlas, limited further by the device. Point/hemisphere lights retain six faces, spots one; directional cascades and area faces share the image.
Point/spot face demand follows the conservative projected world-range box clipped to the viewport. A near-plane intersection requests full viewport demand; a wholly behind-camera bound requests minimum demand. Authored resolution caps demand. Directional/area faces use authored sizes or maximum face size. All tiles are square. Least-screen-important lights lose one resolution level at a time until all faces fit, retaining every face. If minimum demand cannot fit, RangeError asks for a larger atlas or lower minimum; lights are never silently dropped. At most 256 logical faces. Since batch 52 job 4 the atlas caches each face in its own tile (next section). No hysteresis claim.
Deterministic packing proof: sixteen six-face lights at 16 texels use 24,576 rasterized depth texels; four six-face lights requesting 64 texels use 61,440 after fitting a 256 atlas. Both retain every face. This is a work count, not a wall-clock speed result. Source tests cover non-overlap, input immutability, priority, camera-driven viewport changes and caching. Real GPU tests cover point, spot and combined rectangle/sphere filtering on native WebGPU and full WebGL2.
Min+gzip: shadows 11,791 -> 12,052 B (existing 12,145 B ceiling); new /shadow-atlas 0 -> 14,027 B, ceiling 14,448 B. The optional entry reuses the complete caster pipeline rather than duplicating render ownership. Core plus stage remains 24,209 B.

### Batch 52 job 4: cached shadow atlas faces
ShadowAtlas keeps a face's tile while its size class is unchanged: faces that change size or are new take free tiles from a buddy allocator, largest first; only when fragmentation leaves no room is every face placed afresh (and redrawn). A face re-renders only when its light changes (position, direction, range, cone, near/far, shadow size), its tile moves, or a caster whose old or new bounding sphere reaches the face's frustum moves, shows, hides, is added or is removed. A partial redraw keeps the atlas (load) and clears each redrawn tile alone with one depth-0 triangle under its viewport and scissor; a full redraw clears the atlas once. Casters without bounds (instanced or displaced), opacity-mapped and displaced casters (redrawn every frame), a source's shadowVersion, invalidate() and device restore still re-render every face they may reach or every face. Camera-fitted directional cascades follow the camera as before. Point/spot sizes have no hysteresis, so a camera moving across a power-of-two coverage boundary moves and redraws that light's tiles. LocalShadows (the texture array) keeps its whole-array redraw on a caster change. Work count (CPU test, two lights, seven faces): first frame 7 faces, a still frame 0, a box moved under the point light 1 (before this job 7), a hidden, shown, added or removed box under the spot 1, an added third light 1 with the other tiles in place.



## Batch 136: clean-room Draco encoder

The default exporters/draco entry loads one optional Rust/Wasm SIMD encoder on first compression, in a browser worker or in the Node process. The public compressDraco API, abort behavior, GLB preservation and caller-supplied Emscripten encoderPath remain compatible. Sequential and standard/valence EdgeBreaker preserve oriented triangles; independent attribute seams share exact values. Prediction and quantization are described in clean-room.md. A packet is at most 280 MiB (293,601,280 B; 256 MiB before 2026-11-11), the most whose measured peak Wasm memory fits 90% of the encoder's 4 GiB: positions only, the worst measured mix, peaks at 12.9 bytes per input byte (a 16,302,050-triangle grid of 293,505,456 B at 3,780,378,624 B), and a 9,999,392-triangle grid with float normals and UVs (280,126,152 B) at 9.1 (2,538,340,352 B); before, a 243 MB positions-only mesh passed the 256 MiB check and trapped at 4 GiB (KB0035, [draco-encoder-memory.test.js](../packages/exporters/tests/draco-encoder-memory.test.js)). A packet also holds at most 16,777,216 input points, 50,331,648 indices and 255 attributes; each attribute has one through four components. Floats must be finite. Normal quantization accepts 0 or 2 through 30 bits; a one-bit octahedron has no positive reconstruction range and is rejected. Other quantized floats accept 1 through 30 bits, or 0 for exact values. Fan splitting can increase output point count, which the result and GLB accessors report.

Initial replacement measurement: 181,081 -> 89,161 B min+gzip, with Wasm 156,788 B raw / 58,216 B gzip. The complete proof version below is 91,248 B min+gzip, with Wasm 160,900 B raw / 59,962 B gzip. Core plus stage remains 24,209 B. The old prebuilt encoder files have now been removed from source and distribution. No end-to-end speed claim. The byte-output bridge uses eight Wasm boundary calls regardless of output length, rather than one GetValue call per output byte. This counts bridge calls only, not encoding arithmetic or wall-clock time. Quiet speed-phase timing is owed.

At default settings the development comparison preserves exact oriented corner identities and Margo/native-prebuilt decoded result equality on the real fixtures listed in clean-room.md. Box stream 119 vs 130 B; Fox 7,086 vs 7,566 B; the small refrigerator primitive's bounded seed choice gives 352 vs 358 B without changing decoded attributes. This is corpus evidence, not a universal compression-ratio guarantee for arbitrary inputs. The portable normal fixture's maximum Euclidean direction error is below the opaque old encoder at 2/3/8/10/16/24 bits, without weakening its bounds. More settings/corpus evidence belongs to the following proof job.
Batch 191 post/curvature is LDR view-dependent ridge/valley enhancement, not an object-space curvature measurement. Ridge/valley 0..100 (default 1), radius integer 1..16 px (2), gradient threshold 0..1 (0), relative linear-depth rejection >0..1 (0.02). Signed xyz normals come from owned SceneTargets or an any-size callback; supplied normalSpace is world (default) or view. Core meshes capture automatically; optional models use add(model). Empty normals, clear depth and rejected neighbours cannot add silhouette shading. Camera right/up convert world normal derivatives to view space, including rotated and orthographic cameras. The owned capture has the same rgba16float normal/depth footprint as Pixelate. Removing a supplied normal callback after attach switches Pixelate and Curvature to the owned capture from the next frame (it attaches in onPreUpdate, before the frame graph runs); changing the texture returned by a stable callback works. A callback set after the owned capture started leaves that capture attached until the effect is disposed (one extra capture pass).

Batch 191 job 6: post/curvature 0 -> 8940 B min+gzip; core plus stage unchanged at 24,209 B.
