## Scientific datasets (batch 176 job 1)
The optional @margoengine/sciviz/datasets entry normalizes structured curvilinear, rectilinear, mixed PolyData, unstructured, multiblock and partitioned inputs to an AnalysisGrid-compatible DataSet. Fields and geometry are owned snapshots; source cell IDs, sparse blocks, names and top-level block IDs are retained. Composite topology is concatenated without welding separate blocks. Flattened arrays are the intersection of block field names; heterogeneous fields remain available on the original blocks. Shared field widths must agree. Use each block when a field is not common. Empty blocks are null. Source dimensions live under dimensions, not the regular-image dims discriminator. Existing pipeline, contour, clip, calculator, probe and glyph entries consume the normalized type directly. Contours of line cells return points, and matching isolated vertices are retained; clipping supports these dimensions too. Constant line cells do not emit infinitely many contour points.

Defaults: maxPoints=1000000 (allowed 1..10000000), subdivisions=2 (1..64, rounded upward to a power of two). Source cells are bounded by maxPoints and output cells by 4*maxPoints; tessellated points are bounded by maxPoints. Lagrange curve/triangle/quad/tetrahedron/hexahedron/wedge orders 1..10 use equispaced nodes. A Lagrange hexahedron (VTK type 72) from a VTK XML file older than version 2.2, or with no version, has its edge 10 and 11 nodes swapped back to the numbering VTK 9.1 adopted (edge 10 runs corner 2 to 6, edge 11 corner 3 to 7); version 2.2 and later read as written, and a version that is not major.minor is refused. Quadratic curve, triangle, quad, tetrahedron, hexahedron, wedge and pyramid use the standard 3/6/8/10/20/15/13-node spaces. Explicit referenceNodes may permute the standard lattice. Higher-order cells are uniformly approximated with interpolated simplex vertices; callers raise subdivisions for finer approximation. This is deterministic h-refinement, not adaptive error-controlled refinement or an exact curved-cell filter. Matching generated nodes share original-ID interpolation keys across cells. Independent composite blocks remain independent, including ghost boundaries; ghost arrays are retained, not implicitly removed.

PolyData source order is vertices, lines, polygons, strips. Polygons must be simple and planar (relative planarity threshold 1e-10); concave polygons are ear clipped. Polyhedron face streams must be closed and consistently oriented with planar simple faces. Nonconvex cells use a face-plane arrangement, limited to 4096 regions per source cell, and signed solid-angle interior classification. Generated interpolation uses mean-value coordinates with boundary handling and affine checks. Arrangement point merging uses 128*Number.EPSILON times the source diagonal. Self-intersecting surfaces and degenerate cells are not supported input. Linearized filtering follows the existing filter entry's numerical domain and interpolation policy; source curved-cell interpolation is not re-evaluated after each filter.

Readers: .vtr, .vts, .vtu, .vtp, .vtm, .vtpd/.vtpc, with numeric VTK payloads decoded by @margoengine/loaders/vtk-xml. Raw-appended arrays use its bounded range reader; metadata sniffing and composite XML are bounded by maxBytes (default 64 MiB). Every retained array is decoded when creating the owned dataset. Composite references resolve against the input URL or baseURL, or an explicit files map; nesting is limited to 64 and cycles reject. Relative string inputs use baseURL, or document.baseURI in a browser. Files must fit the specified per-read and decoded-array limits. All numeric point/cell tuples are retained; scalar defaults to the first one-component point field. PLOT3D covers whole-grid 2D/3D, single/multiblock, formatted Fortran D/E exponents, stream binary and 4-byte-record-marker unformatted, both byte orders, 4/8-byte coordinates and optional iblank. Defaults: 3D, formatted, multiblock, no blanking; binary defaults little endian, float64, record markers. Options explicitly disambiguate variants. Iblank is retained as an array, not a rendering mask. Solution Q/function files, plane-record layouts and 8-byte record markers are not claimed. The NASA originals use the supported formatted whole-grid variant. No file is fetched or GPU device created on import, and cancellation preserves its exact reason. No core or stage change and no measured speed claim.

Dataset entry size: 35,806 minified bytes and 13,072 gzip bytes, previously 0, optional ceiling 13,423 bytes. The entry keeps topology normalization, interpolation, nonconvex scientific-cell decomposition and VTK/PLOT3D adaptation together; splitting would add cross-entry orchestration for the same bytes to users of this one feature. Core plus stage remains 24,209 gzip bytes.
### Batch 217 job 3: scroll and range playback

Optional cutscene/scroll exports RangePlayback and ScrollPlayback. Range defaults: entire timeline, iterationCount 1 (nonnegative fractions and Infinity supported), normal direction, speed 1. Directions are normal, reverse, alternate and alternateReverse. update(delta) runs the borrowed player's skip() for each crossed leg, preserving instant order; seek resets each repeated leg without firing its start instant. At most 1000 boundaries per update; larger deltas reject before mutation. play resolves true at completion, false on pause/stop, rejects on AbortSignal; pause resumes progress, completion restarts. Instants stay on the player, iteration/finish events on the controller. Controllers own advancement, so pause the base player and update the controller only.

Scroll defaults: window, physical y axis, start 0, end current maximum scroll offset, whole timeline range, scrub 0 seconds (immediate), automatic events/frames true. Pixel offsets and seconds are clamped to the supplied interval. A positive scrub is an exponential time constant; automatic smoothing settles to the target within 1e-7 seconds. automatic false uses update(delta) from the app's clock. refresh() re-reads content bounds; resize and scroll events refresh automatically. No-scroll sources hold the start. Physical horizontal offsets can use explicit signed start/end for RTL layouts. Abort/dispose cancels callbacks and keeps the borrowed player usable. No renderer or core additions, and no speed claim.

Batch 217 job 3 measured min+gzip: new scroll entry 0 to 2,048 B, ceiling 2,304 B. The optional entry combines clock ownership and cleanup for both timeline drivers; splitting those controllers would add entry and integration complexity. Core plus stage remains 24,209 B.

## Batch 177 job 2: statistical charts

Student-t critical values support positive fractional residual df through 100000, including LOESS df below one. Bracketing rejects critical values above 1e150 with a remedy to increase residual df; no fixed-range clipping or unconverged fraction is returned. The continued fraction has a 2048-iteration hard limit and checked relative convergence. The low-df regression includes independent SciPy values at df 0.2 and 0.5.

Entry gzip sizes: `/stats` absent (0 B) to 6,719 B, initial ceiling 6,975 B; `/maths` 5,703 B to 8,854 B, ceiling raised from 5,959 B to 9,120 B. Sharing the math functions between direct transforms and chart marks avoids independent implementations; splitting the public CPU utility entry would add import orchestration and break the requested `/maths` access. Core plus stage remains 24,209 B.

`/stats` creates owned CPU marks and standalone vector SVG with axes, ticks, titles and labels; it introduces no Figure/core/stage API or GPU pass. Error bars support x/y symmetric or asymmetric amounts, caps and points. Box plots use interpolated quartiles, median, Tukey adjacent-value whiskers and outliers; violins use 96 Gaussian KDE queries over data range plus three bandwidths, maximum half-width 0.4 per category. Area and pre/post/mid step lines preserve missing-data breaks. Signed area/bar stacks keep separate positive/negative bases, with optional independent unit normalization. ECDF is right-continuous, two-sample Q-Q interpolates common midpoint probabilities, 2D density is a diagonal Gaussian KDE, and hexagons expose exact input membership. All mathematics is also exported from `/maths`.

Defaults: SVG 800x480, padding 58 px (minimum 24), white background, empty title/x/y labels, six categorical colours, automatic linear axes with nice ticks; point radius 2.5 px, line width 1.4 px. Box width 0.6; whisker multiplier 1.5; area baseline 0; stack kind area, normalization off, bar width 0.8 of smallest positive x gap; step mode post; density queries 32x32 (2..256); hex radius supplied in data units. Silverman bandwidth uses sample SD and IQR/1.34; constant observations use 1% of max(1,abs(value)) before the Silverman factor. Optional bandwidths must be positive. Violins independently normalize maximum width, not sample count. Named box/violin groups label the categorical x axis. Stack series use category colours in input order.

Linear and LOESS confidence defaults to 0.95, accepted range (0,0.999]. OLS needs three paired finite samples and nonconstant x. LOESS local degree is one, span 0.5, two robustness iterations (integer 0..10), at least three neighbours and three finite pairs. Tricube weights exclude the furthest selected neighbour. Queries default to sorted observed x; optional `at` permits explicit positions. Local zero-weight or nonpositive residual-df cases reject with a suggested remedy. LOESS intervals condition on final robust weights and are approximate pointwise mean bands, not simultaneous, prediction or extrapolation guarantees. Missing xy pairs are removed from statistical fits; area/step drawings retain gaps, stack NaN contributes zero. Errors must be nonnegative magnitudes; signed NASA lower errors are converted to magnitude only when drawing their bars.

Inputs are finite with magnitude at most 1e100, with NaN denoting missing. At most 100000 observations per series, 100000 Q-Q queries, 1000000 stack cells, 4000000 sample/query or LOESS fit/sample pairs, and 200000 SVG marks. This bounds allocations/work; reduce the dataset or query resolution beyond it. Maths is synchronous and owns results; import has no DOM, network or global side effects. Argument failures are linked RangeErrors carrying code `out-of-range`. No speed gain, exact confidence coverage, journal layout or new interactive Figure claim. The 13-chart real-data demo includes downloads and a 390 px layout.
Batch 175 optional entry min+gzip: sciviz/omezarr 0 -> 20,866 B, recorded ceiling 21,492 B. These bytes include the shared Zarr region reader, store validation, scalar adapters and codec pipelines. Keeping them together preserves one reader and source contract; splitting the entry solely for a smaller recorded size would duplicate validation or require additional imports for a cloud source. Core and stage source are unchanged.
Batch 175 core plus stage measurement: unchanged at 24,209 B gzip, below the 25,000 B gate.

### Compute Rust SIMD CPU backend (batch 274 job 3)

createCpuWasm from compute/cpu-wasm returns the existing CPU API, with f32/i32/u32 values and all existing built-in CPU operations. Custom WGSL remains unsupported. Every context loads an isolated SIMD-required Wasm instance on demand; creation accepts AbortSignal and normalizes load/compile failures to a coded MargoError. Numerical calls are synchronous and cannot be interrupted mid-dispatch. No GPU or worker is required. Arrays remain normal owned host buffers, so memory growth never invalidates an array or a returned readback. The transient packet limit is 8,388,608 f64 words (including descriptors and parameters); larger work rejects with RangeError and can use smaller stream chunks. The module has a 512 MiB memory ceiling. Transcendental operations use host Math imports; exact A/B equivalence is against the JavaScript CPU backend on the same host. Expression intermediates cross the bulk bridge; there is no wall-clock speed claim. Core plus stage remains 24,209 B gzip. Final entry and Wasm sizes are recorded with the job's size gate.

### Batch 195 job 2: resource quality knobs

`@margoengine/quality/knobs` exports `textureResolutionKnob`, `particleKnob`, `renderTargetKnob` and `msaaKnob`. Live ladders default to scales [1, 0.5, 0.25], weight 2, with custom names/scales/weights. A `FeatureScaler` or `watchFeatures` accepts the first three. Particle levels multiply live VFX rate, followed by a final zero-birth level. Existing particles finish normally; capacity, explicit bursts and simulation work remain unchanged. Level zero restores the original option, including its absence.

Accepted limit: live MSAA change needs an engine re-create. `msaaKnob.apply(0|1)` records 4|1 samples only. ### Batch 173 job 5: direct curvilinear and spherical volumes
Optional sciviz/curvilinear snapshots finite node geometry and scalars (NaN masks missing nodes). General structured cells use trilinear inverse mapping, a stackless spatial cell tree and 24 Newton iterations per candidate; singular or sign-changing corner/centre Jacobians reject. Caller must supply an injective, non-overlapping grid; the validation is not a proof of global injectivity. Spherical axes are strictly increasing, radii positive, latitude in [-pi/2,pi/2], longitude unwrapped across at most 2 pi with a duplicated endpoint for periodic fields. Node indices are x/longitude fastest. Scalar textures retain the root volume's binary16 precision; topology is float32. Masked interpolation support stays transparent, without filling holes.
ReferenceStep is the physical opacity distance (default smallest nonzero grid edge); quality controls samples per reference distance. At most 4096 segments cover each ray, widening the step when necessary. Discrete midpoint sampling can miss sub-step features; quality/refStep control that error. Gradient classifiers use physical finite differences; preintegrated classification shares step/density conventions. Native WebGPU and WebGL2 compatibility are supported; the native GL-only sciviz driver is not. The node, cell-tree and axis textures each need at most maxTextureDimension2D rows of maxTextureDimension2D texels (the cell tree takes two texels per tree node, about four per cell, so a 4096 compatibility device holds about four million cells); a larger grid is refused before its source layer or any GPU resource is created.
Coordinate slices accept fractional indices and tessellate the original coordinate surfaces; spherical slices have node-spaced polygon silhouettes. Outline stride defaults to 8, retains all boundary curves and uses one-pixel lines. Owned source stays hidden, with classifier/density/mode/clip controls on layer.source; dispose the mapped layer to remove its source and all sections. Geometry and missingness are immutable; create a new layer to replace data.
NOAA demos use public-domain modified subsets: NEXRAD straight measured rays (no refraction or earth-curvature correction), WOA23 five-degree stride/11 original depth levels, depth exaggerated 231.67x. Attribution, processing and SHA256 records sit beside the binary subsets. No timing or speed claim.

### Batch 186 job 3: point-light cube cookies
CubeProjectorLights in /cube-projector is a ProjectorLights superset. Use setCubes for point-light entries and inherited setProjectors for spot images on the same light list. Entry i belongs to clustered light i. Cube faces are +X,-X,+Y,-Y,+Z,-Z, equal square RGBA8 images with top-to-bottom rows; side 1..4096, at most 16 distinct cube/colour-space pairs and 16,777,216 combined face texels, at most 1024 indexed entries. Pixels are copied on setCubes. Null/unset entries multiply by one, spots ignore cube entries and point lights ignore spot images. At the emitter origin, direction is undefined and the cookie is neutral.
Defaults: sRGB encoding, identity emitter-to-world quaternion. Rotation accepts finite nonzero quaternions, normalized with scaled arithmetic to avoid overflow. Filtering is bilinear at the supplied image level, seamless across edges with the specified three-face corner average. Decode sRGB and multiply alpha before interpolation. No derivative-based mip selection or HDR/float face input is claimed. Cube storage follows the spot images in the one projector storage binding (143; a separate binding 152 until 2026-11-11, KB5663d, which put the full hook set at nine fragment storage bindings, one over the WebGPU default of eight): one buffer of the next power-of-two size of spot plus cube words, bounded by device storage limits. Restore recreates storage from copied bytes; disposal releases both cookie kinds.
Native WebGPU and full WebGL2 production shaders prove all six colours, face UV orientation, edge continuity, corner average, rotation, sRGB/alpha and mixed spot/cube isolation. Min+gzip: reconstructed prior projector 2,639 B -> 2,720 B, inside its 2,871 B ceiling; new cube-projector 0 -> 4,493 B, ceiling 4,716 B. Composition avoids duplicate spot upload and lifecycle state. Core plus stage remains 24,209 B.




### View-driven geography (batch 180 job 1)
New optional sciviz/geo-lod, no core or stage edits. Defaults: projection mercator, maxZoom 15 (range 0..24), tileBudget 64 selected leaves, tilePixels 256 physical pixels, cacheTiles 128 resident tiles, concurrency 6 tile jobs (imagery and elevation fetch concurrently per tile), fadeSeconds 0.3, segments 32 (1..256), skirt 1000 metres. Cache must exceed the selected budget to retain a root fallback. Coarse fallback plus fading children may draw at most twice the leaf budget; residency is capped independently by cacheTiles. CPU pixels and meshes are retained for device restore. Missing imagery (404 or undefined) keeps a cached ancestor; other errors reject ready and remain in error without retry. Frame-driven loading needs continuing rendering or explicit updateView; ready waits current requests only, with an optional signal. Disposing aborts requests and drops resources. Tiles whose texels are all opaque draw without blending once fully faded in (KB-GEO1: a blend that changed nothing still made frames differ by one level at a few pixels on the RTX A6000, D3D12); fading and translucent tiles blend, so frames during a fade, or of translucent imagery, are not promised bit-stable on every GPU.
Flat Mercator/equirectangular and WGS84 globe use XYZ Mercator source bounds, ending at +/-85.05112878 degrees latitude (polar caps are outside this raster source). View selection uses conservative projected bounding boxes, not terrain occlusion. Heights and skirts are metres; elevation is a pixel-centred bilinear grid. No vertical datum conversion is inferred. geoTerrainStreamSource wraps longitude and clips latitude at a fixed level, resampling to TerrainStream.tileTexels (2..1024); the caller supplies TerrainStream's physical tileSize, origin and colours. quantizedGeoElevation calls tiles/terrain's decoder lazily, rasterises pixel centres, rejects incomplete coverage and does not infer a geographic tiling scheme. Native WebGL2 preview is refused by requireGPU; WebGL2 compatibility uses the same draw path. No wall-clock speed claim.

Geo-lod entry size: new 0 to 7261 B min+gzip, ceiling 7517 B. One optional entry retains a cohesive view/cache/height/render lifecycle. Core plus stage unchanged at 24,209 B.

## Batch 177 job 3: specialised charts

The optional sciviz/charts-extra entry is 7292 B gzip (new entry, previous 0 B, ceiling 7548 B); core + stage remains 24,209 B. It provides polar/wind rose, ternary, candlestick/OHLC, pie/donut, sunburst/squarified treemap, Sugiyama Sankey/alluvial, radar and UTC calendar heatmaps. All paths, own axes/scales, labels and data titles export as vector SVG with no raster fallback. Layout coordinates are 1000x600, export width/height are positive and default to those values. Hierarchies: 10,000 nodes, 64 levels, nonnegative leaves, internal sums. Flow graphs: DAG, 10,000 nodes, 50,000 input/expanded vertices, 129 layers; one global width scale, default 12-unit padding/16-unit nodes/8 sweeps. ### Compute NN extras (batch 274 job 4)

compute/nn-extra adds BatchNorm, GroupNorm, ConvTranspose2d, LSTM, GRU, upsample and Upsample. All support Tensor gradients and the existing JavaScript CPU, Rust SIMD CPU, WebGPU and compatibility routes. Data and parameters use the context's float32 primitives. Norm eps defaults 1e-5 and affine defaults true. BatchNorm accepts rank >=2 and a channel axis (default 1); training needs >1 value per channel. Running mean starts at zero, variance at one; momentum is the new-batch contribution (default 0.1, null cumulative); trackRunningStats defaults true. Inference uses saved buffers. GroupNorm takes NCHW-style [batch,channels,...spatial], channels divisible by groups, and the same statistics in train/eval. Module stateDict/loadStateDict include nested module state; BatchNorm stores running mean, running variance and batch count in addition to learned parameters. Batch count persistence uses f32, so integer counts above 16777216 lose unit resolution.

ConvTranspose2d input is [N,C,H,W], weight [inChannels,outChannels/groups,kh,kw]; stride/dilation default 1, padding/outputPadding 0, groups 1, bias true. Output padding must be below stride or dilation. withOutputSize selects dimensions in the stride-derived output range. Output geometry is (input-1)*stride-2*padding+dilation*(kernel-1)+1+outputPadding. Metadata uses O(outputH*outputW*inChannels/groups*kernelH*kernelW) indices/masks per group and a batch-offset table; backward scatter sums overlapping float contributions in the backend's order. Use smaller batches/images to respect device buffer limits; no tiling is claimed.

Recurrent input/output is [time,batch,features] by default (batchFirst false). numLayers 1, bidirectional false, bias true, dropout 0. Dropout applies between stacked layers while training. LSTM uses i,f,g,o gates; GRU uses r,z,n, with reset applied after recurrent candidate projection. run returns sequence, final h and LSTM c, with state shape [layers*directions,batch,hidden]. Optional lengths mask padded output and retain previous state for each batch item. forward returns sequence only; run's returned tensors share a differentiation graph and must remain alive through their backward uses. States are explicit, never held between calls. Recurrent state/table storage grows with sequence length through the tape.

Upsampling takes [batch,channels,1..3 spatial axes]. Choose size or scaleFactor (default 2), nearest by default. Linear/bilinear/trilinear use half-pixel centers unless alignCorners true; bicubic is 2D with a=-0.75 and clamped edges. Nearest uses floor(outputCoordinate*inputSize/outputSize). Scale-derived sizes floor their products. Interpolation metadata is O(outputPixels*taps^rank), with 1/2/4 taps per spatial axis. It does not implement antialiased downsampling. Different data layouts compose the existing permute operation.

Measured sizes: compute/nn-extra 0 to 20860 B gzip, ceiling 21486 B; compute/nn 19137 to 18873 B; compute root remains 39851 B and core plus stage remains 24209 B. One optional entry shares tape/selection helpers; a split would duplicate them. No wall-clock speed claim.
### Depth, MSAA and mip targets (batch 271 job 1)
`@margoengine/creative/targets-depth` exports DepthTextureRenderTarget, a TextureRenderTarget (cube, array or 3D; rgba8unorm or rgba16float) with per-surface depth, 4x multisampling and mip generation. Defaults: depth true, depthFormat depth32float (also depth24plus, depth24plus-stencil8), samples 1 (1 or 4), per pass depthLoadOp clear and clearDepth 0 (reversed Z, as the engine). Each mip and layer or volume slice owns its own 2D depth texture (multisampled when samples is 4); depth is not resolved or mipmapped, since WebGPU has no depth resolve. At 4x, cube and array layers resolve straight into their layer; a volume slice resolves into a 2D scratch that is copied into the slice when the pass ends. generateMipmaps(encoder) fills mips 1 and up from mip 0 with an exact area-weighted box footprint, so odd sizes (5 to 2 to 1) weight edge texels by their covered fraction; volumes also filter across slices. Allocation, counting colour, retained depth, multisample colour and volume scratch, is capped at 256 MiB per target. restore(device) drops every attachment and pipeline; callers redraw. On the WebGL2 layer, volume slices drawn with depth go through the layer's 2D stand-in (two blits per such pass; operational playbook 3.2). Native WebGPU and full WebGL2 are checked; no speed claim.

Depth target entry: before 0 B, after 3398 B gzip, optional ceiling 3654 B. TextureRenderTarget gains one protected textureUsage() hook (COPY_DST for the volume resolve copy); the /targets entry stays within its ceiling. Core plus stage remains 24209 B.

## Typed tables and cross-filter (batch 174 job 2)

`@margoengine/sciviz/table` is an independent optional entry, 13,003 B min+gzip from 0 B, ceiling 13,167 B (13,092 B before the per-segment GPU aggregation kernel; 12,906 B before the Parquet FLOAT16, JSON, ENUM and UUID reading; 12,694 B before the CSV int64, blank-line and nan/inf reading). `@margoengine/sciviz/series` shares the Parquet reader: 14,137 B (13,943 B before), ceiling 14,169 B. `@margoengine/decoders/snappy` is 1,250 B from 0 B, ceiling 1,506 B. The bytes buy scalar CSV/Arrow/Parquet readers, null/int64 preservation, indexed filters and deterministic aggregation; splitting the table API would complicate shared column and filter identity. Core + stage stays 24,209 B.

Tables borrow immutable equal-length typed columns. Dictionary strings use Uint32 indices; validity is a separate bitmap. Integer and time values retain signed/unsigned 64-bit storage. Wide decimal and opaque binary scalars are lossless dictionary strings (unscaled decimal with its scale, or hex). Parquet FLOAT16 columns read as numbers (little-endian binary16), JSON and ENUM columns (logical or converted type) as UTF-8 text, and UUID columns as 8-4-4-4-12 hex text with unit `uuid`, per the format's LogicalTypes.md. readCSV skips empty and whitespace-only lines and reads nan/NaN/-nan and case-insensitive inf/infinity cells as NaN/+-Infinity, as pandas read_csv does by default; other missing markers (NA, null) are text unless listed in `nullValues`. Readers accept flat scalar tables, not nested/repeated arrays, tensors, encrypted/external Parquet chunks, obsolete LZO/Hadoop LZ4 or Arrow view layouts. Flatten nested sources before reading. Arrow files and streams support dictionaries, replacement/delta dictionaries and LZ4-frame/Zstd buffer compression. Parquet supports flat row groups, v1/v2 pages, plain, dictionary, RLE, delta binary/length/prefix and byte-stream-split encodings, six modern codecs and page CRC. The readers default to 100,000,000 rows and 536,870,912 input/decoded-block bytes; overrides are explicit. Streaming/range reads belong to the separate large-series job.

Arrow Time and Duration columns without a unit read the schema default, milliseconds (Timestamp's default is seconds). A Parquet page with no values may be empty or carry only its encoding header (dictionary bit width, delta block header); both read as nulls. Aggregation bin i holds lo + i w <= v < lo + (i + 1) w with w = (hi - lo) / bins, the last bin also hi, decided against those edges rather than a rounded quotient; a finite range wider than the largest double is binned through halved bounds. With `gpu`, the host sorts each 256-row tile's finite values by bin (row order kept) and one invocation reduces each (tile, bin) run, so the kernel holds no per-bin arrays (WGSL caps a shader's function variables at 8,192 bytes; the earlier per-tile kernel kept 80 KB at 4,096 bins) and makes three stores, which the WebGL2 layer runs as GPU point draws at every bin count (the earlier kernel fell back to the CPU above 204 bins). A chunk's output stays at most 8 MiB (3 floats per segment). Range filters are [lower, upper); set filters use exact typed equality, including explicit null. Dimensions intersect; a cleared dimension passes nulls. Every dimension builds its own index once. Boundary/set changes touch only changed row spans/postings and changed bitmap words; first-time indexing and switching filter kinds are full-index operations. Duplicate row values are retained.

Aggregation supports up to 4,096 1D/2D bins per call, final upper edge included. Host classification uses numeric column values; supplied GPU context performs all count, valid-count, sum, minimum and maximum tile reductions. Mean uses the merged sum/valid count. Rows without a valid coordinate do not enter bins. Null/nonfinite values do not enter numeric statistics. Counts are exact Uint32. Numeric inputs round to f32, each tile adds in fixed source order, and host totals merge in float64; this is not exact-real or float64-input summation. A tile's sum error relative to its f32 inputs follows gamma(255) times its absolute input sum, before host rounding. Rescale values if f32 inputs/tile sums overflow. Empty numeric bins return NaN. CPU fallback follows the same tile order. No timing or rival-throughput claim is made.

The 10,000,000-row correctness proof repeats the 4,096 licensed TLC observations, selects 9,670,406 rows and compares every bin statistic with an independent exhaustive reference on WebGPU and WebGL2 compatibility. The linked demo selects 2,211 observations below two miles and changes both rendered charts.

## Engineering file readers (batch 176 job 2)
Six optional entries: sciviz/hdf5, /cgns, /xdmf, /exodus, /openfoam and /ensight. No new core or stage code. FileOptions maxBytes defaults to 64 MiB per read/metadata object/decoded selection; normalized geometry uses the existing DataSet maxPoints/subdivisions bounds. Integer values outside JavaScript's safe precision reject explicitly. Readers take AbortSignal; lazy HDF5 files support dispose and Symbol.dispose. In-memory companion files use exact resource names via files or resolve; remote files use baseURL or the source URL.
HDF5: superblocks 0..3 including user blocks, object headers 1/2 and continuations, legacy local-heap symbol tables, compact links and dense links in fractal heaps, v1/v2 B-trees, compact/contiguous/chunked arrays, single/implicit/fixed/extensible/v2-B-tree chunk indexes including allocated pages, missing chunks as fill values, fixed numeric/string and variable-string data, deflate and shuffle. HDF5 2.0 layout version 5 filtered chunk records are also accepted. Numeric hyperslabs read only intersecting chunks or contiguous rows; opening does not decode dataset payloads. Attribute name projection avoids decoding unrelated reference/compound attributes. Metadata signatures, ranges and index structure are checked; HDF5 metadata lookup3 checksums are not currently verified. Unsupported shared/huge heap messages, virtual/external datasets, arbitrary compound/array/vlen numeric datatypes, applied filters other than deflate/shuffle and nonstandard float encodings reject by name. Deflate verifies its Adler checksum.
CGNS/HDF5: structured Cartesian/cylindrical grids (one complete X/Y/Z or R/Theta/Z set of equal lengths; spherical or mixed sets reject), unstructured linear and common quadratic/complete order-two cells, mixed sections and NGON/NFACE polyhedra. Primary cells follow base cell dimension; boundary elements do not inflate solution tuple counts. FlowSolution selection defaults to the first solution; Vertex/CellCenter fields are retained. All matching bases/zones become independent blocks. ADF files require conversion through CGNS tools. Boundary condition subtrees, rind arrays, non-node/cell solutions, external CGNS links and uncommon higher-order element families remain outside this entry's current semantic projection.
Xdmf 2/3: XML/HDF/raw Binary data items; numeric endian/precision; strided HyperSlab and JOIN; basic XML path references; uniform/curvilinear/rectilinear/regular and mixed linear/quadratic/polyhedral grids; spatial composites and selected temporal collections. timeIndex defaults 0. Other Function expressions, subset grids, arbitrary XPath/XInclude and compressed Binary items require writer materialization. Structured Dimensions and origin/spacing are converted from slow-to-fast file order to x-fastest dataset order.
Exodus: classic/64-bit-offset NetCDF through the existing /netcdf reader and NetCDF-4/HDF5 storage through /hdf5; coordinates, finite-element blocks, selected nodal/element/global time results, entity maps and node/side sets. timeIndex defaults 0. Element connectivity is read in Exodus II node order (SAND92-2137 Figure 4, SEACAS hex27 figure) and renumbered for the dataset: HEX20, HEX27 and WEDGE15 list their mid-edge and face nodes differently from VTK; TET10, PYRAMID13, QUAD8/9, TRI6 and BAR3 already agree. WEDGE18 is refused, since no public Exodus description gives its mid-face node order; write such blocks as WEDGE15. Results defined on only some blocks remain on elementBlocks with their true block IDs; only fully defined results enter flattened cell arrays. CDF-5, grouped assemblies, arbitrary polyhedral Exodus blocks and edge/face result families are not projected.
OpenFOAM: polyMesh points/faces or faceCompactList/owner/neighbour/boundary; ascii and raw binary, label/scalar widths 32/64 and either byte order; volume/point scalar/vector/tensor internal fields, patch values and owner extrapolation where no patch value is written. Defaults mesh=constant/polyMesh, time=0, fields=[], boundaries=true. Named patches become independent polydata blocks. boundaryField entries resolve as OpenFOAM does: an exact patch name, then a patch group named in the boundary file's inGroups (the last such entry wins), then the last quoted regular expression matching the whole patch name (OpenFOAM User Guide, boundary conditions; OpenFOAM 2.2.0 release notes, patch groups). A `$name` value resolves to a top-level entry of the same field file. Calculated boundary values must be written by the solver; this reader does not execute boundary-condition code, and `#include` style directives are stepped over without reading the included file, so a patch whose value comes only from an include falls back to the owner cell value. Binary lists are skipped by their element width, so raw bytes are never read as text. The binary-safe index and entry precedence took the sciviz/openfoam entry from 10883 to 11272 B gzip; a split would only move the same parser into a second chunk every field read loads. Multi-region/decomposed cases can be resolved as separate calls.
EnSight Gold: ascii, C binary and Fortran record binary geometry; unstructured common linear/quadratic (quadratic elements in the EnSight element figure's numbering, which matches VTK's except the bar3, whose mid node is listed second), nsided/nfaced and structured/rectilinear/uniform blocks; scalar/vector/tensor node/element files; case wildcards and timeIndex selection. littleEndian defaults true. Full transient file-set scheduling, partial/undefined result records, material/species files, complex constants and uncommon structured flags are not interpreted. Original part and source-cell boundaries remain intact. These are file-format limits, not speed or universal-format claims.

Engineering entry gzip bytes (new entries, each before 0 B): sciviz/hdf5 8990 B; sciviz/cgns 18306 B; sciviz/xdmf 19254 B; sciviz/exodus 20029 B; sciviz/openfoam 10566 B; sciviz/ensight 11539 B. Combined core plus stage remains 24209 B. The optional entries retain complete reader ownership, numeric decoding and dataset normalization; splitting them solely for smaller individual numbers would add cross-entry orchestration without reducing an importer's total bytes.

## Batch 175 job 2: figure point clouds

The optional sciviz/pointcloud entry accepts any OctreeSource, including COPC and Potree, and lazily opens COPC, Potree, LAS or LAZ URLs. LAS/LAZ downloads the entire file before building a memory octree; remote COPC uses its existing Range reads, and Potree retains its lazy hierarchy pages. The figure must be 3D with linear axes. Origin defaults to local zero for an explicit source; the URL opener uses the reader origin. Bounds and attribute picks are in world data units; decoding and rendering retain source float32 local-coordinate precision. A statewide EPT tile can span hundreds of kilometres, so centimetre precision is not promised at every point. Use smaller tiles for local precision.

The point budget must be an integer at least the root count; the default is max(2,000,000, root.count). Nodes are additive and admitted whole, so drawn count can be below the budget. maxLoadedPoints defaults to three times the budget and is an LRU target; visible nodes and in-flight node reads can exceed that target. Retained attribute bytes count actual typed-column byte lengths. Attribute colours use a global explicit range (default source z extent for elevation, [0,1] for other fields); scalar and vector-component maps, RGB preservation and live changes share the same map for future loads. Missing columns/components reject. Picks and rectangle/lasso selections cover resident visible nodes; they do not infer unloaded rows. Open SelectionStore universes enumerate explicit selected keys only; inactive rowIds is empty while has(key) follows the empty predicate. Keys survive eviction and reload; selection history remains caller-bounded.

The real demo archives only the root and first level of the 167,692,896,718-point Iowa EPT collection: 188,887 original points in nine LAZ files, 2,266,644 attribute bytes resident. Both backends draw 188,887 with budget 220,000 and 34,923 with budget 40,000; selection and recolouring read zero additional tiles. This proves view and work bounds for the archived levels, not full-density Iowa. A metadata-only billion-point CPU test allocates and loads two visible points and 20 attribute bytes. GPU elapsed-time and country-scale streaming performance remain for the deferred speed phase.

Batch 175 job 2 size record: points/octree 9,179 to 9,372 B gzip (ceiling 9,267 to 9,654 B); points/copc 15,177 to 15,309 B, within its existing ceiling. New sciviz/pointcloud is 21,055 B gzip with ceiling 21,685 B. sciviz/link is 4,662 B. Core + stage remains 24,209 B. ### Batch 173 job 6: direct tetrahedral volumes
Optional sciviz/tetvolume accepts conforming, non-overlapping VTK type-10 grids with shared node IDs. Point scalars interpolate linearly in barycentric coordinates; cell scalars are constant. Geometry/scalars are immutable snapshots; NaN at any supported vertex masks that cell. Adjacency is indexed by the opposite local vertex; boundary is -1. Degenerate cells, repeated nodes, invalid offsets/indices, more than two owners of a face and same-side owners reject. Normalized determinant must exceed 1e-10 times the product of the three edge lengths. Global self-intersections and nonconforming duplicate geometric vertices remain caller constraints.
The float32 cell packet is 96 bytes/cell, with approximately 64 bytes/cell for a binary bounds tree, plus padded texture rows, a 272-byte uniform and the shared classifier source. CPU replay retains those packets and 16 bytes/cell of adjacency. Float-encoded topology caps at 8,388,607 cells; the GPU 2D texture capacity can impose a smaller limit. CPU construction is synchronous; throughput evidence is owed to the speed phase.
The ray uses adjacency when a neighbour has a positive-length interval, then a spatial entry query for boundaries or disconnected pieces. Convex cells are integrated front-to-back once, with at most cellCount+1 traversal iterations. Up to 2048 midpoint segments per cell cover its entire clipped interval; long cells widen the step rather than truncate the ray. Default referenceStep is the smallest physical edge, quality 1.5, association point; other defaults follow VolumeLayerOptions. Physical extinction uses a normalized metric to avoid squared-unit overflow/underflow. Scene depth and up to four source clip planes truncate the ray. MIP finds the exact maximum of each cell's linear field along its ray interval, then uses the classifier opacity.
Point and cell scalars are normalised to the classifier range without clamping, as the regular volume stores its voxels, so a cell whose node values cross the range interpolates the given values, and a colorScale map (under, over and NaN colours, log and binned steps) is read through the shared float-table lookup (tests/tetvolume-browser.mjs `beyond` and `encoded`). Native WebGPU and WebGL2 compatibility are supported; the native GL-only sciviz driver is not. Classifier, density, quality, mode, shading and clips live on the hidden owned layer.source; disposing the tetrahedral layer removes all its owned resources and source. Opaque classifier alpha stays exactly opaque even for a very large referenceStep. Gradient classification uses the constant physical cell gradient; preintegrated classifiers keep the existing segment/density contract. Finite sampling and float32 plane/interpolation precision remain accuracy limits.
The NASA demo uses 2146 original sampled scalar values, extruded as a span-invariant field on 6048 tetrahedra, with height exaggerated 12x. Its 65x3x65 reference is resampled from those same cells with CellLocator; physical opacity is matched nonlinearly at each density. Original zip, output hashes and transforms are recorded in tmr-tet.json. No timing claim.

Tetrahedral entry size: 6322 B min+gzip (ceiling 6578 B), previously absent; core + stage unchanged at 24209 B. Colour scales (2026-11-15): 6403 to 7030 B (ceiling 7286 B) for the shared float-table colour lookup.

### Automatic scatter LOD rings (batch 64 job 5)
scatterLODs(mesh, { ratios, signal }) from @margoengine/scatter/simplify returns { meshes, triangles, deviation }. Defaults: ratios [0.4, 0.12], two triangle fractions decreasing within (0, 1]. Ring 0 is the source object; ring 2 is simplified from ring 1. Input is a core Geometry (positions and normals only) with triangles, up to 200,000 vertices. Every ring vertex is a source vertex, so normals are never interpolated or recomputed; a ring keeps more than its ratio when no collapse is left that keeps seams and hard edges closed (a box keeps all 12 triangles). deviation is a one-sided bound (source vertices to ring surface), tested over every vertex and triangle pair, so it costs source vertices times ring triangles: fine for scatter meshes, slow for a 200,000-vertex one. A collapse may lower a blade's tip: Scatter's blades check refuses a ring whose top falls to the root. ringDistance(deviation, pixels = 1, height = 1080, fov = pi / 3) is the pinhole projection of that bound, ignoring wind bend and instance scale (multiply deviation by the largest scale yourself). Needs the optional peers @margoengine/lod and @margoengine/mesh-edit; no GPU work and no speed claim. Entry size is in scripts/quality/baselines/sizes.json; core plus stage unchanged.

### Water bodies (batch 67 job 1)
water/bodies WaterBodies takes 1 to 64 bodies: closed outlines (3 to 4096 points, even-odd inside, self-intersections not checked) at one level, or river paths (2 to 4096 [x, level, z] points, width 0.01 to 10000 per point) on a uniform Catmull-Rom spline at 16 steps per span. The body map is corner-sampled rgba32float, 16 to 2048 texels on the longer side (default 256), with two texels of margin; past the margin the map clamps, so distances there read at most the margin. The CPU rasterization is brute force over texels and segments with a bounding-box skip and refuses more than 4e8 texel-segment visits. Shorelines are smooth at the map resolution, but the Water grid's triangles still carry level changes between bodies across one grid cell. The Water grid stays origin-centred and is shaded and discarded outside the bodies, so a large grid around a small lake costs its full vertex work. Overlaps: the later body covers the earlier one; there are no holes. Water's wave velocity is scaled by the body's wave share in WaveQuery; coastal flow is not body-aware.

### List 3 batch 66 job 5: underwater view

Underwater options: absorption and scattering three channels 0..100 /m; anisotropy -0.99..0.99; shafts 0..10; steps integer 1..128; shaftDistance 0.1..10000 m; maxDistance 0.1..100000 m; shaftExtent 1..10000 m; resolution power of two 16..1024 (copied); waterline 0..64 px; refractiveIndex 1..2. The waterline is one probe plane under the camera per frame; several views per frame share one uniform. Focusing is clamped to 0.1..10. Owned GPU memory: three rgba32float plus depth32float targets (viewport, resolution squared, 1x1), plus viewport-sized opaque HDR colour and depth32float snapshots.

Batch 234.3 underwater underside: exact dielectric Fresnel, total internal reflection and Snell window on the submitted Water/FFT normals. Screen traces visit at most raySteps pixels (integer 1..2048, default 512) per ray, within maxDistance. Depth-plane validation uses thickness (0.001..10 m, default 0.05) plus the local pixel footprint. ### Water bodies (batch 67 job 1)
water/bodies WaterBodies takes 1 to 64 bodies: closed outlines (3 to 4096 points, even-odd inside, self-intersections not checked) at one level, or river paths (2 to 4096 [x, level, z] points, width 0.01 to 10000 per point) on a uniform Catmull-Rom spline at 16 steps per span. The body map is corner-sampled rgba32float, 16 to 2048 texels on the longer side (default 256), with two texels of margin; past the margin the map clamps, so distances there read at most the margin. The CPU rasterization is brute force over texels and segments with a bounding-box skip and refuses more than 4e8 texel-segment visits. Shorelines are smooth at the map resolution, but the Water grid's triangles still carry level changes between bodies across one grid cell. The Water grid stays origin-centred and is shaded and discarded outside the bodies, so a large grid around a small lake costs its full vertex work. Overlaps: the later body covers the earlier one; there are no holes. Water's wave velocity is scaled by the body's wave share in WaveQuery; coastal flow is not body-aware.

### Wave subsurface scattering (batch 67 job 2)
water/scatter WaterScatter adds a backlit glow to one Water from its two directional lights. color is linear RGB 0 to 1 (default [0.04, 0.32, 0.24]), strength 0 to 100 (default 1, 0 is off), power 0.5 to 64 (default 4), distortion 0 to 1 (default 0.3). Thickness is a proxy (height above the still or body level over total wave amplitude, or crest), not a baked thickness map; it ignores point and spot lights and the water depth below the surface. It shades only: geometry, WaveQuery and SSR capture are unchanged. Optional entry, so the water root entry does not grow. One scatter per Water; attach after WaterBodies so crests are measured from each body's level and wave share.

### Procedural grass blades (batch 64 job 6)
GrassScatter(options) from @margoengine/scatter/grass is a Scatter with no mesh input; options.grass is { height 0.6, heightVariance 0.4, width 0.04, blades 8, radius 0.15, lean 0.35, round 0.3, segments [5, 3, 1] } by default, in instance units (ScatterOptions.scale scales the clump). Ranges: height 0.0001 to 10000, width 0.00001 to 1000, radius 0 to 10000, heightVariance and lean 0 to 0.95, round 0 to 1, blades an integer 1 to 64, segments three non-increasing integers 1 to 16. A clump draws blades * (2 * segments - 1) triangles a ring. blades shading is on unless options.blades replaces it; its root-to-tip shade uses the tallest blade's height, so a shorter blade's tip shades slightly darker. The shape is compiled into the WGSL, so it is fixed for the scatter's life. Blade randomness hashes the instance's world root bits, so two instances at one exact spot draw the same clump. GrassScatter.attach(engine, options) takes no meshes. Proof is on WebGPU only (diffuse and PBR colour passes); the shadow pass uses the same pose code but has no picture test yet. No speed claim. Entry size is in scripts/quality/baselines/sizes.json; core plus stage unchanged.

### List 3 batch 66 job 8: steep-bed rivers

Rivers options: substeps integer 1..64 (default 8); maxFroude 0.1..20 (default 4); at most 16 sources, each a finite [x, z], discharge 0..100000 m^3/s and radius 0..10000 m (square footprint, cells whose centres lie inside it). One Rivers per Water; it needs a Water with a terrain coast. Pipe speed is capped at maxFroude * sqrt(g a) and at half a cell per substep, so a fall of any height stays bounded, but the reconstruction drives flow by the depth above the brink only: on beds steeper than the depth per cell a chute front runs slower than the slope's gravity component (about 2 m/s on a 0.5 slope in the float64 oracle). No bed friction term beyond the 0.12 /s flux decay. Water's own coast flow (no Rivers attached) is since 2026-11-18 a momentum-conservative staggered step with Manning friction n = 0.02 (KB-WATER-SWASH1, below in Water surf), its face speed capped at half a cell per step, so its falls stay bounded too (a 10 m fall stays under free fall from the top); use Rivers for falls and chutes with sources (2026-11-11).

### Rain ripples (batch 67 job 3)
water/rain WaterRain draws rain rings on one Water: rain 0 to 1 (or a weather's, read every frame from `rain` or a WeatherMachine's `state.rain`), cell 0.05 to 5 m (default 0.4), lifetime 0.1 to 10 s (default 0.8), strength 0 to 1 (default 0.35). At most one ring per cell in each of three grids at a time; a ring spreads to a quarter of its cell. Rings fade out where a pixel covers more than 0.2 of a cell. Rings shade only (normals); optional splashes put real drops into a Ripples field: rate 0 to 1000 per second at full rain (default 20), at most 32 a frame, inside a square of side area (default 16 m) around the camera, radius default 0.5 m and depth default 0.02 m. The splash radius must cover one cell of the field, or Ripples rejects the drop when the frame renders. One rain per Water. Optional entry, so the water root entry does not grow.

## Astronomy and microscopy import, batch 176 job 3
- Optional sciviz/fits reads primary/IMAGE HDUs, all FITS BITPIX types, BSCALE/BZERO/BLANK and BINTABLE L/X/B/I/J/K/A/E/D/C/M plus single P/Q variable descriptors. Physical integers stay exact for unscaled 64-bit values; rendering explicitly converts to floating point. Cells retain vector/complex arrays, nulls, dimensions and units. ASCII tables, random groups, compressed-image table conventions and multiple P/Q descriptors per cell reject explicitly.
- WCS retains primary or A..Z axes, units, CRPIX/CRVAL, CD or PC/CDELT and legacy CROTA, with zero-based pixel input. Linear axes, SIP forward polynomials and TAN/SIN/ARC/STG/ZEA sky projections have independent WCSLIB tests. Other projection/rotation/spectral algorithms are outside this entry's current world() projection support; original cards and linear metadata remain available. No all-projections claim.
- sciviz/mrc reads MRC/CCP4 little/big endian modes 0/1/2/3/4/6/12/101, complex selection, labels and opaque extended headers, MAPC/MAPR/MAPS, starts, origin and triclinic unit-cell geometry. Storage order is never silently flipped; file handedness cannot be inferred from this standard. Vendor extended headers and crystallographic symmetry operators are retained as bytes rather than interpreted. ORIGIN and NXSTART/NYSTART/NZSTART both place the first sample (Cheng et al. 2015, section 4.6, same sign convention), so world() applies one, never both: a nonzero real-mode ORIGIN in angstroms, else the starts in grid steps; complex modes keep ORIGIN as a phase origin in pixels, not a position, and Fourier phase origins remain metadata, not an inverse FFT. Files carrying the IMOD stamp (word 39) follow its flags (word 40): flag 1 clear reads mode 0 as unsigned bytes (IMOD before 4.9), flag 4 clear negates ORIGIN (IMOD before 4.11). Mode 101 puts the lower-coordinate pixel in the low nibble, as the IMOD format page states for both byte orders. Remaining ambiguity: a mode 0 file written unsigned without the IMOD stamp (IMOD before 4.3, other old writers) cannot be told from a signed one and reads as signed, the MRC2014 consensus; when ORIGIN and the starts are both nonzero and disagree, ORIGIN wins; MRC2014 (Cheng et al. 2015, section 4.6) calls ORIGIN the outside corner of the first pixel, yet world() places sample index 0 at ORIGIN with no half-sample shift: the same section gives ORIGIN the sign convention of the integer START fields, whose index n is grid point n, and a file with ORIGIN 0 cannot be told from a crystallographic grid read through START, so a corner shift applied only to nonzero ORIGIN would move a crop half a sample against its parent; the CCP-EM page's subvolume example (ORIGIN 100, 120 inside a volume at 0, 0) holds under either reading. Shift by half the voxel size when a writer is known to mean the corner.
- sciviz/ometiff reads classic/BigTIFF Z/C/T stacks through decoders/tiff. Quantitative uint8/int8/uint16/int16/uint32/int32/float32/float64 samples remain unscaled. LZW, deflate, PackBits and uncompressed tiles/strips, chunky/planar samples and integer/floating predictors are supported. Explicit TiffData, series selection and multi-file FileName/UUID resolution are supported; unspecified planes reject on access. A TiffData with neither IFD nor PlaneCount covers every IFD of the file it names, so such a companion file is read when the stack opens. image() takes its origin from the Plane whose TheC is the channel holding the sample (an RGB channel's three samples share one Plane); a Position in a length unit converts to the PhysicalSize unit, while a 'reference frame' (the OME default) or 'pixel' position is added as written. The UnitsLength table and the channel lookup raised the sciviz/ometiff size budget from 3732 to 4192 B gzip; the table is needed by every image() call, so a separate chunk would save nothing. Metadata and individual planes are lazy after bounded full-file acquisition. SubIFD pyramids, BinaryOnly companion XML, JPEG/JPEG2000 microscopy payloads and vendor annotations are outside the requested lossless stack projection. The real IDR fixture is an explicitly identified, native-pixel, lossless crop of the original JPEG2000 image, not a claim that the runtime decodes JPEG2000 TIFF.
- Default per-file/per-read maxBytes is 64 MiB; TIFF default maxPixels is 2^26 and safe integer 64-bit offsets are required. The OME loader bounds each volume by maxBytes and planes conservatively by maxBytes/8 pixels. FITS and MRC accept gzip; FITS also bzip2. Non-axis-aligned/celestial world() coordinates are preserved exactly within supported transforms; generic grid/volume helpers preserve directed physical axes and reject rotation, shear, permutation or nonuniform sample spacing with code unsupported, without physical resampling. Readers retain full precision independently of Float32 renderer grids. Scientific volume helpers do not imply celestial reprojection or an affine/sheared volume renderer.

Scientific entry gzip (bare package imports external): TIFF 4401 -> 6064 B; new sciviz/fits 4908 B, /mrc 2906 B, /ometiff 3207 B. Their optional budgets are raised in the same change. Quantitative BigTIFF addressing, lazy pages, signed/floating samples and full plane mappings justify these bytes; splitting TIFF would duplicate directory or codec infrastructure. Core + stage root remains 24209 B.

Landing accounting for upstream tiled export (batch 178): shared tile-aware line-batch uniforms also grew optional lines/debug from 9549 to 9874 B gzip, above its old 9836 B ceiling. The ceiling is 10171 B; tile-aware debug geometry is retained. A split would duplicate batch viewport uniforms and shader state. No additional line source change or core/stage bytes.

## AVIF still images (batch 203 job 4)

### Batch 176: adaptive mesh refinement
sciviz/amr accepts nonoverlapping Cartesian cell-centred blocks with integer refinement ratios and finer faces aligned to coarse cells. Coarse masks hide completely covered cells; NaN denotes missing values. Native AMReX/BoxLib Header, Cell_H and IEEE32/64 FAB data support endian descriptors, scalar selection and stored ghost-box trimming. Enzo ASCII/HDF5 hierarchies and grouped HDF5 baryons support active or ghost-inclusive arrays. FLASH HDF5 uses only node-type-1 leaves. Non-Cartesian solver coordinates, AMReX headerless/raw and HDF5 plotfiles, staggered/nodal fields, Enzo particle arrays and FLASH CORNERS output need separate format extensions; readers do not silently treat these as the supported cell-centred layout. Points and in-face rays on a face follow the clamped cell index: cells own [lo, hi), an interior face belongs to the block above it (an empty region above it gives NaN and no interval), and the hierarchy's upper faces are closed, so sampleAMR and traceAMR agree everywhere.
Direct volume rendering uses a disjoint k-d tree of block boundaries and packed scalar textures; no finest-resolution dense volume is allocated. Default interpolation is linear inside each block, clamped at that block's outer cell centres. Composite and sampled MIP, scalar transfer functions, density, scene-depth clipping, up to four clip planes, device restoration and level outlines work on WebGPU and WebGL2 compatibility. Gradient/preintegrated classifiers are rejected. There are at most 2048 integration samples per leaf interval. Construction defaults to 1,000,000 nodes, rejects depth over 128, and exact f32 indexing limits samples to 2^24 and packed texels to 2^23 (device texture limits may be lower). An explicit referenceStep defaults to the smallest physical cell spacing.
Masked slices preserve the original cell values and native resolution. Contours use a shared point lattice at finest spacing by default, bounded to 2,000,000 sample points, with explicit dims for coarser extraction. This resampling is analysis only and is never used by the volume renderer. The openly licensed demonstration is Natarajan's final oscillating-cylinder AMReX timestep (CC BY 4.0), with one unscaled float64 velocity field; same-level rectangular packing changes storage only. Nyx native plotfiles are provided by yt expressly for experimentation/testing, a narrower permission than the CC BY demo; no CC0 licence is asserted. No speed number is claimed during the build phase.

AMR optional entry size: new entry, 0 to 30,067 B gzip; ceiling 30,374 B. With the in-face ray rule (2026-11-15) the entry measures 30,377 B; ceiling 31,289 B. The bytes include native solver readers, HDF5 parsing, masks, k-d integration and analysis helpers. Splitting these into mandatory companion entries would complicate one coherent AMR API and its loading contract. Core plus stage remains 24,209 B.

AMR scalar transfer lookup also accepts the shared log/symmetric-log, binned and under/over colour encodings, using unfilterable float textures and explicit lookup. Below-range negative samples remain eligible for MIP; missing NaNs are skipped rather than confused with a numeric sentinel.




### Batch 175 job 3: exact aggregation
Optional sciviz/aggregate defaults to 256x256 bins, edges 1..4096, at most 1048576 bins and 16777216 bin/category cells. Partial GPU storage is bins*(280+categories)*4 B and must fit maxStorageBufferBindingSize. Chunk rows default to 32768, maximum 65536, with at most 8388608 row/bin tests per dispatch. On the GPU one invocation tests at most 512 rows (a bin's slice of the chunk) and a merge pass folds the slices; slice records take bins*slices*(280+categories)*4 B, slices = ceil(chunk rows/512), and a chunk whose records would not fit one storage binding is shortened. Chrome on ANGLE Metal drops a WebGL2 draw whose single invocation runs too long, with no error (docs/known-bugs.md). Finite binary64 values retain all bits; sums and means round once, ties to even. Geometry uses projected f32 coordinates; point bin ownership is corrected at f32 boundaries. Mesh values are cell values, polygons use even/odd pixel-centre coverage and segments use pixel-box intersection. Fractional antialiasing and vertex interpolation are outside this contract. Exhaustive work is O(rows*bins); no throughput claim. The 100M physical-row WebGPU check repeats 4096 original TLC observations, uses 2400000000 B input arrays, 10736160 B peak staging (2293760 B of it slice records), 17920 B partial output, 3052 dispatches and 1600000000 row/bin tests. All 100M rows contribute. Display spreading uses circular radii 0..32; density, when supplied, is in (0,1] and measures occupied pixels having an occupied eight-neighbour. Growth stops at the first qualifying radius or the cap, without changing original statistics. Details and evidence: docs/sciviz-aggregate.md.

Batch 175 job 3 measured optional entry: sciviz/aggregate 0 -> 28201 B gzip, ceiling 29019 B. Exact full-range binary64 accumulators, five glyphs, all reductions and one coherent figure/shading lifecycle justify the bytes. Splitting would fragment table/trace ownership. Core + stage remains 24209 B. On 2026-11-15 the entry went from 28228 to 29742 B (+1514 B), ceiling 30635 B: segment and polygon coverage on the GPU now runs IEEE binary32 round-to-nearest-even arithmetic in u32 integer operations, because WGSL leaves f32 rounding, fusion and division accuracy to the hardware and one ULP decides a pixel centre on an edge (1081 B), and each invocation tests at most 512 rows with a merge pass after, because a long single invocation is dropped on the WebGL2 layer under ANGLE Metal (433 B) (docs/sciviz-aggregate.md). Core + stage is unchanged.
- Batch 174 job 6: optional sciviz/views absent to 4786 B min+gzip, ceiling 5042 B. Current sciviz root 60851 B; this job changes no root source. Core + stage remains 24209 B. Each FigureLayout cell owns one engine and canvas; there is no shared GPU-resource or single-canvas claim. Defaults: ceil(sqrt(count)) columns, 320px cell height, 12px gap; labels default View N. Links default to 3D cameras or 2D x/y physical ranges, with first-figure initial state; selected axes, programmatic sync and AbortSignal are supported. Polling follows changes on the next active engine frame; call sync for stopped engines. All linked figures must have the same dimensionality. Camera projection overrides are borrowed functions. ComparativeGrid uses independent FilterPipeline caches with a shared registry; complete node params replace per-cell params, time defaults to zero, and all outputs are released by the owning pipeline's operator contracts. VolumeQuad owns three orthographic nearest-sample heatmaps and a 3D volume plus three slice planes. It clamps and snaps the crosshair to exact sample centres, retains voxel IDs/orientation, and keeps physical screen scale isotropic across resize. Source CPU samples are borrowed, dimensions must each be >=2, and total voxel count must fit uint32 provenance IDs. Default colormap gray; one shared colour range comes from the 3D volume. Box extent/spacing is axis aligned; no oblique reslicing or patient-space registration is added. Layouts/controllers are disposable; individual setCrosshair signals cancel unpublished work and ready accepts an abortable wait. No timing or clinical claim.


## Above-water screen-space refraction
With a borrowed scene color texture, Water traces up to 50 m along the
refracted ray inside the active viewport. It refines the intersection in at
most five depth-plane steps. If needed, it checks up to eight increasingly
spaced intervals for depth crossings, bisecting each candidate up to ten
times before validation. This bounded first-layer depth approximation cannot
see hidden or offscreen geometry or resolve every narrow crossing. On an
open-water miss the body uses the 50 m deep-water fallback. A terrain-coupled
Water can use its modeled gap. The Water frame uniform is 576 B.

## HDR open water and partial camera waterline

Water estimates diffuse sky light with eight cosine-weighted directions. Sharp solar illumination remains the direct
light's job. Its HDR sky transform and scale occupy two unused float lanes of the existing 560 B frame.
Planar reflections feather their capture boundary and fade out toward the ocean horizon. The underwater near-plane
mask filters at the pixel footprint and keeps its physical ray-traversal limits. A planar capture still represents
one reference plane, so very steep or breaking waves can distort the captured geometry.

On the public base, water measured 30,644 B gzip and water/underwater 8,754 B. The changed builds measure 31,356 B
and 9,087 B respectively, with ceilings of 32,297 B and 9,360 B. Both share their existing rendering, capture and
resource paths. Moving them behind separate entries would duplicate that work. Core and stage remain at 24,797 B.

## Short wind waves and sky reflection

Each of the five baseline ripple lattices fades over a projected pixel width of 0.25 to 1.0 lattice
cells. The broadest keeps detail out to 13.33 m per pixel along its least sampled axis. Nonzero
`chop` adds normal detail at wavelengths near 3.7 m and 2.3 m, with nominal amplitudes of 0.060 m and
0.029 m before chop and wind-patch gain. Each band filters from 0.9 to pi radians of phase change per
pixel. Short-wave depth and forces are outside this shading model.

The reflection uses five taps in an angular lobe from either supplied sky type. Down-going rays on
open water lose at most 34% of their sky weight. This is an approximation of surface occlusion and
secondary reflection. There is one water fragment path and no extra binding, texture, or pass.

The root water entry measures 32,655 B minified and gzipped, up from 32,150 B. Its ceiling is 33,635 B.

## Shader comments in package builds

Package dists ship no WGSL or GLSL comment text (KB-WGSL1). Every package build strips the comments from the shader
strings it emits (`scripts/shader-comments.mjs`; conventions.md, "Shader comments"), keeping every token's text, order
and line; the sources keep their comments. The quality gate `shader-comments` fails when a comment ships. Two kinds of
comment stay on purpose: anchors that code searches for by text (`//INDICES` in compute's quantized kernels,
`/*lod:direct*/` in lod's imposter shader, five in voxel-pathtracer, one in scatter). Columns after a
removed block comment on the same line move; line numbers never do. Core and stage ship no shader comments, so core +
stage is unchanged. Rolled out in batches; min+gzip per entry before and after (entry-sizes.json's method):

## Batch 180 job 5: temporal analysis

The optional @margoengine/sciviz/temporal entry measures 3,901 B min+gzip (previously 0 B), ceiling 4,157 B; core + stage remains 24,209 B. It reads one field per step and retains O(field length) arrays. Statistics use equal step weights with population or sample deviation, not duration weighting. ## Compute quantized inference (batch 274 job 6)

`@margoengine/compute/quant` uses signed int8 packed four per word. Matmul supports
vector promotion and broadcast batches, per-row activation and per-column weight
parameters shared across batches. Conv2d uses NCHW/OIHW, per-tensor activations,
per-output-channel weights, groups/depthwise, stride, dilation and explicit or same
padding. Output parameters are per tensor. Int32 accumulator overflow is rejected
conservatively, including bias. Dimensions and index products must fit signed
32-bit indexing and device storage/dispatch limits. Nearest-even f32 requantization
is lossy and saturates. Float-reference error bounds, scale representability and
finite-output assumptions are in docs/compute-quant.md. No latency or model-wide
accuracy claim; uint8, training and integer-only requantization are outside this
signed-int8 entry. Core and stage receive no changes.

The new optional /quant entry measures 3,927 B minified gzip (previously absent,
0 B), with a 4,183 B quality ceiling. The bytes provide both backends, packed
storage and validation in one optional module; splitting would add loading and
API complexity without reducing core/stage. The core + stage root remains
24,209 B gzip in this build, below its unchanged 25,000 B ceiling.


## GPU graph layout (batch 175 job 5)

Optional @margoengine/sciviz/graph-gpu has device-resident 2D/3D FR and ForceAtlas2, a sorted Morton grid tree, styled screen-space edges/arrows, GPU FDEB and collision-avoiding labels. CPU all-pairs references remain available. There is no root/core/stage import.

Graph counts are 1..16,777,216 nodes, subject to per-device buffer/binding limits; indices are exact u32. Grid side is a power of two, 2..512 in 2D or 2..64 in 3D. Defaults are 128 and 16. theta defaults to 0.7; 0 gives all pairs. Tree bounds use actual points even outside the Morton partition box. Sorting takes log2(padded N)*(log2(padded N)+1)/2 device passes; every node is represented, with no sampling. Concentrated/coincident leaves can require quadratic pair work. Force storage and accumulation are float32, not bit-identical to binary64 CPU results. Zero-length pairs receive a seeded index direction.

FDEB defaults to six cycles, 50 initial iterations, 0.1 step/stiffness and 0.6 compatibility; 1..9 cycles, at most 10,000 initial iterations. It is deliberately opt-in: compatible pairs are evaluated without truncation, O(E squared * subdivision points * iterations), and buffers must fit device limits. Rebundle after moving nodes; bundled endpoints are a snapshot. Arrows follow each edge's own direction. Self loops do not pull on their node; degenerate projected edge segments are not drawn.

Label candidates are explicit node/text records, default maximum 200 visible (`maxLabels`, any integer of 0 or more): candidates are placed in priority order and the first that fit are kept, so the ones left out are the lowest-priority or overlapping ones. Only candidate positions are gathered/read back by refreshLabels(); frame hooks reproject that snapshot for camera changes. Call refreshLabels after layout changes. Labels avoid each other and viewport boundaries; obscured labels can be suppressed. Device loss hides a GPU-owned layer; recreate layout/bundles/layer on the replacement device, as with other caller-owned GPU arrays. Dispose drawing layers before their caller-owned layout and bundles.

The million-node proof records all output positions, moved-node count, capped movement, persistent buffer bytes, dispatches, compare-exchanges and many-body interaction count. These are logical allocations/work, not physical VRAM, heap totals, FPS or wall-clock measurements. Million-node topology repeats the original OpenAlex citation subgraph; it does not claim a million unique works. Runtime speed comparisons await the speed phase.

The new graph-gpu entry measures 13717 B gzip (before 0 B), ceiling 14129 B. Core + stage remains 24,209 B. Full layout, bundling and drawing share one optional lifecycle; a split would add resource coordination solely to save optional bytes.
Batch 180 job 4 CF and projections: /cf reads existing CDF-1/2 NetCDF lazily, not HDF5/NetCDF-4. Independent dimension coordinates, scalar numeric and character labels, matching two-dimensional geographic auxiliaries and selected time-dependent auxiliaries are recognised. Every non-horizontal dimension longer than one requires an explicit zero-based index; no implicit first member/time/level. Projected x/y mappings supported: CF Lambert conformal conic, Albers, polar stereographic, Mercator and latitude/longitude; other CRS names require geographic auxiliary coordinates. The coordinate metadata is retained, not a complete CF validation or general UDUNITS implementation. Unit conversion covers documented climate SI vocabulary, compound integer exponents, pressure, degrees/radians and affine Celsius/Fahrenheit/Kelvin; unknown or incompatible conversions reject. As in UDUNITS-2, a plural is taken only on a unit name (meters, hours, days), never on a symbol: ms, Pas and Ns are not metre, pascal or newton and reject as unknown. A longitude cell's bounds name the arc that holds its centre, so a conservative remap keeps cells wider than 180 degrees. Units metadata temperature differences suppress affine offsets.
CF reference-time conversion supports standard/gregorian with the 1582 gap, proleptic Gregorian, Julian, noleap/365_day, all_leap/366_day and 360_day. Uses fixed SI durations, numeric timezone offsets, fractional/negative offsets, no Date conversion of model dates. Years bounded +/-1000000; standard/Julian require positive years. Leap-second instants, calendar=none and custom calendars require caller conversion, not silent Gregorian fallback. Appendix D vertical formulas broadcast by dimension names into Pa/down or m/up; dimensional positive metadata is preserved. ocean_double_sigma_coordinate counts k from 1 along the level dimension, so k_c is the number of upper sigma levels, as in the HOPS and NCOM Fortran formulas CF took the definition from (CF does not state the base). Its lower-set formula is evaluated as CF writes it; that text is self-consistent only in HOPS depths (positive down, lower sigma 1 to 2), so a writer using negative heights for z1 and z2 does not get -depth at the seafloor. Maximum broadcast 16777216 elements, caller configurable.
Source sampler cap 16777216 nodes, target default cap 4194304 cells. Rectilinear axes must be monotonic after longitude unwrap; full cycles inferred, regional seams explicit, duplicate seam values must agree. Bilinear default or nearest, strict missing corners by default or explicit renormalization. Curvilinear uses a 5 degree cell index and bounded inverse bilinear solves; folded/degenerate cells and missing geographic positions are holes. Curvilinear periodicity requires explicit periodic=true. No extrapolation beyond source nodal coverage. Land masks are independent fraction/percent grids sampled categorically; default threshold 0.5. Map-cell centre sampling is for display and is not conservative. conservativeCF separately preserves rectilinear cell-average area integrals using CF bounds or midpoint-derived edges; returns valid-area coverage, and rejects overlapping source cells. It does not invent arbitrary curvilinear conservative cell corners.
Projection angular inputs are degrees, outputs use radius units (default metres with radius6378137). Default WGS84 flattening for conics/polar/Mercator, zero for plate/Robinson/Mollweide. Conic defaults parallels30/60; origin0 except polar90; central meridian0, false origin0, scale1. Opposite standard parallels reject as a degenerate cone; singular poles return undefined, out-of-domain inverses return undefined. Robinson uses the published 5-degree table and a local monotone Hermite interpolant, so between-knot pixels can differ from other interpolants. Mollweide is spherical. Neither conformality nor equal-area properties are claimed for Robinson. Rendering uses retained finite-cell meshes, existing colour maps and both backends, with device restore.

Batch 180 job 4 entry sizes: cf 0 -> 14438 B gzip, ceiling 14872 B; projections 0 -> 2328 B, ceiling 2584 B. Optional CF semantics and independent Snyder transforms are retained together to avoid duplicated dimension/lifetime coordination; the existing mesh owner stays lazy. Core + stage source unchanged.



Batch 274 ONNX tree/SVM follow-up: TreeEnsembleRegressor and TreeEnsembleClassifier execute legacy ML1..4 encodings, plus a compatibility extension retaining their semantics under deprecated ML5 imports. TreeEnsemble uses ML5 with float16/float32/float64 typed splits/weights and membership sets. Legacy trees accept float32/float64/int32/int64 inputs and produce float32 scores, preserving exact int64 labels. Graph tuples, references, targets, flag vectors and all cycles validate before traversal. Combined modern nodes/leaves and legacy node counts cap at 16777216; output tensors share the existing element/storage caps. SVMClassifier/Regressor implement all four kernels, regression/one-class output, linear and support-vector classification, raw pairwise multiclass scores, labels, calibration and post-transforms. Uncalibrated support-vector output has K*(K-1)/2 scores (two for binary), calibrated output K. Calibration uses at most 16777216 workspace scalars, at most 4096 classes, residual <0.005/K and at most max(100,K) sweeps; exhaustion rejects. Model parameters must be finite. All inference remains synchronous CPU SIMD Wasm inside each graph node. Compatibility does not mean GPU inference. No throughput claim.
Accepted provider differences and exact evidence are in clean-room.md: top-class labels follow raw class scores, regression honors post_transform, and PROBIT retains the existing mathematical inverse-normal behavior. The external provider refuses deprecated ML5 legacy trees; analytic tests cover that compatibility extension. Wider single-score binary metadata and extreme calibration coverage remain review work. Remaining unbuilt groups listed above are unchanged.

Follow-up measured size: ONNX entry 10139 -> 10139 B min+gzip (existing 10444 B ceiling retained); separate onnx-kernel.wasm 684541 -> 753589 B raw and 244935 -> 270831 B gzip. The additional 25896 B gzip retains complete tree/SVM inference, topology validation and calibrated probabilities in the same optional per-model Wasm owner; splitting would add another ABI and attribute/resource lifetime bridge. Core plus stage remains 24209 B.

## Batch 175 job 4: series
Optional /series uses 1 MiB network chunks, 512 MiB per encoded/decoded block, 100M rows by default (override reader limits), and at most uint32 original row IDs. Exact selection retains loaded binary64 blocks; it is not constant-total-memory storage. Flat scalar Arrow/Parquet limits and codecs match /table. M4 is exact for the aliased pixel-column line model, not arbitrary antialiasing/thick-line blending. Min-max/LTTB are alternatives; LTTB defaults to retaining pixel extrema too. NaN gaps split lines and can exceed the usual four-vertices-per-column output. Spectra require finite uniform samples, explicit sample rate and 2..16777216 values. STFT defaults to 256-sample periodic Hann, half-window hop, mean removal, complete windows, 256 MiB output bound and one-window GPU staging. HTTP sources need valid 206 byte ranges and immutable versions; Range/CORS headers must be exposed. Details, defaults and physical PSD normalization: docs/sciviz-series.md. No speed claim.

The bytes preserve one coherent reader/data/selection/spectral lifecycle instead of a split requiring applications to duplicate state. Core plus stage remains 24209 B before and after.
