On 2026-11-25 the worker measures 41,108 B gzip and 109,131 B raw, up from 40,935 and 108,708 B, and its test ceilings
are 41,200 and 109,300 B. The whole difference is each paint layer's own blend width (`PaintLayer.ecotone`,
`ec34c7f3be`): without it a 2 m painted hedge is averaged across the world's 24 m ecotone and almost vanishes. The
classification's paint feather runs on every tile a worker makes, so a separate worker file would be loaded by every
painted world.

## Terrain relief lighting (2026-11-23)

The optional relief-lighting entry adds 8 bytes per height sample for a filterable RGBA16F bake, about 8 MiB
for a 1,024×1,024 map. The heightmap is borrowed. One 48-byte uniform buffer is released after the submitted
bake finishes. Each bake takes up to 32 sky azimuths plus the directional sun and 256 samples per ray, bounded
by the configured radius and the heightmap edge. The lit draw adds one bilinear lookup. The bake captures a
single sun direction and a static heightmap. Changing either needs `rebake()`. A heightfield cannot represent
overhangs, and distant features between samples may be missed.
## Open-ocean horizon depth (2026-11-23)

Water with `horizon: true` keeps the scene far plane for its displaced grid. Its flat extension reaches 10,000 km
in each world-horizontal axis from the snapped grid center and covers only rays beyond the original far plane.
Depth there is reversed-Z zero, the same as the sky. It supports the existing Water colour and reflection passes.
It adds four vertices and six indices to the same draw and uses no new buffer, texture, pass or package option.
The horizon remains a flat ocean approximation. See [GPU evidence](architecture/operational-playbook.md#section-5-evidence-open-ocean-horizon-depth-2026-11-23).
Blob and planar shadows (`@margoengine/materials/fake-shadows`, 2026-11-25): the planar shadow projects on the CPU in `update` (cost grows with the caster's vertex count, so characters and props, not levels); it flattens onto one plane, does not follow terrain, and overlapping parts of one caster darken twice (translucent blend, no stencil); with a point light, keep the caster between the light and the plane. The blob is a vertex-alpha disc, not a blurred render of the caster's silhouette. Drawn pixels are checked on a real GPU, WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer (`node packages/materials/test/features-browser.mjs fakeShadows`, 2026-11-25): along a blob spoke every pixel is within 3 of 255 of 1 - opacity x the rings' alpha (measured within 0.5), and the planar shadow of a square under a directional and a point light covers exactly the footprint the light projects, at 1 - opacity. No core change.


## Grade tonal ranges (`@margoengine/tonemap/grade` `ranges`, 2026-11-25)

Enforced per range (global, shadows, midtones, highlights): hue 0..360, density 0..1, saturation 0..4, exposure -8..8
stops. Applied to display-linear 0..1 after the primaries and before the wheels, clamped after the gain and after the
saturation; the three tonal ranges mix by the wheels' luminance masks, which are not adjustable. The tint keeps the
luminance of a grey before clipping, not of a saturated colour, and a negative density is not accepted (turn the hue by
180). No settings-table rows. Compiled only while a range changes something. GPU frames are within 1.02 levels of a CPU
oracle on WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer (`tests/grade-browser.mjs`). Measured min+gzip: grade 1,877 to 2,426 B, hue 2,596
to 3,158 B, export-cube 1,360 to 1,431 B, 3dl 2,367 to 2,434 B; core and stage source unchanged. Controls as named in
the Babylon.js `ColorCurves` API documentation (no source read), 2026,
https://doc.babylonjs.com/typedoc/classes/BABYLON.ColorCurves; the maths is Margo's own (HSV hexcone, A. R. Smith,
"Color Gamut Transform Pairs", SIGGRAPH 1978, https://doi.org/10.1145/800248.807361).
Scene helpers (`@margoengine/scene/helpers`, 2026-11-25): `worldBounds`, `center` and `resize` read every vertex of every mesh under the root on each call (call them when the model loads, not every frame); a mesh with no geometry is skipped, and `center` moves `root.position`, which is in the parent's space (equal to world space under an unrotated, unscaled parent). `resize` scales uniformly and multiplies `root.scale`. `float` writes `position.y` and the three rotation angles from the values the mesh had when it was created, so do not animate those yourself meanwhile. `InteractionPrompt` is timing only: you draw the hint. Accepted difference from drei: functions you call, not React components that re-render.

## Recorded frames as a texture (2026-11-25, GAP-FILM-VIDEOTEX)

`@margoengine/video/frames` `FrameVideo` takes straight-alpha sRGB RGBA8 frames from the caller, 1 to 16384 pixels a
side (the GPU's `maxTextureDimension2D` also limits it), and puts the frame of a film time in a materials `Texture`.
One frame is held on the CPU and one texture per device (mip chain included). Each new frame uploads the whole picture
and regenerates the chain; upload cost is not measured. It decodes no video: ffmpeg or another decoder gives the pixels.
Materials and glTF PBR meshes only. Measured: `packages/video/test/frames-gpu.mjs` (Node, WebGPU) reads four frames of
a 64 x 48 clip and a four-frame `renderFrames` sequence back within 1 level of the source, a seek back gives the same
bytes, and a quarter-size draw of a black and white checker reads 188 (the linear-light average);
`frames-check.mjs` draws the frames on WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer within 2 levels, as a map and as a glowing screen.
UV transform centre (`uvTransform.center`, `@margoengine/materials`, 2026-11-25): applies to `new Material({ uvTransform })` and `setUVTransform`; it folds into the offset, so `transformUVs`, the atlas packer and `setUVTransformAt` on instances still take a plain `KHR_texture_transform` without `center`. Metaballs (`Metaballs`, `@margoengine/procedural`, 2026-11-25): each `geometry()` call re-polygonizes the whole grid on the CPU (resolution up to 128 per axis, the marching-cubes limit), so a 40-cube grid per frame is fine and a 128-cube grid is not; the pull is the finite-support cubic of Wyvill et al., not three.js's 1/d^2, so a ball's surface radius is under its `radius`. 3MF layered textures (`multiproperties` with several texture layers) are still not read: one texture per group.

### Thermal conduction (`@margoengine/physics/thermal`, FIRE-06)

The heat grid is Cartesian and cell-centred, with isotropic conductivity and piecewise constant sensible heat capacity. Phase change is isothermal and of fixed volume. Exterior faces support insulation, fixed temperature, convection using half-cell and film resistances in series, diffuse-grey radiation to fixed-temperature surroundings, and prescribed heat flux.

The solver and scratch regions occupy 136 bytes per cell and a 40-byte geometry record in world memory. Backward Euler adds 8 bytes of scratch per cell. A grid with radiating faces adds another 8 bytes per cell and 40 bytes per radiating face. The field registry adds its mirrors and any accumulated sources. The solver supports plain and shared Wasm memory with SIMD. Each solver instance uses a 64 KiB stack region in world memory. The solver chooses the world rate from the finite-volume diffusion bound and subdivides a tick when needed. The numerical limits follow the world's Wasm address space and the kernel's u32 subdivision count. Forward Euler uses a step diffusion number at most 1/2. Backward Euler subdivides above 2 to bound the stationary iteration's convergence rate. Very stiff large grids still need a scalable sparse solve. The optional entry measures 6,684 B gzip. Each of its two lazy Wasm builds measures 12,160 B raw and 5,120 B gzip. A browser without shared memory support loads the plain build.

Thermoelasticity solves quasistatic small-strain equilibrium in a bonded solid on the same Cartesian grid. Each
cell is decomposed into six tetrahedra, with a common per-cell temperature and isotropic elastic properties. The
solid takes prescribed nodal displacements and has zero traction on free surfaces. Coupling is one-way from the
heat grid. A supplied liquid-fraction field rejects any positive melt fraction. Plastic flow, fracture and stresses
within a fluid are outside this elastic model.

Before alignment and the registry's mirrors, the elastic solver uses 136 bytes per cell, 65 bytes per nodal degree
of freedom, and a 72-byte geometry record. The grid count is limited by the Wasm address space. A solve fails before
publishing new mechanical results when the residual remains above the requested tolerance after its iteration budget.

Heat haze accepts a temperature volume with the device's 3D texture dimension limit and one r32float texel per
cell. The field fades to ambient at its exterior sample centres. The optional path uses a single reference
wavelength, fixed local pressure, small-angle deflection along the camera ray, and the frame's existing colour
and opaque depth. The effect samples the displaced colour inside the frame. Off-screen background
and light paths that require large-angle or multiple refraction are outside this screen-space model. The heat-haze entry grows from 11,008 B to 13,299 B gzip for volume upload, ray integration and lifetime management.

The shared sparse solver for stiff heat grids and the original kiln and turbofan scene integrations remain open.


## Collective animal motion

`@margoengine/physics/schooling` uses a deterministic grid over local coordinates, with f64 distance and
field rows. A rank limit applies only to neighbours within the outer radius and the visible sector. The
model assumes a predator holds velocity over the prediction horizon. Dense groups or very large sensing
radii increase the number of candidates. The kernel uses world memory and a private per-instance arena region
for its stack, static data, and grid work. Its capacity grows with the number of configured members.
Membership and port layout stay fixed for a solver's lifetime. Use a fresh world setup for a different row layout.

The point-mass model represents inertial mass, thrust and quadratic drag. Its local curvature bound concerns
propulsive acceleration relative to the medium. A spatially varying current can also bend the trajectory.
Body bending, contact, wing lift, flap power and tail propulsion belong to the body solver. The intent
fixture verifies the field hand-off and a bank derived from lateral acceleration. The original film shots
still need playback checks.

The optional entry is 4,998 B gzip. The plain SIMD kernel is 4,464 B gzip (8,622 B raw). The shared variant is 4,523 B gzip (8,710 B raw).
That budget covers the field adapter and the point-mass mode in one import. Core and stage gain zero bytes.

## Rooted plant mechanics (BIO-01)

The optional vegetation kernel integrates two small-angle transverse modes about one upright root. The crown is a
distributed load and mass on the stem. The model has fixed geometry, no branch topology, axial motion, finite-angle
reconfiguration, growth or reciprocal flow feedback. The effect of a fluid is integrated at three stations on each
element, and stem rupture is checked at nine cross-sections. A fluid sampler supplies density and velocity in the same
origin cell. Deep-water Airy motion in the coupling test is a supplied field. Mixed media can use separate plant
solvers; the sampled `medium` determines the default added mass and whether buoyancy is computed. Kernel execution
requires Wasm SIMD. The plain and shared builds use the same layout in module slot 3, with a separate stack per
instance. The dry model is checked against the uniform clamped–free solution.
The optional physics entry is 9,402 B min+gzip. Each Wasm build is 6,456 B, or 2,226 B gzip. Loading on a
shared-memory host prepares both builds so the same solver API can use either world memory type.
The optional scatter entry is 2,248 B min+gzip. The measured core + stage gzip remains 24,820 B on Windows.

`@margoengine/scatter/plant-motion` copies four modal displacements per plant to a 32-byte GPU record and maps
instances to one root per selected X/Z cell. Bin indices and displacement use float32 for rendering. The input
root and mesh pivot need to share a cell, and the rendered reach must fit Scatter's culling radius. A zero-strength
Scatter wind enables its existing doubled reach while the solver poses mapped roots. The normal transform
uses the derivative of the same displacement as the colour, depth and shadow geometry.

The rigid adapter uses a fixed standing trunk proxy, so the rigid impact sees a fixed obstacle until release. It
passes normal impulse to the bending modes at the stored contact heights. A released stem uses one authored rigid
geometry with the pose and velocity of its detached chord. Release needs a preallocated dynamic fragment at the
matching section height. Scatter can hide the entire failed instance when a separate body draws the fragment.

### Catchment runoff (HYDRO-02, 2026-11-25)

`@margoengine/physics/runoff` uses fixed directed drainage links and one active soil-water layer per cell.
The surface rating assumes a wide Manning section. Use the shallow-water solver for backwater, reversed flow
and two-dimensional inundation at an outlet. The next soil step takes up routed water left upstream or downstream
by the current routing step. Climate-only BiomeView flows use a quantized local climate representative of the
contributing area. Event hydrographs use the live field. Calibrated flood return periods must come from separate
hydraulic runs or from measurements.

The optional runoff entry is 3,906 B min+gzip. Its lazy SIMD Wasm images are 7,311 B for plain memory and 7,402 B
for shared memory before HTTP compression. Both preserve the existing world arena outside their reserved section.

### Aquatic locomotion (`@margoengine/physics/life`, LIFE-03)

The linearly implicit swimmer treats mass and inertia as an ellipsoid with semi-empirical resistance and
potential-flow strip added mass. Use it for slender-body tail propulsion, pectoral steering/sculling, neutral
or ballasted bodies, free-surface crossing and stationary control in an ambient flow. It uses local sea
elevation and slope for wet volume and its centroid. Added inertia scales with wetted fraction. It approximates
potential flow near the swimmer with one material acceleration sample at the submerged centroid. Breaking
waves, slamming and vortices layered on the emitted wake impulse require water-side consumers. Thin-body
forces are cycle-averaged and omit a resolved fluke vortex sheet. Use a wetted mesh or geometric profile to
supply the true skin area if it differs materially from the ellipsoid. Skin deformation is prescribed by an
ellipsoid-weighted centreline with a separate contact field for articulated segment loads.
The optional JavaScript entry measures 7,286 B gzip. The plain and shared Wasm assets measure 6,410 B and 6,501 B raw. Shared memory and
browser use require a runtime with Wasm SIMD. The ordinary page path loads plain Wasm.

## Falling plates, winged seeds and hail (AERO-05)

The plate model uses the 2005 Andersen, Pesavento and Wang quasi-steady coefficients for the intermediate-Re
measurements (about 100–1,000). It represents an elliptical cross section, a fixed rotation axis and a separate
spanwise drag term. The autorotating wing model resolves three translation axes and spin about a fixed axis.
The authored wing strips have rigid pitch and coning is zero. Airflow is sampled once per body per world tick at
the predicted midpoint. The fluid is prescribed and neither model reconstructs the shed wake.

Sphere contact is one-way against fixed, nonsensor geometry. The swept chord approximates the curved path over
one world tick, and contact applies normal restitution without a tangential friction law. Plates and seeds are
airborne models. Shape casts and Hail drawing use float32 in their respective coordinate frames. The physics
solver has f64 state and uses local dyadic RK4 substeps with a relative/absolute defect target of 1e-8.
The kernel requires Wasm SIMD. Its plain and shared variants occupy static window slot 7, with per-instance stacks.

The optional Hail source reads one 32-byte vertex-storage record per visible stone on WebGPU. The batch is
created at setup. Supply a world-scale placement and advance the world before rendering. Camera-wrapped
emission, chip splashes and collision-driven emission are independent effects. The world-stepped draw uses
the supplied diameter, positions and velocities.

The optional falling entry measures 6,259 B min+gzip. Each lazy Wasm build is 10,109 B,
4,273 B gzip. The Hail overlay measures 5,443 B and its optional world adapter 1,056 B min+gzip.
Core and stage remain at 24,820 B min+gzip combined.

### Sediment transport and bed change (HYDRO-03, 2026-11-25)

`@margoengine/physics/sediment` works on one co-located rectangular TerrainBed and shallow-water grid. It uses a
representative bed diameter and a representative suspended diameter for dilute transport. The bank model uses
local near-bank velocity relative to the wet reach mean with user-supplied erodibility and optional root stress.
The vertex reserve covers the mobile layer the caller declares. Set it to the bedrock clearance when TerrainBed
has a floor. Fluid momentum and bed evolution exchange one field update per world tick. An open boundary exports
sediment; external inflow at that edge carries clear water. Use the source grid's same rectangle for Flood tint.

The optional sediment entry measures 5,256 B min+gzip. The plain and shared SIMD Wasm files are 12,483 B and
12,571 B before HTTP compression. The Flood entry measures 14,457 B min+gzip with the concentration upload.

### Pedestrian contact and crowd motion (LIFE-05)

`@margoengine/physics/pedestrians` models horizontal translation, finite shoulder turn rate, and
a specified ground height. Its uniformly oriented ellipses give an analytic projected footprint.
An approximate support along the line of centres is used for ellipse pairs. It computes the normal
and sliding impulse once per broadphase pair in canonical order. The density response is locally
compressible. The open approach uses the measured time-to-collision power law with a finite reaction
offset. The solver raises the dyadic rate so ideally dt·√(2k/m)≤1/2 for the lightest body and travel
per tick stays inside half the shortest footprint radius. Multi-floor surfaces use separate groups or
walkable route guidance with a height sampler. Injury, fall and ragdoll transitions use external
consumers of the force/pose ports. Doorway and terrain fixtures use simulated actors and route geometry.
The optional JavaScript entry is 4,590 B gzip. The plain and shared Wasm assets are 12,041 B and 12,129 B raw.

### Landscape evolution (HYDRO-04)

`LandscapeEvolution` uses one rectangular TerrainBed, a linear stream-power slope exponent and a fixed downhill
graph within each step. Closed depressions trap incoming sediment. Route floodwater, lake overtopping and rapid
flows with the shallow-water solver. Specified open edges supply fixed elevations and accept downhill export.

The solver can estimate equilibrium Manning depth or consume a time-averaged shear field. Its independently
transported size classes share one bed porosity. The model tracks changing loose material and parent fractions,
with no hiding or exposure correction between grain classes. Thermal erosional transfer uses a parameterised
repose slope and coefficient. Weathering rates and rooted cohesion vary by terrain and must be supplied for
site predictions. The loose sediment field excludes material brought by external bed writers unless it is
initially supplied.

Bed changes are accrued in f64 and become TerrainBed elevations on the following tick. The geometry used to
choose downhill directions comes from the shared f32 bed field. The biomes snapshot rounds the current terrain
to millimetres and keeps the relief's authored river lines. Use fixed boundary elevations if a snapshot must join
unchanged terrain outside the simulated rectangle.

The optional Physics and Biomes landscape entries measure 4,347 B and 614 B min+gzip respectively. The
plain and shared SIMD files are 12,166 B and 12,254 B before HTTP compression.

### Utility passes (`@margoengine/post`: `kawase-blur`, `lut1d`, `color-average`, `depth-downsample`, 2026-11-25)

WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer. KawaseBlur: an HDR PostStack stage; `levels` 1..8, `offsets` 1..32 values of 0..64,
`scale` 0..8, `resolutionScale` 0.0625..1; not an exact Gaussian (the presets match its sigma within 15% up to
`very-large`), small bright points can flicker at a low working size, its `texture` is the reduced image of the last view
drawn. LUT1D: 2..65536 entries, linear interpolation, input clamped to the domain, display values only (use
`Tonemap.setLUT` for 3D and HDR-side grading); a texture source must have a linear format. ColorAverage: display values;
the overlay blend modes. DepthDownsample: single-sample reversed-Z source, output from 1/16 of the source size up to it;
`'representative'` is the median of at most 4 x 4 texels of the footprint; reading the stack's resolved depth needs an
order after 30. GPU cost of none of them measured.

## Playground

The playground page (`site/playground/`, [docs/playground.md](playground.md)), 2026-11-26:

- A share link's `#code=` holds at most 65,536 characters (`MAX_LINK_CHARS`) and expands to at most 262,144 bytes of
  UTF-8 code (`MAX_CODE_BYTES`); longer code is refused with a message to download it instead. Browsers and servers
  cap URL length separately; the hash never reaches the server.
- The version history keeps the newest 30 snapshots (`MAX_SNAPSHOTS`) in this browser's `localStorage`. When storage
  is full the oldest go first; where storage is blocked (some private windows) versions last only until the tab closes.
- The console keeps the last 500 lines; each message is cut to 4,000 characters.
- An error's line is read from the stack frame of the code's blob module (or the error event for it); an error thrown
  inside a package, or one with no stack, shows no line.
- A project holds at most 12 files (`MAX_FILES`), named with letters, digits, `-` and `_` then `.js` (32 characters
  before the extension); the 256 KiB cap is for all files together. Only `./name.js` imports of the project's own files
  are linked; a path into a folder (`./lib/x.js`) is not.
- On margoengine.com the page loads the import map of `margoengine@1.0.0` from jsDelivr, which works once the packages
  are published on npm (they are not yet: the catalog lists 0 of 108 published). Until then, run it against a checkout
  with `npm run playground` and `?packages=/node_modules/`.
- Download HTML gives the run frame with the code built in; it loads the packages from the same place as the page did,
  so a file downloaded from a local run needs that local server.
- The API panel lists top-level exports only (no class members, no full type checking, no inferred types), read from
  at most 120 `.d.ts` files per run, 20 imported entries and 400 names each; a declaration's line is cut at 300
  characters and its doc at its first sentence.
- The embed (`/playground/embed/`) saves nothing in the browser and has no templates, versions, sharing or download;
  its Open in Playground link carries the files only while they fit a share link (256 KiB, 64 KiB of link).
- The glTF template loads the Khronos Box sample from raw.githubusercontent.com, so it needs the network.

## Contact and modal sound (SOUND-04)

Modal material presets contain authored resonances for a wood object, metal object, glass object and bell.
Use measured modes and gains for a specific object. Each rigid radiator uses one bank with effective
point-independent gain. The mono output is dry normalized PCM with linear superposition. Use a listener
for spatial transfer and a mixer for headroom. The snapshot includes the retained sample history.

Rigid contacts use the total normal impulse for a step, the last manifold's point weights, and relative
motion at those points. Impacts use the pre-step approach speed. A contact that forms and disappears
between published rigid steps may lack point data. With the current rigid interface, transients are
placed at the first sample of the observed range. Source timing is bounded by one rigid step on a matched
clock. The scrape and roll spectra use effective roughness profiles. Acoustic microcontact feedback, exact
geometry-dependent roughness, and elastic radiation into the room require additional field models.
The optional joint route computes equivalent scalar fracture excitation from supplied energy and mass.
A brittle-fracture producer can publish per-track excitation in the same field layout.

The optional entry measures 9,736 bytes gzip. Its plain and shared Wasm files each measure 1,567 bytes
raw, fetched only when the caller loads the solver.

### Radiation fog and cold-air pooling (ATMO-08)

The cold-air layer resolves one vertical bulk temperature, velocity and droplet population per ground column.
It models near-surface nocturnal radiation fog, valley pooling and exchange with overlying air. Its pressure and
ambient weather inputs are held per coupling step. The grey longwave boundary does not resolve spectral radiation.
The bulk fall speed uses small spherical liquid droplets. Multiple radiative strata, aerosol activation, supercooled
phase changes and synoptic weather require their own field models. Open edges export the layer. Sealed edges retain
it while settling and external surface inputs exchange water with the ground.

The visual grid interpolates extinction horizontally and uses the bulk column thickness vertically. Its storage is
16 bytes per column plus the 48-byte header, limited by the device's storage binding and buffer sizes. Analytic fog
volumes and the live grid each work as an optional `VolumetricFog` medium.
The optional solver is 4,666 bytes gzip with an 8,955-byte lazy Wasm asset per memory mode. The optional
fog renderer is 2,243 bytes gzip.

### Layered snowpack (ICE-01)

The model resolves a vertical column for each sample, with a fresh surface layer and the configured initial layers.
It represents freeze/thaw, surface-settling overburden, pairwise conduction, capillary storage and gravity drainage.
It uses bulk density and viscosity. Grain metamorphism, vapor diffusion and hydraulic travel time through the pack
require more state. The optional Weather renderer consumes the stored ground and snow depth directly.

Snow drift uses local near-surface wind and the flux capacity of adjacent columns, with closed lateral boundaries.
The overhang stores a labeled fraction of the rim mass and gives a direction and extension at its specified density
and thickness. It represents accretion and scouring. Fracturing a three-dimensional cornice requires a structural
model. The slab field reports a static interface safety factor, with no assessment of fracture propagation.
Weather's blocked footprints and drag act on the dense avalanche layer. The powder cloud is transported separately.

The optional snowpack entry is 5,737 B min+gzip. Its plain and shared Wasm variants are each 6,455 B raw. The
Weather avalanche entry is 7,195 B min+gzip with its obstacle terms.

### Dune and snow transport (EARTH-07)

The solver resolves a single grain material and a mobile surface layer on the uniform `TerrainBed` grid.
Set `mobileDepth` to the available layer above bedrock. Coarse grids describe dune evolution. For impact ripples,
supply `ripples.meanHop` and put multiple vertices inside a typical ripple wavelength. The short-hop model uses one
material and a fixed wind-relative incident angle. Suspension, snow cohesion changes and multi-grain sorting require
additional models. In an explicit world the latest bed change
may be in flight for one base step. Other contributors sharing the bed need to coordinate their erodible depths.

Open sides export saltating grains and closed sides retain them. The mass ledger reports mobile bed, airborne grains,
dust and open-boundary export. Snow uses a seasonal threshold and optional exposure. Wind stress and dust use exported
surface fields. Atmosphere feedback needs an ATMO-01 momentum sink and ATMO-06 dust receiver on the matching grid.
The rendering entry uses the current ground and transport field, and maps moving mass to opacity with `referenceMass`.
The optional physics entry is 5,633 B min+gzip. Its separate plain and shared Wasm variants are each 8,172 B raw.
The rendering entry, with its live transport route, is 11,061 B min+gzip.

### Groundwater and springs (HYDRO-06)

Use an unconfined aquifer with one active horizontal layer. Darcy conductance is integrated over the saturated
overlap and held during each implicit tick. Opposite face transfers conserve liquid volume. The water table follows
the terrain if bound. A drain below the aquifer floor is limited to that floor. Surface level limits saturated
storage and excess leaves as seepage. Springs and seepage supply the shallow-water solver in one direction.
Specify a physical groundwater time scale appropriate to the rate at which the saturated thickness changes.

Detailed unsaturated pressure and moisture profiles, multiple aquifer layers and surface-water backflow through
spring openings are outside this model. HYDRO-02 calculates recharge through the active soil.

The optional JavaScript entry measures 3,939 B min+gzip. Both Wasm variants are 11,142 B before HTTP compression.

### Grounded glacier and ice-sheet flow (ICE-02)

The rectangular x-z grid resolves isothermal, grounded, no-slip ice with the shallow-ice approximation,
a constant Glen exponent of 3, and constant or per-cell climatic inputs. It uses the world's gravity
component along the vertical axis. External edges are closed to ice. Horizontal stress transmission,
basal sliding and lubrication, floating shelves and evolving bed topography are outside this model.
At an open-water boundary, waterline or flotation failure removes a whole grid cell's ice. Dry cliff
release needs full crevasse penetration. Resolve the terminus with smaller cells for smaller events.
The volume ports support downstream motion and impact solvers.

The step lags the nonlinear face weight and uses a symmetric backward-Euler solve with a relative
residual norm target of √(f64 machine epsilon). The initial residual is evaluated from differences
in surface elevation. Limit accelerated time steps for accuracy on steep or rapidly evolving terrain.
D8 drains each source to an outlet or local depression during the same tick. It represents no
routing delay, subglacial storage or lake spill. Discharge is in m³ per world second even if the ice
runs on accelerated physical time.

The optional entry is 3,519 B min+gzip with a 3,775 B ceiling. Plain and shared Wasm are 15,437 B
and 15,525 B raw, or 6,189 B and 6,250 B gzip. A solver reserves 260 B of arena and scratch per cell,
144 B of fixed config and budget, and a 64 KiB instance stack. Core and stage together stay at
24,820 B gzip.

### Ground animal locomotion (LIFE-02)

`@margoengine/physics/locomotion` hosts independent body rows, with a one-dimensional clocked chain for a snake
and fixed world-space stance contacts for lizards, insects, spiders and crabs. Each legged animal has an additional
torso contact. Body state uses 112 B per row, published contact uses 104 B per element, and three f64 foothold
values per element are part of replay. Both optional modules import the same world memory and use one static
slot and a 64 KiB arena stack per solver instance. The world rate ranges from 60 to 7,680 Hz; extreme stiffness,
damping or gait frequencies that require faster stepping are reported when configuring the group. Storage scales
with the configured body and contact counts.

The snake's motion uses a planar travelling wave across a heightfield and yaw about world up. The compiled leg
templates use a single rigid torso and massless compressive legs, with stick-phase anchors and contact forces
limited by the ground friction cone. These models resolve terrain height and contact normals. A terrain with
caves or overhanging holds needs a collider-based foot placement system. The pose/contact ports expose
kinematics and reaction wrenches for downstream animation or an erosion consumer. Inter-animal collision and
feedback into the live terrain require downstream coupling.

The optional entry measures 17,194 B raw and 6,926 B gzip. The plain Wasm is 10,782 B raw and 4,873 B gzip. The shared Wasm is 10,870 B raw and 4,937 B gzip.

## Material ageing (BIO-04)

State is one uniform column per material patch. Atmospheric loss uses ISO 9223 annual inputs
and the ISO 9224 carbon steel or copper average curves. Instantaneous local climates are a
piecewise-constant equivalent-exposure approximation when used in these empirical annual curves.
Current density sets uniform immersion attack. Localized pits, galvanic pairs, coatings
with delamination or adhesion, and loss of a structure's load capacity require extra models.

Wood decay represents untreated pine sapwood at 0–30 °C and at least 95% RH. The exposed wood
model uses that calibration. Wood loss is expressed as equivalent thickness at unchanged surface area
and density. The immersion fraction suppresses atmospheric pine decay. Marine fouling is one
aggregate population limited by free area, with caller-provided rates to distinguish conditions.
Submerged loss of wood by marine borers is outside the fit.

Limestone models carbonate dissolution from incident water and an optional dry deposition term.
Physical exfoliation and freeze-thaw are separate effects. The appearance result uses per-patch
diffuse layer transport for the metal colors and a coverage mix for the aggregate fouling.
The material consumes linear PBR values. Multi-spectral gloss, grain, individual corrosion
pits and run-off streak geometry require authored patch variation or other algorithms.

The optional Physics ageing entry measures 4,922 bytes gzip.

### Iceberg rigid-body dynamics and calving (ICE-03)

The optional 60 Hz solver handles homogeneous rectangular solids with exact planar hydrostatic
loads, six degrees of freedom, quadratic normal-pressure drag and prescribed wet-face recession.
It uses dyadic substeps from hydrostatic stiffness, rotation, and drag. The ablation step moves the
centre of mass with the shape. It preserves lost solid volume in the freshwater budget at
1000 kg/m³. Release sources and WakeSolver must publish at the same 60 Hz and use one origin cell.
A WakeSolver receives two area-scaled patches per changing body and gives the linear wave response.

Wind and water currents are each uniform and use the still-water plane. The model excludes large
wave feedback on the body, fragment collisions, grounding and sea-ice resistance. Calving sites
have explicitly allocated body rows, with queued volumes retained across snapshots when full.
The optional iceberg entry measures 5,162 B gzip with a 5,418 B ceiling. The plain and shared
assets each measure 9,128 B raw and 4,318 B gzip. Physics/sea measures 7,745 B gzip
with the field reader, with an 8,001 B ceiling. Core plus stage remains 24,820 B gzip.

### Live forest ecosystem (BIO-03)

The forest entry is 7,194 B gzip and each optional Wasm variant is 1,276 B raw. The shared annual implementation
raises the offline ecosystem entry from 3,210 B to 3,652 B gzip. Core and stage stay at 24,820 B gzip.

The optional `@margoengine/biomes/forest` advances individual crowns with millimetre radii, centimetre positions
within 100 km of the origin and Q16 competition. Default capacity is 16,384 trees including snags. Set capacity for
a plot with `limit`, up to the offline model's one million trees. The annual transition uses one grid of crown
neighbours sized to twice capacity or the next power of two. Native workspace bytes scale as four times
`(capacity + 3 * tableSize)`, with a further four per capacity row for shade output. Native scratch is rebuilt
each year and shared between releases only through the world's arena. World state holds 44 bytes per tree slot for
population and permanent lean. The annual grid holds four f64 channels per patch plus one duration per distinct
species flood depth. Match extent and origin with water, landscape and snow readers.

The patch placement approximation bins an entire crown at its stem. Cover is the sum of projected crown shares
limited to unity. Fuel sums individual crown mass so overlapping live crowns still carry fuel. The wind rule
updates the crown axis in proportion to new projected area. It represents long-term flagging by changing the crown
axis rather than tracking individual branches or modelling physiological dormancy, burial or ice damage. Flood
tolerance represents measured depth and duration for one species and life stage. The burn and fuel-moisture input
is an explicit versioned port. Cover, roots and canopy fuel update at annual boundaries.

### Grounded biped and quadruped gait (LIFE-01)

The optional `@margoengine/physics/legged` entry and the ground-animal entry share the same slot-13 SIMD module.
Each moving body has 16 B of stored target, 40 B of gait state and two or four persistent foot contact points,
plus the torso. A deck uses its declared planar rectangular support and the rigid body's pose. The projected COM
sets the approximation for angularly varying contact-surface velocity. A highly articulated surface needs a
contactable support-patch field. Planting and flight follow a reduced spring-mass model with a finite support
couple. The renderer's baked export clips keep a single pace for each clip, while runtime horse posing uses the
actual instantaneous stride.

The legged entry measures 29,240 B raw and 11,101 B gzip and shares the ground kernel bytes listed above.
Horses measures 40,737 B raw and 16,724 B gzip. Its gait utilities measure 2,738 B raw and 1,266 B gzip.

### Pack ice and floe contact (ICE-04)

Planar circular floes have constant mass, a shrinking level-ice footprint and conserved raft and
ridge volumes. The pile is a subgrid volume on the originating floe. Independent ridge blocks,
finger rafting, bending under waves, welds between floes and shoreline grounding require explicit
geometry outside this model. The deterministic contact sweep approximates multiple simultaneous
contacts. Vessel bounds are horizontal waterline capsules and send XZ impulse and yaw torque to
the rigid world. The method resolves broken pack ice rather than applying a continuous-sheet
resistance regression. The Water adapter displays equivalent thickness and a water-surface tangent.

The optional Physics entry measures 5,112 B gzip with a 5,368 B ceiling. Each lazy Wasm asset uses 5,716 B raw and 2,534 B gzip. Water/ice measures 13,297 B gzip with a 13,364 B ceiling. Core plus stage stays at 24,820 B gzip.

### Crush response for civilian barriers (BREAK-03)

Station-level input curves represent creased plating, rail absorbers, or road crumple members. Each station resolves a normal load-release event during one 60 Hz coupling interval. Peak compression is a ledger and pose input, while the rigid integrator receives its net impulse. Use distinct contact pairs and exclude their ordinary rigid response during the crush event. The reduced model uses measured backing and ignores shear and sustained contact. A separately coupled seakeeping hull keeps its water loads, and dynamic added mass during the short crush event needs an effective-inertia port. The seal field reports a caller-calibrated stroke threshold. Below-deck ingress requires geometry and a compartment consumer. The optional crush package entry measures 8120 B minified and 3507 B gzip. Core and Stage gain zero bytes.

### Lubrication films on moving surfaces (FLUID-07)

A depth column assumes a film thin compared with the distance it varies over. The model fits
water rivulets, flattening droplets and puddle margins. One film patch has planar orthogonal
coordinates and can carry a sampled substrate height. Viscous shear is held at its midpoint
over each coupling interval. Strongly curved glass needs multiple patches and flying splash
droplets need a separate ballistic solver. Rim coalescence is by the shared depth field.
The film accepts registered impact events and transfers their pressure to a local wake, while
the film keeps their deposited water. Normal pressure acts along the supported side of the
surface. Detaching films, contact-angle dynamics on a steep drop, thin-film interference and
general rain damping of ocean waves are outside this equation.

The optional thin-film entry is 5,917 B gzip with a 6,173 B ceiling. Both Wasm assets are 9,209 B raw and each is 3,995 B gzip. Core plus stage remains 24,820 B gzip.

### Environmental airborne transport (ATMO-06)

The optional `@margoengine/physics/airborne` advances mineral dust, freshwater mist and sea spray at 240 Hz.
Source parcels represent many physical particles. Each parcel holds 16 f64 words in the arena. Sources retain
pending mass and get round-robin emission turns when the parcel allocation is full. Both native builds are
610 B raw. The optional entry is 8,260 B gzip. Core plus stage remains 24,820 B gzip. The portable and shared variants use the same SIMD arithmetic and import the world memory without
an initial static region.

The drag law is for rounded particles in environmental air. The Stokes option checks Re ≤ 0.1; the default
uses a transitional correlation and a constant-drag large-particle approximation. Wind and drag are held during
one 1/240 s interval, so gradients are resolved at the local query rate. Homogeneous turbulence approaches the
specified variance from a zero initial fluctuation. The wet-droplet evaporation model is diffusion-limited with
prescribed humidity and a salt-dependent equilibrium diameter. It conserves the dry sea salt remaining after water loss. Mixed atmospheric chemistry,
collisions between droplets and two-way air heating need separate fields. Deposition tests use heightfield
subdivision at half the smallest horizontal cell width; the aggregate ledger retains the mass.

### Developmental wood growth (BIO-02)

The parametric solver places shoots on 60 Hz season boundaries and stores permanent branch structure. The initialization footprint follows the supplied productive seasons and the minimum extension per new branch. The light grid uses cubic voxels with a vertical, distance-attenuated penumbra and horizontal light-seeking gradient. Sites outside the supplied grid receive open light. Roots use a measured water threshold and the mean storage in their own supplied HYDRO-02 cell. The model has no water extraction, leaf anatomy, root branching or moving obstructors. Renderer-adapted coordinates are f32 within an origin cell. The optional growth entry measures 12,386 B minified and 5,474 B gzip. The selected lazy SIMD kernel is 601 B raw in either memory mode. Core and Stage gain zero bytes.

### Enclosed and urban acoustics (SOUND-02)

`@margoengine/physics/room-sound` separates finite specular paths from a linear low-frequency wave field.
Paths accept convex planar faces and trace direct and reflected segments through the requested order, default two.
The bounded search reports when its candidate image budget is exceeded. The ray gains are relative to a one-metre
monopole and keep pressure signs. Their fractional sample impulses use two-point interpolation.

The native scheme has cubic voxels and one real reflection coefficient per air cell at its closed faces.
Normal-incidence wall admittance is exact in the model. Grazing and mixed-frequency impedance need finer
geometry or a richer material boundary. For an axis wave resolved with ten cells per wavelength, the
sinusoidal stencil bounds numerical phase speed from below by 1 − π²/600 of the configured speed.
Use a finer grid for higher frequencies. The data-free plain and shared variants each measure 753 B raw.
The optional entry measures 5,758 B gzip. Core plus stage stays at 24,820 B gzip.

### Three-dimensional viscoplastic material (FLUID-06)

The material point field follows finite strain and plastic shear in a uniform three-dimensional
grid. Longitudinal elastic waves limit its internal step. Rest density is fixed, while current
volume changes with the volumetric strain `J`. Coulomb contact applies on closed box faces
and a triangulated sampled terrain bed. The optional implicit solvent diffusion is on occupied
grid nodes. Resolve strong gradients with several points per cell. Very thin stretched
filaments can become under-resolved until an adaptive particle split/merge pass is available.
Bulk elastic stress is weakly compressible, with no incompressible pressure projection. The
entry emits positions and stresses for a separate renderer and leaves grain segregation and
bed entrainment to their own solvers.

The optional viscoplastic entry is 4,931 B gzip with a 5,187 B ceiling. Both Wasm assets are 16,986 B raw and each is 6,744 B gzip. Core plus stage remains 24,820 B gzip.

### Gas-filled soft shells (SOFT-06)

`@margoengine/physics/soft` solves the pressure of an outward-wound, watertight hollow triangle mesh. The chamber
has uniform pressure and a fixed pressure–volume product between fill changes. A changing external pressure or an
independent chamber uses an explicit fill or a separate body. The model has no through-mesh gas transport,
thermodynamic heat solve, or automatic gas loss when an edge constraint tears. Use a valid shell without
self-intersections, and its existing material, contacts and substeps still determine the membrane's mechanics.
Geometry uses f64 local coordinates for signed volume and f32 particle positions in the existing native step. The gas
product and ambient pressure also use f32 state columns. Each constraint pass takes work linear in vertices and
triangles and allocates no new scratch while stepping. The same optional soft Wasm runs under either renderer.
The complete optional soft entry measures 110,995 B gzip, up from 108,726 B, within its 111,864 B ceiling.
The separately loaded kernel chunk is 75,819 B gzip, up from 74,174 B, and the native kernel is 211,555 B raw.
Core plus stage remains 24,820 B gzip.

=== Known bugs and unverified features (docs/known-bugs.md) ===

# Known bugs and unverified features

Every bug found in Margo Engine is logged here with a repro and its cause, fixed or not, and an open one stays here
until it is fixed. Entries are newest first. A heading starts with the state (Open, Fixed with its date, Corrected);
an entry gives the **Repro**, the **Cause** and, once fixed, the commit and the regression test that keeps it fixed.
"Needs a maintainer decision" marks a fix that would change what a check accepts or touch the frozen core. Report a
new bug as [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md#reporting-bugs) describes.

### Fixed 2026-11-26: simulated earthquake loads lacked a propagating ground field (EARTH-08)

- **Repro:** Trigger a moment below a layered site. Scene shake parameters could move a camera, but the ground
  did not propagate a wave or supply different site accelerations to structures.
- **Cause:** The engine had no solver for the site's elastic propagation and free-surface response.
- **Fix:** `SeismicGround` propagates P and SV waves and publishes surface acceleration, building response,
  and soil cyclic demand. `SeismicInertialLoad` moves coupled rigid bodies in their support reference frame.
- **Regression:** `packages/physics/tests/coupling/seismic.test.js` checks the analytic wave branches, a
  free surface and layered site, live body recoil, and replay in both memory modes.

### Fixed 2026-11-26: outdoor sounds played before the pressure wave arrived (PA-64)

- **Repro:** Send a brief sound from 3 km away. Its old positional path pans and attenuates the sound as soon as it plays.
- **Cause:** Panning and Doppler act on the source's current pose. The graph carried no travel time or air absorption.
- **Fix:** `OutdoorSound` solves the acoustic path and `OutdoorAudio` applies its delay and broad spectral response.
- **Regression:** `packages/physics/tests/coupling/outdoor-sound.test.js` checks air, diffraction and reflection.
  `packages/audio/tests/outdoor-sound.browser.mjs` measures the added arrival delay in real PCM.
### Fixed 2026-11-26: a glTF wall added to LightBounce did not stop the bounce in the visibility maps (KB-BOUNCE-OCCLUDE1, clustered)

- **Repro:** packages/clustered/test/bounce.test.js, the table-by-the-wall room given as gltf/pbr primitives: before, only
  core meshes' triangles (`occluderMeshes` of the frame's batches) were scene occluders, so a model added with
  `bounce.add` occluded through its captured texels alone, and the wall the table hides from the lantern let the room's
  VPLs light the ground outside (over 5% of the unblocked bounce at three receivers, where an exact cast gives 0).
- **Cause:** `LightBounce.rebuild` built the visibility maps' scene occluders from core's batches only; PR #150 drew added
  models into the captures but never gave their triangles to `sampleSurfaces` (imperfect shadow maps sample every surface
  of the scene: Ritschel et al., ACM TOG 27(5), 2008, doi:10.1145/1409060.1409082).
- **Fix:** `bounceModelMeshes(model, store)` reads an added model's public `primitives` (20-float vertices, node matrix,
  instance rows; the primitives the capture draws, nodes shown in the transform store), and the rebuild samples them
  with core's meshes. `BounceMesh.stride` (default 6) lets `sampleSurfaces` read gltf/pbr's vertex layout.
- **Regression:** the CPU test above (the model's occluders equal the core meshes' to 1e-5, under 2% of unblocked behind
  the wall, filters for BLEND, tint, after-opaque, unlit, lines, skinned and hidden nodes), and the `wallModel` row of
  scripts/clustered-bounce-gpu-check.js on WebGPU and `MARGO_COMPAT=1` (the rooms' wall as a glTF box: 36 occluder pieces,
  the core wall's 36; the dark room 0). Skinned primitives, terrain and voxel still occlude through their captures only
  (docs/limits.md).

### Fixed 2026-11-26: a clearcoat from `materials.install` reflected its full base albedo into SSR and LightBounce captures (KB-BOUNCE-CAPTURE2, gltf)

- **Repro:** `node scripts/clustered-bounce-gpu-check.js` with its `installed` row: the LightBounce patch as a glTF quad with
  KHR_materials_clearcoat 1 drawn by `materials.install`, added with `bounce.add`, bounced exactly the uncoated patch's
  light onto the wall (ratio 1.000 at both points), where the same coat on a materials `Material` (`clearcoat: 1`) bounced
  0.955 and 0.959 of it, the base layer's 1 - F_coat(n.v) share (KHR_materials_clearcoat, "Layering"; F0 0.04 head on).
- **Cause:** gltf/pbr builds the capture shader by appending a `capture` entry point (`capturePBR`) after
  `materialExtensionShader` had run the extension's surface edits on every `let s=surface(i,front);`. The appended entry
  built the plain surface, so `materialClearcoatLighting` never ran there and its `materialCoatKeep` stayed 1, and the
  capture's base-layer weight `k` read only the native `layers` (none on an extension coat). SSR's capture shares the
  path, so its split-sum weight under an installed coat was too high as well.
- **Fix:** `capturePBR(code, declarations, keep)` multiplies `k` by the extension coat's `keep` expression, and
  `PBRModel`'s capture derivation applies `materialExtensionSurface` to the appended entry, as the SSAO occlusion entry
  already does. A materials `createMesh` mesh (a gltf/pbr model) needed nothing: `bounce.add(mesh)` and its clearcoat were
  right already, and the GPU check now holds them (`materials` and `coated` rows).
- **Regression:** packages/gltf/test/extensions.test.js ("a material extension coat weighs k by its keep"), and the
  `installed`, `materials` and `coated` rows of scripts/clustered-bounce-gpu-check.js on WebGPU and `MARGO_COMPAT=1`
  (0.9548 and 0.9586 of the core patch, within 1% of 0.96; the materials patch 1.0000; the JS twin within 2%).

### Fixed 2026-11-26: the order bodies woke in changed how the world moved (KB-PHYS-ORDER1, physics kernel)

- **Repro:** `packages/physics/kernel/tests/canonical.rs`: two worlds with the same rows, one with its awake list put back in
  a shuffled order (as if its bodies had woken in that order); their bodies differed after 45 steps.
- **Cause:** a step works through its lists in the order they were filled: the awake list in wake order (which numbered the
  islands and ordered each island's bodies), the active pairs in the order they were found and swapped out. Gauss-Seidel
  passes give different bits in a different order, so history the world does not hold as state decided its path, against
  rule 4 of docs/physics-framework.md section 7 (iteration order never depends on allocation order).
- **Fix:** at the start of every step and again after the island build's wake-ups, the awake list is put in body order and
  the active pairs in the order of their colliders and parts (`canonical_lists`, a stable bottom-up merge sort through
  scratch columns). Islands are numbered by their lowest body, and bodies, pairs and events come in row and collider order.
- **Regression:** the test above (600 steps, three wake orders shuffled again every 50 steps, and a snapshot restored at step
  300, bit for bit). The joint web's seed 1 now takes another path, on which its drivers do 1.7e12 J of work and a body
  reaches 172 km/s with no energy gained; `a_web_of_joints_stays_in_the_numbers` bounded speeds at 1e5 m/s, a figure with
  no derivation, and now bounds them by the range a step refuses past (RANGE), the energy ledger holding the physics.

### Fixed 2026-11-26: a held hull's deck volume fed by the sea's inflow took about half its water's weight (KB-FLIP-DECKLOAD2, physics flip)

- **Repro:** a box hull (2 m by 1 m by 1 m, a dynamic body held still by its locks) with its deck 0.2 m under still fresh
  water, `HullSolver` writing `deckInflow` and `DeckWaterSolver` (inflow on, the deck box on the deck, cells [20, 6, 10] of
  0.1 m). The deck volume takes the inflow and settles at 0.438 m^3 (4,297 N), but its load on the hull (its forces region,
  y) settles at -2,198 N after 6 s. KB-FLIP-DECKLOAD1's fix brought the same case from +1,124 N; its regression (0.3 m of
  water placed at the start, no inflow) takes the full weight.
- **Cause:** the water was right to the load; the particles were not right to the water. Each particle stands for an
  eighth of a cell of water, but the inflow put its particles along the bulwark whether a cell there was full or not,
  and particles then clustered where the flow converged and against the walls that stop them (FLIP's known volume loss):
  at 6 s the deck's particles stood 16.8 to a cell, so the liquid the grid kept, and its load, were half the water they
  counted.
- **Fix:** the inflow puts each particle in the first cell inward from the bulwark with room for it (fewer than eight),
  and the liquid now runs the implicit density projection of Kugelstadt, Longva, Thuerey and Bender (IEEE TVCG 27(4),
  2021) after each advection: the particles' density on the grid, held at 1 or more beside the air and to 0.5 to 1.5,
  with the walls sampled as water at rest, drives a second pressure solve whose gradient moves the particles apart.
  The same case now holds the hull with -4,578 N for 4,393 N of water (within the grid's bound), its particles at 7.2 a
  cell.
- **Regression:** `packages/physics/tests/deck-water.test.js`, "the deck volume claims its hull, so the hull carries one
  deck load, not two": the deck volume's load equals its water's weight within rho g l b h / 2.

### Fixed 2026-11-26: deck water on a hull held still loaded it with a fraction of its weight (KB-FLIP-DECKLOAD1, physics/flip)

- **Repro:** a dynamic hull held by locks (or by contacts, joints, a mooring) with a `DeckWaterSolver` on it: 0.3 m of
  water on a 2 m by 1 m deck (5,886 N) held the hull with -237 N; with the exceedance solver's inflow and the real hull
  solver, +1,124 N against -4,297 N.
- **Cause:** the deck volume carries its water as added mass in an implicit solve, M (M + A)^-1 (F + W) - W, which takes
  the hull as free: the water's weight went into a fall the hull never made, so little of it reached a hull something
  else held.
- **Fix:** the solve carries every other load on the hull too, seen in what moved it at the last step (M a_last less the
  load held and the weight), as the hull solver does: M (M + A)^-1 (F + A a_last + W + O) - W - O. A held hull takes the
  water's weight; a free one still falls with its water at g.
- **Regression:** `packages/physics/tests/deck-water.test.js`, "a dynamic hull held by locks takes its deck water's
  weight as the deck load (KB-FLIP-DECKLOAD1)".

### Open 2026-11-26: on the WebGL2 compatibility layer, test:shot's sky-coverage check loses the device on the orrery shot (KB-SHOT-COMPATLOST1, tools/shot)

- **Repro:** on an Apple M6 Mac (ANGLE on Metal), `npm run build:packages`, then `MARGO_COMPAT=1 npm run test:shot`. Two
  runs out of two failed the same way. `determinism-check.mjs` passes all its cases. `sky-coverage-check.mjs` passes its
  first two shots (cabin-hearth-kettle, cabin-window-snow). On its third, orrery-dolly (the page with no sky), the page
  logs `AbortError: The device was lost before the buffer mapped; map it again on the restored device`, and the shot
  tool fails on that page error (`tools/shot/render.mjs`, the console handler). `moving-check.mjs` and
  `look-masks-check.mjs` did not run after it. On WebGPU, `npm run test:shot` passes.
- **Cause:** not found yet. The compatibility layer reports a device loss while a readback buffer is waiting to map.
  The page then rejects that map, as the loss contract asks. What makes the layer lose its device on this shot is
  unknown: it is the third page the same browser opens in that check, and the first without a sky.
- **Same on main:** main's tools/shot fails the same way. The film hook added for PA-03 does not change it.

### Fixed 2026-11-26: GitHub CI's lint failed every pull request, and quality checked less there (KB-CI-MERGEBASE1, .github/workflows/ci.yml)

- **Repro:** any pull request (PR 68, job 139720307693): `npm run lint` stops with `fatal: Not a valid object name
  origin/main`.
- **Cause:** `actions/checkout@v4` checks out a pull request's merge commit at depth 1 with no origin/main, and
  scripts/lint.mjs diffs against the merge base with origin/main. The test job's `npm run quality` has two readers of
  the same merge base (scripts/quality/ratchet.js `droppedHistory`, scripts/support/unit-readers.mjs
  `changedAgainstMain`) that treat a missing one as nothing to check, so a pull request's dropped baseline history and
  changed documents' readers went unchecked.
- **Fixed:** the lint and test jobs check out the whole history (`fetch-depth: 0`). Regression: tests/ci-checkout.test.js
  follows each CI job's npm scripts through their imports and fails on a job that reaches `git merge-base` without a
  full checkout (it named `lint` and `test` on the old ci.yml).

### Fixed 2026-11-26: GitHub CI's bundler matrix and Node 22 tests failed on CI setup, not on code (KB-CI-PWVERSION1, KB-CI-ORACLE1, KB-CI-FIXTURES1, ci)

### Fixed 2026-11-26: the branches of a multibody under a fixed root were islands that walked each other's links (KB-PHYS-MBISLAND1, physics kernel)

- **Repro:** `packages/physics/tests/next-multibody.test.js`, "two branches under a fixed root are one island, and swing as
  mirror images of each other": two pendulums hung from one fixed root by one `addMultibody` tree.
- **Cause:** joints unite only moving bodies into an island, so under a fixed or kinematic root each branch was an island of
  its own. Each island's substeps walk every multibody tree they reach (`mb_roots`), from the root through every link, so one
  island projected and placed the other branch's links in its own substeps. Solved one island at a time this re-did work on
  links already consistent; solved at once on threads it would write another island's bodies.
- **Fix:** the moving links of a multibody whose root does not move are one island (`unite_multibodies`). Branches under a
  root that does not move do not move each other, so the physics is unchanged: the replay scenes' state hashes are the same.
- **Regression:** the test above (two islands before).

### Open 2026-11-26: check:rust-kernels builds the physics kernels with flags they no longer ship with (KB-RUST-KERNELFLAGS1, scripts)

- **Repro:** `node --test tests/rust-kernel-tests.test.js`: "every kernel that ships as Wasm is built for wasm32 with the
  shipped flags" fails, `WASM_RUSTFLAGS` (`-C target-feature=+simd128`) against the 3D kernel blueprint's `RUSTFLAGS`,
  which since 8fbdc409d4 (K05) add the world-memory link flags (`--import-memory`, the slot's `--global-base` and the
  exported stack and data symbols). The test runs in hygiene, so hygiene is red on main.
- **Cause:** each physics kernel is now built with its own slot's link flags (packages/physics/scripts/build-*-kernel.mjs,
  `rustFlags(slot, shared)`), while scripts/rust-kernel-tests.mjs builds every kernel that ships as Wasm with the one
  `WASM_RUSTFLAGS` of scripts/support/wasm-kernel.mjs, so check:rust-kernels no longer checks the build that ships.
- **Fix to make:** take each kernel's shipped flags from its build script (the blueprint's `RUSTFLAGS` for the 3D
  kernel, the 2D kernel's own variant flags) in check:rust-kernels and in the test, owned by the physics kernel work.


### Fixed 2026-11-25: a box face resting on a block's edge was held at one end at a time and rocked for ever (KB-PHYS-EDGEHOLD1, physics kernel, contacts)

- **Repro:** `packages/voxel/tests/debris.test.js`, "with physics a piece is a dynamic body of its cells mass that falls onto
  the voxel floor and comes to rest", with the block solver on: the L-shaped piece came to lie on the edge of the pillar's
  stump and on one corner of its beam, and still moved at 0.03 to 0.16 m/s after 20 s, sinking 4 mm. The same rocking state
  stepped on with the sweeps did not settle either.
- **Cause:** the separating axis test kept last step's edge pair when it came within the face bias (1 mm) of the best face
  (`sat_coherent`, the held-edge margin `-FACE_BIAS`). An edge pair gives one point. Where it ties a face, its two edges lie
  near parallel along that face, so the closest points clamp to one end of the block's edge: the manifold held that end
  alone, the other side fell until it struck, and the held point hopped to the other end. The geometry query, with no
  history, chose the face and clipped both ends.
- **Fix:** an edge pair must beat the face by the bias whether or not it was held, the rule Gregorius (GDC 2015) gives:
  faces win ties. A held face still wins its own ties, so the reference face stays coherent. Over 1,734 poses of a plank on
  a cube's edge (turns of -40 to 40 mrad in 5 mrad steps about its length and in the face's plane, its edge 0 to 30 cm past
  the cube's), a held edge pair now gives the manifold a test with no history gives on every pose; before, 1,499 lost an end.
- **Regression:** `packages/physics/kernel/tests/sat.rs` `a_face_resting_on_a_parallel_edge_keeps_both_ends_after_an_edge_pair`
  (one point with the held edge pair before), and the voxel debris test above with the block solver.
### Fixed 2026-11-25: the joint webs' energy ledger read a kinematic body's speed as energy gained (KB-PHYS-LEDGER1, physics kernel tests)

- **Repro:** `packages/physics/kernel/tests/stability.rs` `the_energy_ledger_reads_the_same_in_a_moving_frame`: a kinematic
  hub drags a 1 kg box on a spherical joint 0.2 m out of place. At rest the ledger reads no gain; with hub and box moving at
  50 m/s it read -4,800 J. With the block solver, web seed 17 of `a_web_of_joints_stays_in_the_numbers` reached a state where
  one step read 3.4 MJ of work as a gain against the 73 kJ its bodies gained (2.7 percent of the run's kinematic work, bound
  one part in a million).
- **Cause:** the native ledger `solver::DRIVEN` left out the work a kinematic body does through a joint's position-bias push
  (the `BIASED` flag) but counted the relaxing pass's taking back of that push. A push p from a body at speed u is the work
  p . u whatever it is for, so the ledger's "energy no force made" grew with the frame's speed.
- **Fix:** every impulse a kinematic body hands on counts. A push taken back nets nothing, and one left behind still shows as
  a gain of about p b / 2 (b the bias speed). All 60 web seeds gain nothing with either solver; the joint-drift proof
  `a_joint_does_not_turn_its_drift_into_speed` measures speed directly and still fails on the drift bug it was made for. No
  shipped code changes: the ledger is native only.
- **Regression:** the moving-frame test above (-4,800 J before), within f32's rounding of the box's kinetic energy.

The air propagation path used a fixed sound speed and had no depth axis for water. In a layered water column

### Fixed 2026-11-26: a WgslMaterial could not read a borrowed 32-bit float texture, so the depth-texture demo drew black (KB-DEPTHTEX-BLACK1, materials)

- **Repro:** `npm run visual:update` on a186f625f0 (RTX A6000, Edge 158.0.4370.33): `depth-texture-high` and `-phone`
  captured an all-black canvas in 4 of 4 runs with no page or WGSL error. The page's status, watched as it changed,
  briefly read `MargoError: Texture samples 32-bit float texels, which needs the device feature float32-filterable`.
  Chrome 158 gave the same; not a browser change.
- **Cause:** f6f22a4977 (2026-11-20, borrowed-object rule) added a `float32-filterable` refusal to the shared bind of
  every Texture made from a GPUTexture. A WgslMaterial reads such a texture with `textureLoad`, which needs no
  filtering (as its docs say), so DepthTexture's r32float `distance` threw on the first frame, core stopped the loop
  and the demo then wrote its ready text over the error and reported ready. The visual check took the black canvas.
- **Fix:** the refusal stays only where texels are filtered: material map slots (`sampled`) and envMap, each now
  checked after the bind so a function source, whose format is known only then, is refused too. The demo keeps an
  error on screen and never reports ready after one. Class guard: `scripts/visual-regression.js` fails a view that
  showed an error text at any moment, even one other text replaced (`scripts/support/shown-errors.js`); on the bug
  build it fails both depth-texture views with the MargoError above. A guard on GPU work was tried first and dropped:
  gameplay-sandbox and windy-meadow stop their loop on purpose under reduced motion, so they submit no work either.
  Regressions: "a borrowed 32-bit float GPUTexture binds to a WgslMaterial without float32-filterable" in
  packages/materials/test/texture-formats.test.js (fails on the old code) and tests/visual-shown-errors.test.js.
  Other demos still write their ready text over an onError message; the guard catches them in the visual check.

### Fixed 2026-11-25: native glass with the shared scene depth or a sciviz volume left the glass's own picture on screen (materials, KB-FILM-NEST2)

- **Repro:** a transmissive glTF material in a scene that also holds water, `html`, clustered contact shadows (the
  shared scene depth) or a sciviz volume, with no HDR post effect: with the shared depth at 4x, one frame on a new
  background reads the frame before (`packages/materials/test/native-glass-browser.mjs` `hdrNesting`, `scene depth 4x`).
  On a recorded pass list the glass presents a colour nothing has drawn into and the later capture writes after it, at
  4x for both and at 1x for the sciviz volume (`packages/materials/tests/native-glass-nesting.test.js`).
- **Cause:** captures nest, but the native glass capture presented at order 29 whatever had begun inside it: the shared
  depth begins at -15 and ends at 10000, the volume depth begins at -0.001 and ends at 39. The glass copied its own
  empty target to the frame, and the inner capture then wrote the scene into the glass's target, which was not shown
  again until the next frame.
- **Fix:** the glass presents at 29 only while it still owns the frame's colour; with a capture still open inside it,
  it presents at 10000.5, after every such capture has ended (`packages/materials/src/native-glass.js`). Scenes with no
  inner capture draw the same passes as before. A frame graph keeps a target until its last user is done (O'Donnell,
  "FrameGraph: Extensible Rendering Architecture in Frostbite", GDC 2017, https://www.gdcvault.com/play/1024612);
  no source treats this engine's pass orders.
- **Regression:** the two tests above, the GPU one on native WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer.

### Fixed 2026-11-25: on ANGLE Direct3D 11 a lit glTF scene with image light, both shadow kinds and LightBounce crashed the GPU process (KB-BOUNCE-COMPATUNITS1, webgl2-compat)

- **Repro:** `node scripts/run-with-timeout.mjs -- node scripts/compat-units-gpu-check.js --compat` (Edge, default
  ANGLE Direct3D 11, RTX A6000): a gltf physical material with all 13 maps (or the 5 + 5 peak) under Environment
  lighting, Shadows `soft`, a shadowed Clustered spot (LocalShadows) and LightBounce. Every WebGL context was lost at
  the first lit draw, shown as "The compatibility layer's own present program did not link (a bug: report it)". The
  same scene drew on ANGLE Vulkan and GL, and on Direct3D 11 with one texture unit fewer.
- **Cause:** ANGLE's Direct3D 11 back end gives a std140 uniform block that holds one array of 50 or more rows a shader
  resource after the stage's textures (a StructuredBuffer, its HLSL `register(t15)` and `register(t16)` here); the lit
  fragment program had 15 texture units and two such blocks, 17 resources, and past 16 the browser's GPU process ends
  at the program's first draw (exit 0xC000001D). A raw WebGL2 page shows it with no Margo code:
  `packages/webgl2-compat/test/d3d11-srv-crash-repro.mjs` (16 samplers and one `uvec4[50]` block crash, `uvec4[49]`
  does not; 14 samplers and 3 blocks crash, 13 do not; ANGLE Vulkan draws every case). The layer's unit count (15 of
  16) was right; the blocks are not texture units to GL. Second defect: a lost context surfaced as a layer bug (the
  present program "did not link"), as a validation error (a framebuffer "not complete") or as a thrown
  transferToImageBitmap, because the context is lost at once and its webglcontextlost event comes a task later.
- **Fix:** the GLSL back end (glsl/emit.ts `fitShaderResources`) counts a stage's texture units and uniform blocks
  together; past the stage's limit (`translateWGSL` `textureUnits`, from MAX_TEXTURE_IMAGE_UNITS and
  MAX_VERTEX_TEXTURE_IMAGE_UNITS) each block declares its rows inside a struct, the same std140 layout, which ANGLE
  keeps as a constant buffer. Stages that fit are byte for byte as before. A lost context now loses the device
  (`device.lost`, reason 'unknown'): errors are not raised after it, the present stops, and the layer's helper
  programs return unlinked instead of throwing.
- **Regression:** `packages/webgl2-compat/test/glsl.test.js` (the struct form past the limit, per stage, and the plain
  form within it), `packages/webgl2-compat/test/lost-context-browser.mjs` and `scripts/compat-units-gpu-check.js
  --compat` (both in webgl2-compat's test:gpu; the check passes on native WebGPU, ANGLE Direct3D 11 and Vulkan).
  The room the plan in the row asks for landed after it: glTF slots sharing a texture bind it once (2026-11-25), gltf
  materials past the device limit pack their base maps, and the layer counts units per stage before linking and
  refuses past a limit with code `unsupported` (errors#texture-units) (2026-11-26; `packages/gltf/test/materials-ext.test.js`,
  `packages/webgl2-compat/test/device.test.js`). A scene that needs more than 16 units even packed still gets that
  coded refusal.
- **Sources:** Direct3D 11 has 128 shader resource slots, 16 sampler slots and 14 constant buffer slots per stage, so
  the 16 is ANGLE's own table, not the API's (Microsoft, "Direct3D 11.3 Functional Specification", 2015, section 21
  limits, https://microsoft.github.io/DirectX-Specs/d3d/archive/D3D11_3_FunctionalSpec.htm). A struct member of a
  std140 block holding one uvec4 array keeps offset 0 and a 16-byte stride, so the layout is unchanged (Khronos, "OpenGL
  ES Version 3.0.6", 2019, section 2.12.6.4, https://registry.khronos.org/OpenGL/specs/es/3.0/es_spec_3.0.pdf), and a
  `#define` maps each row read onto it (Khronos, "The OpenGL ES Shading Language 3.00", 2016, section 3.4,
  https://registry.khronos.org/OpenGL/specs/es/3.0/GLSL_ES_Specification_3.00.pdf). ANGLE's source was not read; its
  behaviour comes from the raw repro.
### Fixed 2026-11-25: fsm's equivalent mutants named lines that had moved (KB-MUTATION-PINS1, scripts, mutation)
