=== @margoengine/humans (packages/humans/README.md) ===

# @margoengine/humans

People in one call. `addPerson(engine, model)` takes a character loaded with `@margoengine/gltf/pbr` and dresses it
the way a film needs it: skin, eyes and strand hair on the materials named for them, an Animator that plays the clips
with cross-fades, dual quaternion skinning so a raised arm keeps its shoulder, relaxed hands on clips whose fingers are flat, and the
scene's shadows and sky light. Each further default (face, cloth) arrives as it is built, with no change to the call.

```ts
import {Engine} from 'margoengine';
import {loadGLTF} from 'margoengine/gltf/pbr';
import {addPerson} from 'margoengine/humans';
const canvas = document.querySelector('canvas')!;
const engine = await Engine.create(canvas);
const model = await loadGLTF(engine, '/examples/assets/khronos/RiggedFigure/RiggedFigure.glb');
const person = await addPerson(engine, model, {materials: {skin: [model.primitives[0].material.name ?? '']}});
console.log(person.clips.length, person.animator?.state); // its clips; the first one plays
```

## Crowds of hundreds (`./crowd`)

`walkCrowd(crowd, drawer, {walk, stand, stride})` joins a `@margoengine/navmesh` `Crowd`, which moves the people, to a
`SkinnedCrowd` or `VATCrowd` from `@margoengine/animation`, which draws them all in one instanced call. Each agent gets an
instance placed and turned with it (at most `turnRate`, 4 radians a second, so avoidance does not snap a head round), and
its walk cycle moves on by the ground the agent covers divided by `stride`, so feet do not slide at any speed. With
`new Crowd(nav, {density: true})` those speeds are Weidmann's measured ones: about 0.6 m/s at 2 people a square metre.
Agents slower than `standBelow` (0.05 m/s) play the `stand` clip. An agent the crowd pushes back against where it means
to go (its `velocity` against its `preferredVelocity`, which a navmesh `CrowdAgent` has) steps back facing its way, its
walk cycle running backward, instead of turning round to face the push; without `preferredVelocity` the heading follows
the velocity. `variants` (atlas regions) give each agent one outfit
of several by a seeded hash. The entry imports neither package; it reads them by shape.

```ts
import {Engine} from 'margoengine';
import {loadGLTF} from 'margoengine/gltf/pbr';
import {Animation} from 'margoengine/animation';
import {SkinnedCrowd, bakeBones} from 'margoengine/animation/instanced-skin';
import {Crowd, NavMesh} from 'margoengine/navmesh';
import {walkCrowd} from 'margoengine/humans/crowd';
const canvas = document.querySelector('canvas')!;
const engine = await Engine.create(canvas);
const model = await loadGLTF(engine, '/examples/assets/khronos/RiggedFigure/RiggedFigure.glb');
const people = SkinnedCrowd.attach(engine, bakeBones(new Animation(model)));
model.dispose();
const plaza = new NavMesh([[0,0,0], [40,0,0], [40,0,40], [0,0,40]], [[0,1,2,3]]);
const crowd = new Crowd(plaza, {density: true});
for (let k = 0; k < 300; k++)
  crowd.addAgent({position: [1 + (k % 20) * 0.6, 0, 1 + Math.floor(k / 20) * 0.6], radius: 0.25, maxSpeed: 1.34}).setTarget([39, 0, 20]);
const walkers = walkCrowd(crowd, people, {walk: 0, stride: 1.4});
for (let k = 0; k < 30; k++) {
  crowd.update(1 / 30);
  walkers.update(1 / 30);
}
console.log(walkers.instances.length, walkers.phases[0]); // 300 people, each at its own place in the cycle
```

## Period cast kit (`./cast`)

Clothes for a period film, cut in code for measured bodies: 1910 American West (US Forest Service rangers, miners,
loggers, railwaymen, townsmen) and 2011 coastal Japan (office workers, school pupils, fishermen). Each garment is a
thick mesh with seams and hems; layers stack from the skin out and never pass through each other at rest. Cloth
reflects light by the microcylinder model fitted to measured fabrics (Sadeghi et al. 2013), with a thin layer of loose
fibre ends over wool and cotton (`fuzz`: their grazing sheen), and is drawn with glTF base colour plus
`KHR_materials_sheen`, fitted to that model with the dye's measured colour kept.

```ts
import {Engine} from 'margoengine/core';
import {parseGLTFAsync} from 'margoengine/gltf/pbr';
import {OUTFITS, BODIES, dress, outfitGLB, castCrowd, castVariants, applyCastSettings} from 'margoengine/humans/cast';

const engine = await Engine.create(document.querySelector('canvas')!);
// The 1910 ranger's uniform as one glTF binary: a mesh per garment with its cloth material.
const ranger = await parseGLTFAsync(engine, outfitGLB(OUTFITS['ranger-1910']));

// The garments as data: positions, normals, uvs, indices, seams and fit rings.
const garments = dress(BODIES.us1919Man, OUTFITS['miner-1910']);
console.log(garments.map((g) => `${g.spec.name}: ${g.geometry.positions.length / 3} vertices`));
```

=== @margoengine/horses (packages/horses/README.md) ===

# @margoengine/horses

Horses built in code from published equine measurements. `addHorse(engine)` builds a riding horse, a cavalry remount or
a heavy draft horse to its breed group's proportions, with a coat, white markings, a mane and tail of hair cards shaded
as strand hair, a 37-joint rig and walk, trot, canter and gallop taken from equine biomechanics. Its gait follows its
speed, a stance hoof stays where it struck, and film time seeks exactly. A rider seat gives a person the saddle, stirrups
and reins and a hip that rides the horse's back; `addHorseCrowd` draws hundreds in one call.

```ts
import {Engine} from 'margoengine';
import {addHorse} from 'margoengine/horses';
const engine = await Engine.create(document.querySelector('canvas')!);
const horse = await addHorse(engine, {type: 'cavalry', coat: 'bay', markings: {blaze: true}});
horse.speed = 4; // eases into a trot at 3 m/s^2
horse.advanceTime(1 / 30); // or horse.seek(12.5) for a film frame
console.log(horse.currentGait, horse.body.mass.toFixed(0)); // 'walk' as it sets off, 'trot' near 4 m/s; about 459 kg
```

An existing skinned horse can use the same controller through `skin`. Provide its loaded model in the same engine,
its fitted skeleton in metres facing +Z, and a function that applies the solved pose to its joint map. The controller
sets root position and yaw, attaches its skinning pass, and keeps the authored materials. The tightest of the four
fitted limbs determines whether the stride must shorten to keep the same speed at a quicker cadence. Fit the skeleton
in metres in a naturally bent stance so the package can measure extension in both directions. The caller owns the model.

```ts
import type { Engine } from 'margoengine';
import { addHorse, type HorseSkin } from 'margoengine/horses';

export async function startImportedHorse(engine: Engine, skin: HorseSkin) {
  const horse = await addHorse(engine, { skin });
  horse.speed = 3;
  horse.advanceTime(1);
  return horse;
}
```

Pass `ground(x, z)` for an uneven path. The controller holds each stance hoof at its world-space landing point
through turns, then releases the horizontal correction over 0.18 seconds. It conforms the hoof to the local grade and
retains toe breakover and swing clearance. The back and saddle lean with the wider ground slope. Supply a stable,
continuous height field in metres for deterministic seeks. Jumps, large risers, and overhangs require separate route
planning. Limb reach and splay constraints still apply.

```ts
import type { Engine } from 'margoengine';
import { addHorse } from 'margoengine/horses';

export async function walkOnAGrade(engine: Engine) {
  const horse = await addHorse(engine, { ground: (x, z) => 0.08 * z - 0.06 * x + 0.04 * Math.sin(2 * z) });
  horse.gait = 'walk';
  horse.speed = 1.4;
  horse.seek(2.4);
  return horse;
}
```

The terrain pass follows the world-space plant and continuous correction approach of [Kovar, Schreiner and Gleicher,
Footskate Cleanup for Motion Capture Editing (2002)](https://research.cs.wisc.edu/graphics/Papers/Gleicher/Mocap/cleanup.pdf).
Its separate support frames and trunk sampling draw on [Coros, Karpathy, Jones, Reveret and van de Panne,
Locomotion Skills for Simulated Quadrupeds (2011)](https://www.cs.ubc.ca/~van/papers/2011-TOG-quadruped/index.html)
and [Miller, Holden, Al-Ashqar, Dubach, Mitchell and Komura, Carpet Unrolling for Character Control on Uneven Terrain
(2015)](https://www.pure.ed.ac.uk/ws/portalfiles/portal/21937045/MIG_2015_paper_22.pdf).

## Anatomy (`./anatomy`)

| Group | Withers | Build | Weight |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `riding` | 1.63 m (16 hh) | Thoroughbred: long legs, narrow chest | about 488 kg |
| `cavalry` | 1.57 m (15.2 hh) | remount: 15 to 16 hands, 950 to 1,200 lb | about 459 kg |
| `draft` | 1.75 m (17.1 hh) | Shire, Clydesdale, Percheron: deep chest, heavy bone | about 859 kg |

Every length is a ratio of the withers height: body length, croup, heart girth, chest depth and width, hip width, head
and neck, the heights of the elbow, knee, fetlocks, hip joint, stifle and hock, and the cannon circumference. Weight is
girth squared times length over 11,880 (Carroll and Huntington 1988). `withers` sets another height, `condition` (0.8 to
1.25) a lean or heavy horse.

```ts
import {handsToMetres, horseBody} from 'margoengine/horses/anatomy';
const shire = horseBody({type: 'draft', withers: handsToMetres(17.2)});
console.log(shire.withers.toFixed(3), shire.mass.toFixed(0)); // 1.778, about 900 kg
```

=== @margoengine/armies (packages/armies/README.md) ===

# @margoengine/armies

Armies of hundreds of soldiers and horses, drawn at every distance. A `@margoengine/navmesh/formations` `Army` moves
the men and horses in line, column, square, wedge or skirmish order, on the march or in a charge; `addArmy` draws them:
every foot soldier and rider as one crowd of a baked person (skinned on the GPU when big on screen, a vertex animation
of a simplified mesh when small, culled when off screen or too small to see, all inside a budget), every horse in one
`@margoengine/horses/crowd` herd, each rider seated on the saddle its horse is drawn with. Clips follow each man's
ground speed (stand, walk, run) at the phase the ground he covered gives, so feet never slide; soldiers keep step;
each has his own height and outfit. Every frame is a pure function of the army's film time and the camera, so a film
seeks exactly.

Any person plugs in: a Character Creator export loaded through `@margoengine/fbx` and dressed by
`@margoengine/humans` `addPerson`, a glTF, or a body built in code. Bake it once with `bakePerson`.

```ts
import {Engine} from 'margoengine';
import {loadGLTF} from 'margoengine/gltf/pbr';
import {Animation} from 'margoengine/animation';
import {Army} from 'margoengine/navmesh/formations';
import {addArmy, bakePerson} from 'margoengine/armies';
const engine = await Engine.create(document.querySelector('canvas')!, {camera: {position: [0, 6, -40], target: [0, 1, 10], fov: 35}});
const model = await loadGLTF(engine, '/examples/assets/khronos/RiggedFigure/RiggedFigure.glb');
const person = await bakePerson(new Animation(model));
model.dispose();
const army = new Army();
army.add({count: 200, shape: 'line', ranks: 2}).march();
army.add({count: 30, kind: 'cavalry', shape: 'line', ranks: 2, position: [0, -25]}).charge({goal: [0, 150]});
const drawn = await addArmy(engine, army, {person});
army.advanceTime(4);
drawn.update(engine.camera);
console.log(drawn.persons.length, drawn.horses?.count, drawn.people.counts); // 230 people (200 on foot, 30 riders), 30 horses
```

| Option of `addArmy` | Default |
| --- | --- |
| `person` | needed: a `bakePerson` bake |
| `clips` | `{stand: 'stand', walk: 'walk', run: 'run', ride: 'ride'}` by name or index; a missing run walks, a missing stand holds the walk, a missing ride stands |
| `strides` | ground one clip cycle covers at scale 1: walk 1.524 m (two 30 inch steps, quick time), run 1.829 m (two 36 inch steps, double time), Infantry Drill Regulations 1911 |
| `runAbove`, `blendBand`, `standBelow` | 2 m/s (the walk-run change), 0.4 m/s, 0.1 m/s |
| `step` | `'cadence'`: the men keep step; `'route'`: each his own phase |
| `stature` | 0.04: one standard deviation of height as a fraction of the mean (about 7 cm on 1.75 m), cut at 2.5 |
| `variants` | outfits as atlas regions (`castVariants` of `@margoengine/humans/cast` fits), handed out by a seeded hash |
| `facing` | 0: the model faces +Z (glTF) |
| `horses` | `addHorseCrowd` options for cavalry; `false` draws no horses (and no riders) |
| `rider` | `{height, hipHeight, seatHip, pitchShare}` as `riderMatrix` |
| `near`, `far`, `vertices`, `nearScreen`, `cullScreen`, `hysteresis` | the crowd budget: see Levels |
| `map`, `color`, `roughness`, `metalness` | the person's look, as `VATCrowd` |
| `seed` | 1 |

`drawn.update(view, aspect?)` reads `army.members` and `army.time`: call it after `army.advanceTime(dt)` or
`army.seek(t)` and after placing the camera, with the engine's camera. A core Camera only refreshes its frustum as it
renders, so `update` brings it up to date first (at `aspect`, default the canvas's): the plan follows where the camera
is now, on the first frame and on a seek alike. `drawn.people.near` and `drawn.people.far` are the two draws and `drawn.horses.crowd` the
herd, for `shadows.add(...)` and `lighting.add(...)`.

## Baking a person (`./bake`)

`bakePerson(animation, {fps, clips, farTriangles})` bakes the person's clips into a bone texture (the near level,
`@margoengine/animation/instanced-skin` `bakeBones`), simplifies the mesh to at most `farTriangles` (3000) by quadric
collapses (`@margoengine/lod/auto`; every kept vertex is one of the source's, with its own position, normal, UV and skin
weights; vertices that follow different bones are never welded), and poses the simplified mesh on the CPU from the same
bone rows into a vertex animation texture (the far level, `@margoengine/animation/vat`). Skinning is linear in the bone
matrices, so posing the rows and interpolating them gives what the shader gets by interpolating the matrices: a member
handed from one level to the other stands where it stood, within 1e-5 m. The far texture of four one-second clips at
30 a second and 3000 triangles is about 12 MB; past 8192 texture rows `bakePerson` throws and names the fix.

[README continues: https://margoengine.com/llms/packages/armies.md]

=== @margoengine/tween (packages/tween/README.md) ===

# @margoengine/tween

Allocation-free numeric tween updates and easing timelines.

Import `margoengine/tween` from the `margoengine` package, or `@margoengine/tween` from this package alone; the two are the same module. Neither is on npm yet: the [Install](../../README.md#install) section lists the two routes that work today (run in a clone, or install local tarballs).

Numeric property interpolation and easing; `update` steps the existing tracks in place and creates no per-track objects.

## Choose a clock and entry

The root Tween and Timeline remain the small numeric API. Additional workflows use
explicit imports from `@margoengine/tween/<entry>` or `margoengine/tween/<entry>`:

| Entry | API | Clock owner |
|---|---|---|
| `async` | AsyncTween, AsyncTimeline | Caller calls update in seconds. |
| `props` | to, from, fromTo, keyframes | Each returned operation has update. |
| `timeline` | Timeline with arrays, paths, custom clips and nesting | Caller updates the parent. |
| `control` | TweenControl with target/property ownership | Caller updates the control world. |
| `scroll-pin` | pinTimeline, scrollSnapPoint | The link owns scroll listeners and requestAnimationFrame. |
| `inertia` | VelocityTracker, inertia | Caller supplies sample times and update deltas in seconds. |

These imports do not start a clock or install listeners. Only attaching a scroll link
takes browser input ownership. Do not advance the same operation from both a world or
parent and an independent frame loop. Handle completion rejections when cancelling,
replacing or disposing awaitable work; cancellation preserves the last written values.

## Awaitable operations

`AsyncTween` provides the root Tween's to, array, path and custom methods as awaitable
tasks. A returned TweenTask is also a cancel function; it exposes `finished`,
`cancel(reason)` and Symbol.dispose. Completion resolves; abort, replacement, clear or
an update failure rejects. An AbortSignal rejects with its exact reason; explicit
cancellation defaults to AbortError. A replacement on the same target/property rejects
the previous task. Invalid input is checked before valid work is replaced.

Call `driver.update(deltaSeconds)` from the application loop. Awaiting a task does not
advance it. `driver.finished` captures operations active when it is read; tasks added
later are independent. Callback-created work starts on the next update. Recursive
update is rejected. `clear()` or disposal cancels all active tasks. Timing options
match the root Tween: required nonnegative duration, delay 0, linear easing, repeat 0,
yoyo false and optional completion/repeat callbacks; signal defaults to unset.

`AsyncTimeline` wraps the root scalar Timeline with `finished` and then support,
signal cancellation and disposal. Its to, label, call, seek, reverse, pause, play and
update follow the root API. Pause and seek do not settle completion. Replaying a
settled run creates a fresh finished promise; save or await the promise for that run.
An already-aborted signal also cancels a replay. Playback callbacks run during update,
not during seek. Cancelling pauses the timeline and leaves sampled values in place.


```ts
import {AsyncTween, AsyncTimeline} from '@margoengine/tween/async';
const target = {x: 0};
const driver = new AsyncTween();
const task = driver.to(target, 'x', 10, {duration: 1});
driver.update(1); // Application clock, seconds. Await alone does not advance it.
await task;
if (target.x !== 10) throw new Error('Tween did not finish');
const timeline = new AsyncTimeline().to(target, 'x', 20, {duration: 1}).play();
timeline.update(1);
await timeline.finished;
const controller = new AbortController();
const cancelled = driver.to(target, 'x', 30, {duration: 1, signal: controller.signal});
const observed = cancelled.finished.catch(reason => console.log(reason.name));
controller.abort();
await observed;
driver.clear();
```

## Multiple properties and keyframes

The `props` entry's `to(target, values, options)`, `from(target, values, options)` and
`fromTo(target, start, end, options)` animate finite numeric writable properties,
including a Vector3's x/y/z. Destinations may be numbers or relative strings using
+=, -=, *= or /=. Relative scalars resolve against the captured starting value;
relative entries in a keyframe value list resolve against the preceding value.
Nonfinite arithmetic, including division by zero, rejects.

[README continues: https://margoengine.com/llms/packages/tween.md]

=== @margoengine/cinematic (packages/cinematic/README.md) ===

# @margoengine/cinematic

Virtual cameras with priorities and blends, framing, dolly tracks, group framing, camera noise, confiners and focus tracking, on top of damped follow, look-at and shake.

`Cinematic` and `CameraBrain` detach from the scene where their actual plugin
instance was registered. Direct disposal, removing the owning plugin or scene,
and engine disposal all release the registration. Repeated disposal preserves
same-name replacements. Both plugins can attach to another scene after disposal;
later cleanup follows that new registration.

Import `margoengine/cinematic` from the `margoengine` package, or `@margoengine/cinematic` from this package alone; the two are the same module. Neither is on npm yet: the [Install](../../README.md#install) section lists the two routes that work today (run in a clone, or install local tarballs).

`rig.setOrbitOffset(yaw, pitch, distance, height = 0)` writes the retained camera
offset in place from orbit angles (no new vector is created). The sandbox uses this
public method after its shared locomotion step.

A virtual camera with analytically integrated critically damped follow and look-at springs plus additive screen shake.

```ts
import {Cinematic} from 'margoengine/cinematic';
import {Engine} from 'margoengine/core';
import {boxGeometry} from 'margoengine/geometry';
import {PbrMaterial, createMesh} from 'margoengine/materials';
const engine = await Engine.create(document.querySelector('canvas')!);
const player = createMesh(engine, boxGeometry(0.5, 1.8, 0.5), new PbrMaterial()).root;
const rig = Cinematic.attach(engine, {offset: [0,3,6], damping: 6});
rig.follow(player);
rig.shake(0.2, 0.4);
```

follow accepts a live mesh from the attached engine or a world-position tuple. Mesh targets use world transforms. Shake amplitude is in world units and duration is seconds; it does not alter the settled spring position. The frame plugin owns camera position/target while attached, so disable competing camera controls. dispose detaches it.

Film time: `rig.advanceTime(delta)` is one frame of the rig with no draw (springs, shake, `rig.time`), so `seek` from
`@margoengine/cutscene/seek` starts a film scene where a continuous run's follow and shake are. A `CameraNoise` stage
moves its clock with `noise.advanceTime(delta)`; pass it to `seek` as an `extra` clock when no attached `CameraBrain`
runs it as a stage (the brain's own clock steps its stages).

Scope the rig with `using` (it calls `dispose()` and returns the camera to your controls):

```ts
import {Cinematic} from 'margoengine/cinematic';
import {Engine} from 'margoengine/core';
import {Physics} from 'margoengine/physics';
const engine = await Engine.create(document.querySelector('canvas')!);
await Physics.load();
const physics = Physics.attach(engine);
{
  using rig = Cinematic.attach(engine, {offset: [0, 3, 6]});
  rig.follow([0, 1.6, 0]);
  rig.update(1 / 60);
}
```

Errors name their fix: a bad argument throws `RangeError` or `TypeError` (for example `Invalid camera delta; pass a finite delta of 0 or more seconds`), and attaching a rig twice throws `MargoError` with code `attached`.

Set `ground: (x,z) => height` to keep the camera arm above a CPU heightfield.
`clearance` defaults to 0.65 world units. The rig checks both its desired arm and
the resulting damped/shaken camera, without changing your requested `offset`.
For a below-target orbit, it raises the rendered aim point by as much as the ground
lifted the camera, so terrain clearance preserves upward look instead of forcing the
view back down; shake and spring lag never move the aim point.
Six samples along each arm suit broad terrain; narrow ridges and buildings need
collision geometry. Heights must be finite. Ground handling is disabled by default.

Walls and ceilings: set `collide: (origin, direction, distance) => hitDistance | null`. Each frame
the rig asks for the first obstacle along the arm from the look-at point to the (damped, shaken,
ground-lifted) camera; on a hit the camera moves in at once to `clearance` short of it, and once the
arm is clear it eases back out at the follow damping. The spring state and your `offset` are
unchanged. The arrays passed in are reused each frame. Any scene query fits, for example a sphere
cast against the physics world (so the near plane does not clip into the wall):

```ts
const rig = Cinematic.attach(engine, {offset: [0, 3, 6], clearance: 0.3,
  collide: (o, d, max) => physics.shapeCast({shape: 'sphere', radius: 0.2}, [o[0], o[1], o[2]], [0, 0, 0, 1], [d[0], d[1], d[2]], {maxDistance: max, excludeDynamic: true})?.distance});
```

or `@margoengine/bvh`'s Raycaster (`firstHitOnly`, `far = max`) over the level. Exclude the followed
character from the query, and start it above the floor if the look-at point sits on it (the arm
starts at the target, usually the character's feet).

## Camera priorities and blends

[README continues: https://margoengine.com/llms/packages/cinematic.md]

=== @margoengine/cutscene (packages/cutscene/README.md) ===

# @margoengine/cutscene

Import `margoengine/cutscene` from the `margoengine` package, or `@margoengine/cutscene` from this package alone; the two are the same module. Neither is on npm yet: the [Install](../../README.md#install) section lists the two routes that work today (run in a clone, or install local tarballs).

A timeline sequencer for cutscenes and in-game cinematics: tracks of keys and clips in a JSON document, a pure
`evaluate(t)` that gives the whole scene state at any time, and a player with play, pause, reverse, speed, scrubbing,
skip and fast-forward that fires every event in order. It renders nothing itself and imports nothing heavy: apply the
state to your camera, objects, animation mixer, audio and UI.

```ts
import { Camera } from 'margoengine/core';
import { CutscenePlayer, type CutsceneDocument } from 'margoengine/cutscene';

const intro: CutsceneDocument = {
  format: 'margo-cutscene',
  version: 1,
  duration: 6,
  markers: [{ time: 3, name: 'reveal' }],
  tracks: [
    {
      type: 'camera',
      id: 'cam',
      keys: [
        { time: 0, position: [0, 2, 8], target: [0, 1, 0] },
        { time: 3, position: [5, 3, 4], target: [0, 1, 0], ease: 'easeInOutCubic' },
        { time: 4, position: [0, 1.6, 2], target: [0, 1.5, 0], fov: 35, cut: true },
      ],
    },
    { type: 'transform', id: 'door', target: 'door', keys: [{ time: 3, rotation: [0, 0, 0, 1] }, { time: 4, rotation: [0, 0.7071, 0, 0.7071] }] },
    { type: 'animation', id: 'hero', target: 'hero', clips: [{ start: 0, duration: 6, clip: 'Walk', loop: true, length: 1.2 }] },
    { type: 'audio', id: 'music', clips: [{ start: 0, duration: 6, sound: 'theme', fadeIn: 1 }] },
    { type: 'subtitle', id: 'subs', clips: [{ start: 1, duration: 2, text: 'Someone left the door open.', speaker: 'Ada' }] },
    { type: 'event', id: 'cues', events: [{ time: 3.5, name: 'spawnBats', data: { count: 12 } }] },
  ],
};

const camera = new Camera();
const player = new CutscenePlayer(intro);
player.on('event', (event) => console.log('event', event.name, event.data));
player.on('marker', (marker) => console.log('marker', marker.name));
const done = player.play();

// Each frame:
player.update(1 / 60);
const state = player.state;
if (state.camera) {
  camera.position = state.camera.position;
  camera.target = state.camera.target;
  camera.fov = state.camera.fov;
  camera.up = state.camera.up;
}
// state.transforms.door.rotation, state.animations, state.audio, state.subtitles: apply them the same way.

player.skip(); // "Skip cutscene": jumps to the end and still fires spawnBats and the marker, in order.
await done; // true: it finished
```

## Tracks

Every track has an `id` (unique in its timeline) and may be `muted`. Key tracks interpolate between keys sorted by
`time`, holding the first value before the first key and the last after the last; `ease` on a key shapes the move into
it (`'linear'` default, `'step'`, `'smoothstep'`, any `ease*` easing of `@margoengine/tween` such as
`'easeOutBack'`, or cubic-bezier points `[x1, y1, x2, y2]`). Clip tracks hold spans `start` + `duration` (start
inclusive, end exclusive) that may overlap.

| Track | Fields | State |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `camera` | `keys: [{time, position, target, fov?, roll?, ease?, cut?}]`, `path` (`'catmull-rom'` default, `'linear'`) | `camera`: `position`, `target`, `fov` (degrees, default 60), `roll`, `up` |
| `transform` | `target`, `keys: [{time, position?, rotation?, scale?, ease?}]` | `transforms[target]`; each channel among the keys that set it; rotations slerp |
| `property` | `target`, `property`, `keys: [{time, value, ease?}]` (a number or an array) | `properties[target][property]` |
| `animation` | `target`, `clips: [{start, duration, clip, speed?, offset?, loop?, length?, blendIn?, blendOut?}]` | `animations`: clip name, clip time and blend weight |
| `audio` | `clips: [{start, duration, sound, volume?, offset?, fadeIn?, fadeOut?}]` | `audio`: sound, time into it, volume |
| `subtitle` | `clips: [{start, duration, text, speaker?}]` | `subtitles` |
| `event` | `events: [{time, name, data?}]` | fired by the player |
| `timeline` | `clips: [{start, duration, timeline, speed?, offset?}]` naming one of the document's `timelines` | the nested timeline's state, merged in |

Camera keys with `cut: true` jump instead of moving there, and the Catmull-Rom path never bends across a cut, so one
track holds a whole edit. The first unmuted camera track wins; a later transform or property track wins a channel two
tracks key. Markers name points in time; `state.marker` is the last one passed.

Nested timelines live under `timelines` and are placed by timeline clips with their own speed and offset; they may
nest (up to 16 levels, no cycles). Their tracks report paths like `intro/sfx`. A nested clip cut by the window of
its timeline clip still enters and exits, at the window's edges.

## Evaluating, scrubbing and seeking

```ts
import { Cutscene } from 'margoengine/cutscene';
```

[README continues: https://margoengine.com/llms/packages/cutscene.md]

=== @margoengine/controls (packages/controls/README.md) ===

# @margoengine/controls

Orbit, map, trackball, arcball, fly, first-person, pointer-lock and collision-aware walkthrough (/walk) camera controls, a transform gizmo and drag controls for Margo Engine.

Import `margoengine/controls` from the `margoengine` package, or `@margoengine/controls` from this package alone; the two are the same module. Neither is on npm yet: the [Install](../../README.md#install) section lists the two routes that work today (run in a clone, or install local tarballs).

`stepLocomotion(state, actions, delta, height, options?)` provides ground-following
character movement with normalized diagonals, damped speed and heading, and a
50 ms movement-step limit. Retained state is `[x,y,z,heading,cameraYaw,cameraPitch,
gaitPhase,speed]`; actions are `[strafe,forward,lookX,lookY,sprint]`.
Options include `bounds: [minX,maxX,minZ,maxZ]`, `minHeight`, `walkSpeed` (3.4),
and `runSpeed` (7). Bounds and minimum height are omitted by default. Look values
are angular deltas; pitch stays between -1.4 (look up) and 0.9 radians (look down).
Use `Cinematic` ground clearance to keep upward-looking cameras above terrain. Height samples must
be finite. The caller owns input bindings, character meshes and gait animation.

```ts
import {stepLocomotion} from 'margoengine/controls';

const state = new Float32Array(8);                    // x, y, z, heading, cameraYaw, cameraPitch, gaitPhase, speed
const actions = new Float32Array([0, 1, 0, 0, 0]);    // strafe, forward, lookX, lookY, sprint: walk forward
const ground = (x: number, z: number) => 0.1 * Math.sin(x) * Math.cos(z); // any finite height sampler
for (let frame = 0; frame < 60; frame++) stepLocomotion(state, actions, 1 / 60, ground, {bounds: [-50, 50, -50, 50]});
console.log(state[0], state[2]);                      // where the walker is after one second
```

Bad inputs throw a `RangeError` that says what to pass (finite numbers, bounds with min below max).

Orbit, map, trackball, arcball, fly, first-person and pointer-lock camera controls plus an interactive transform gizmo and drag controls for Margo Engine, each tree-shakable on its own. `DragControls` uses `@margoengine/bvh` (a peer dependency) for its hits.

Build from source with `npm run build` in `packages/controls`.

```ts
import {Engine, box} from 'margoengine/core';
import {OrbitControls, TransformControls} from 'margoengine/controls';

const canvas = document.createElement('canvas');
const engine = await Engine.create(canvas);
const mesh = engine.createMesh().setGeometry(box());

// Passing the engine attaches to engine.canvas and updates before every render.
const orbit = OrbitControls.attach(engine);
orbit.enableDamping = true;

const gizmo = TransformControls.attach(engine, {mode: 'translate', translationSnap: 0.25});
gizmo.attach(mesh);
gizmo.addEventListener('dragging-changed', event => {orbit.enabled = !event.value;});
addEventListener('keydown', event => {if (event.key === 'r') gizmo.setMode('rotate');});

engine.start();

// On teardown (engine.dispose() also disposes both):
gizmo.dispose(); orbit.dispose();
```

Drag core meshes and gltf/pbr models (a model moves by its `root`), with the mouse or touch:

```ts
import {Engine, box} from 'margoengine/core';
import {DragControls, OrbitControls} from 'margoengine/controls';
import {loadGLTF} from 'margoengine/gltf/pbr';

const engine = await Engine.create(document.querySelector('canvas')!);
const mesh = engine.createMesh().setGeometry(box());
const part = await loadGLTF(engine, '/part.glb');
const drag = DragControls.attach(engine, [mesh, part]);          // created before OrbitControls: a grab stops the orbit drag
const orbit = OrbitControls.attach(engine);
drag.plane = [0, 1, 0];                                        // slide on the ground; default 'view' faces the camera
drag.axis = [1, 0, 0];                                         // or only along world X
drag.addEventListener('dragstart', event => console.log(event.object, event.hit)); // hit: a bvh RaycasterHit
drag.addEventListener('hoveron', () => {engine.canvas.style.cursor = 'grab';});
drag.addEventListener('hoveroff', () => {engine.canvas.style.cursor = '';});
```

Turn by dragging, carry a set together, and reach into a hierarchy:

```ts
import {Engine, box} from 'margoengine/core';
import {DragControls} from 'margoengine/controls/drag';

const engine = await Engine.create(document.querySelector('canvas')!);
const table = engine.createMesh().setGeometry(box());
engine.createMesh().setGeometry(box()).setParent(table).setPosition([0.4, -0.5, 0.4]); // a leg
const chair = engine.createMesh().setGeometry(box()).setPosition([2, 0, 0]);
const stool = engine.createMesh().setGeometry(box()).setPosition([3, 0, 0]);
```

[README continues: https://margoengine.com/llms/packages/controls.md]

=== @margoengine/cameras (packages/cameras/README.md) ===

# @margoengine/cameras

Orthographic projection and exactly vertical (top-down) views for the core camera, with matching culling and picking.

`WideAngle` and `WideAngleCube` detach from their owning scene when disposed and
preserve same-name effects in other scenes. Device restoration keeps them attached.
Use `scene.use()` to attach their PostStack to a secondary scene:

```ts
import {Engine} from 'margoengine/core';
import {PostStack} from 'margoengine/post/stack';
import {CubeCamera} from 'margoengine/environment/cube-camera';
import {WideAngle} from 'margoengine/cameras/panini';
import {WideAngleCube} from 'margoengine/cameras/wide-cube';
const engine = await Engine.create(document.querySelector('canvas')!, {backend:'webgpu'});
const product = engine.createScene('product');
const cube = new CubeCamera({size:64});
product.use(cube);
const stack = new PostStack([new WideAngleCube({cube}), new WideAngle()]);
product.use(stack);
stack.dispose();
cube.dispose();
engine.dispose();
```

Import `margoengine/cameras` from the `margoengine` package, or `@margoengine/cameras` from this package alone; the two are the same module. Neither is on npm yet: the [Install](../../README.md#install) section lists the two routes that work today (run in a clone, or install local tarballs).

Orthographic projection and exactly vertical (top-down and bottom-up) views for core's camera, for CAD, plans, maps
and isometric views. Culling, `engine.pick`, selection, bvh rays, TAA and every pass that reads `camera.matrix` see the
same view. It uses core's `camera.project` and `camera.up` hooks.

```ts
import {Engine} from 'margoengine/core';
import {CameraProjection} from 'margoengine/cameras';
import {loadGLTF} from 'margoengine/gltf/pbr';
const canvas = document.querySelector('canvas')!;

const engine = await Engine.create(canvas, {camera: {position: [0, 40, 0], target: [0, 0, 0]}}); // straight down
const model = await loadGLTF(engine, '/model.glb');
const projection = CameraProjection.attach(engine); // orthographic, framed like the perspective view at the target

projection.mode = 'perspective';             // toggle at any time; vertical views keep working
projection.mode = 'orthographic';
projection.height = 12;                      // or fix the visible world height (resize widens with the aspect)
projection.zoom = 2;
projection.fit(model.bounds);                // frame a box: [minX, minY, minZ, maxX, maxY, maxZ], animated
projection.mode = 'perspective';
projection.fit(model.bounds, {framing: 'box'}); // move in until the box's corners fill the frame
```

- **Fitting**: `fit(bounds, {aspect, duration, padding})` takes the flat bounds array models carry (no slicing into
  min/max). Orthographic: the view direction and distance stay, the box centre moves to the view centre and `zoom` is
  set so the box's projected outline (not a bounding sphere) fills the view less `padding` (default 1.1), honouring
  `height` or `left`/`right`/`top`/`bottom`. Perspective: core's `fitToBoundingBox`. `aspect` defaults to the engine
  canvas, `duration` to 0.3 s; the engine advances the animation (after `attach(camera)` call `onPreUpdate(delta)`
  yourself). Throws `Bounds exceed far` when the box does not fit the default depth range (`camera.far` deep).
  `framing: 'box'` (perspective) keeps the view direction and field of view and moves the eye to the closest point from
  which all eight corners sit in the padded frame, so a car side-on fills 48 % of a 16:9 frame where the bounding
  sphere gave 13 %. The box is centred on screen on both axes: the tighter one touches the padded frame on both
  sides, the looser one has equal margins in pixels even when the box's near and far corners sit at different depths
  (a plate seen from above). The default, `'sphere'`, stays core's framing.
- **`fitBox(view, bounds, {aspect, padding})`** is that framing as a pure function: it returns `{position, target,
  distance, nearest}` for a `{position, target, fov, up?}` view, to set on any camera or to plan a shot without one:

```ts
import {fitBox} from 'margoengine/cameras';

const fit = fitBox({position: [0, 1, 10], target: [0, 0.7, 0], fov: 40}, [-2.3, 0, -1, 2.3, 1.5, 1], {aspect: 16 / 9});
console.log(fit.position, fit.target, fit.nearest); // nearest: the closest corner's depth, to check against camera.near
```

[README continues: https://margoengine.com/llms/packages/cameras.md]

=== @margoengine/input (packages/input/README.md) ===

# @margoengine/input

Import `margoengine/input` from the `margoengine` package, or `@margoengine/input` from this package alone; the two are the same module. Neither is on npm yet: the [Install](../../README.md#install) section lists the two routes that work today (run in a clone, or install local tarballs).

Semantic actions combine keyboard codes, mouse buttons and relative motion, gamepad axes/buttons, and touch controls.

```ts
import {Input} from 'margoengine/input';
const input = new Input({jump: [{type: 'key', code: 'Space'}]});
input.update();
const {pressed, value} = input.state('jump');
```

Call update once per simulation tick. State objects are reused. Opposing bindings sum and clamp to -1..1; gamepad axes use a configurable deadzone. createStick(parent, id) creates a pointer-captured virtual stick; bindTouchButton(button, id) supports pointer and keyboard activation. rumble(durationMs, strength, gamepadIndex) returns false when no actuator is available. dispose removes listeners and owned stick elements. Editable fields do not trigger gameplay key-down actions. Mouse motion is relative, not an absolute screen cursor.

## Chords, contexts, rebinding and prompts

```ts
import {Input, bindingLabel} from 'margoengine/input';
const input = new Input(
  {
    jump: [{type: 'key', code: 'Space'}],
    save: [{type: 'key', code: 'KeyS', modifiers: ['ctrl']}],
    confirm: [{type: 'key', code: 'Enter'}],
  },
  {contexts: {game: ['jump'], menu: ['confirm']}},
);
input.setContext('game', false); // a menu opened: jump reads 0 and releases; confirm keeps working
const prompt = bindingLabel(input.actions.save[0]); // "Ctrl+S"; gamepad buttons use 'xbox' | 'playstation' | 'generic' names
const pressed = input.captureBinding({signal: AbortSignal.timeout(10_000)}); // "press a key to rebind"
window.dispatchEvent(new KeyboardEvent('keydown', {code: 'KeyJ'})); // stands in for the player's key press
const binding = await pressed;
input.rebind('jump', [binding]);
localStorage.setItem('bindings', JSON.stringify(input.exportBindings()));
input.importBindings(localStorage.getItem('bindings')!); // unknown actions are ignored; invalid data changes nothing
input.resetBindings();
```

- `modifiers` (`'shift' | 'ctrl' | 'alt' | 'meta'`) on a `key` binding makes a chord: the key counts only while every modifier is held.
- `contexts` (option) group actions; an action owned by contexts reads 0 unless one is enabled. Unlisted actions are always active.
- `captureBinding` resolves with the next key (with held modifiers), mouse button or gamepad button; Escape or the signal rejects with `AbortError`. A modifier pressed alone waits: Ctrl then S gives Ctrl+S, and Shift pressed and released alone gives Shift. A gamepad button already held when the prompt opens counts only after it is released and pressed again.
- Mouse buttons follow Pointer Events chords: a second button pressed or released during a drag counts, though the browser sends it as a `pointermove`.

## Tap, hold, slow tap and double press

`@margoengine/input/interactions` turns a press into what the player meant. Rules are named, like actions, and read any action, or one binding of it:

```ts
import {Input} from 'margoengine/input';
import {Interactions} from 'margoengine/input/interactions';

const input = new Input({
  use: [{type: 'key', code: 'KeyE'}, {type: 'gamepad-button', index: 2}],
  dodge: [{type: 'key', code: 'KeyD'}],
  fire: [{type: 'gamepad-button', index: 7}],
});
const rules = new Interactions(input, {
  open: {type: 'tap', action: 'use'},
  inspect: {type: 'hold', action: 'use', time: 600},
  dash: {type: 'double-press', action: 'dodge'},
  heavy: {type: 'slow-tap', action: 'fire', threshold: 0.8},
  padOnly: {type: 'hold', action: 'use', binding: 1},
});
function tick() {
  input.update();
  rules.update();
  if (rules.state('open').performed) console.log('open');
  if (rules.state('dash').performed) console.log('dash');
  const charge = rules.state('heavy').progress; // 0 to 1, for a charge bar
  console.log(charge);
}
tick();
```

- `tap`: pressed and released within `time` (default 200 ms). Performed on release.
- `hold`: held for `time` (default 400 ms). Performed while still held.
- `slow-tap`: held for at least `time` (default 500 ms), then released. Performed on release.
- `double-press`: `count` presses (default 2), each shorter than `time` (default 200 ms), each within `gap` (default 300 ms) of the last release. Performed on the last press.
- `binding` (default: the whole action): an index into `input.actions[action]`, so a rule can read one device; after a rebind it reads what is bound there.
- `threshold` (default 0.5): magnitude that counts as pressed, for triggers and sticks. The press ends at three quarters of it, so noise at the press point cannot flicker.
- Option `now` (default `performance.now`): the clock in milliseconds.

[README continues: https://margoengine.com/llms/packages/input.md]

=== @margoengine/ui (packages/ui/README.md) ===

# @margoengine/ui

Import `margoengine/ui` from the `margoengine` package, or `@margoengine/ui` from this package alone; the two are the same module. Neither is on npm yet: the [Install](../../README.md#install) section lists the two routes that work today (run in a clone, or install local tarballs).

Game UI that is drawn inside the engine, so it works in fullscreen and in exported games, with no DOM on top of the
canvas:

- **Widgets:** panels, labels, buttons, toggles, sliders, progress and health bars, lists, inventory grids, menus,
  dialogs, toasts and tooltips.
- **Layout:** anchors, flex-style rows and columns, grids, scrolling, safe areas.
- **Scaling:** a reference resolution, the device pixel ratio and the user's text size, with text that stays sharp
  because it is drawn by `@margoengine/text` as signed distance fields.
- **Themes:** a good-looking dark theme by default, a light theme, a high contrast theme, and `createTheme` for your own.
  All status colours come from the colour-blind-safe Okabe-Ito palette and meaning never rests on colour alone.

The package is optional and tree-shakable and adds nothing to core. `Ui` holds the widgets and produces a list of
rectangles and text in pixels; it touches neither the GPU nor the DOM, so it runs in Node and in tests.
`UiRenderer` is the engine plugin that draws that list, on WebGPU and on core's WebGL2 preview backend alike.

```ts
import { Engine } from '@margoengine/core';
import { Ui, UiRenderer, Menu } from '@margoengine/ui';

const engine = await Engine.create(document.querySelector('canvas')!);
const ui = new Ui(); // dark theme, 1 UI unit = 1 CSS pixel, system font
UiRenderer.attach(engine, ui); // steps the UI every frame and draws it over the finished frame

ui.add(
  new Menu({
    title: 'Paused',
    items: [
      { label: 'Resume', onSelect: () => ui.toast('Back in the game') },
      { label: 'Quit', onSelect: async () => (await ui.confirm('Quit to the title screen?')) && location.reload() },
    ],
  }),
);
```

## Building a screen

Every widget is a class you construct with an options object. Put them in a `Panel` (a column by default) and add the
panel to `ui`. Layout options are on every widget.

```ts
import { Ui, Panel, Label, Button, Toggle, Slider } from '@margoengine/ui';

const ui = new Ui();
const settings = new Panel({
  background: 'surface',
  border: true,
  shadow: true,
  padding: 24,
  gap: 12,
  width: 360,
  anchor: 'center',
  children: [
    new Label({ text: 'Settings', size: 'title' }),
    new Slider({ text: 'Volume', value: 0.8, onChange: (e) => console.log('volume', e.value) }),
    new Toggle({ text: 'Subtitles', checked: true, onChange: (e) => console.log('subtitles', e.value) }),
    new Button({ text: 'Done', variant: 'primary', onClick: () => settings.removeFromParent() }),
  ],
});
ui.add(settings);
```

`on(type, handler)` works on every widget and returns a function that unsubscribes; it is also disposable, so
`using off = button.on('click', fn)` ends the subscription at the end of the block. Option callbacks (`onClick`,
`onChange`, `onSelect`) are shortcuts for `on('click' | 'change' | 'select', ...)`.

## Layout

Sizes are UI units. By default one unit is one CSS pixel; see Scaling.

`arrange` shares measurements of the same node and available width within one call. A custom
`LayoutNode.measure` returns a stable content size for that width during the call. The next call
measures again, so direct edits to styles, children or content take effect without an invalidation API.
The cache belongs to that call, including when a measurer starts a separate layout.

```ts
import { arrange, type LayoutNode } from '@margoengine/ui';

const label: LayoutNode = {
  style: {}, children: [], rect: { x: 0, y: 0, width: 0, height: 0 },
  measure: (width) => ({ width: Math.min(80, width), height: 20 }),
};
const row: LayoutNode = {
  style: { direction: 'row', align: 'center' }, children: [label],
  rect: { x: 0, y: 0, width: 0, height: 0 },
};
arrange(row, { x: 0, y: 0, width: 200, height: 100 });
console.log(label.rect); // { x: 0, y: 40, width: 80, height: 20 }
```

[README continues: https://margoengine.com/llms/packages/ui.md]

=== @margoengine/viewcube (packages/viewcube/README.md) ===

# @margoengine/viewcube

Import `margoengine/viewcube` from the `margoengine` package, or `@margoengine/viewcube` from this package alone; the two are the same module. Neither is on npm yet: the [Install](../../README.md#install) section lists the two routes that work today (run in a clone, or install local tarballs).

A CAD orientation cube for Margo Engine: a small cube in a corner of the view that turns with the camera. Click a face,
edge or corner and the camera animates around its target to that view (Top, Front, Right, ..., the twelve edge views
and the eight isometric corners), keeping the distance. With `@margoengine/cameras` it also toggles perspective and
orthographic projection.

```ts
import {Engine} from 'margoengine/core';
import {CameraProjection} from 'margoengine/cameras';
import {OrbitControls} from 'margoengine/controls';
import {ViewCube} from 'margoengine/viewcube';
const canvas = document.querySelector('canvas')!;

const engine = await Engine.create(canvas);           // the canvas needs a parent element; the cube is placed in it
const projection = CameraProjection.attach(engine, {mode: 'perspective'});
OrbitControls.attach(engine);                             // or the stage's CADCameraControls
const cube = ViewCube.attach(engine, {projection});       // omit projection to hide the toggle

cube.view('top');                                      // 'top' | 'bottom' | 'front' | 'back' | 'left' | 'right' | 'iso'
cube.view([1, 1, 0]);                                  // any direction from the target toward the camera
cube.view('front', 0);                                 // jump without animating
cube.setProjection('orthographic');
cube.setTheme('dark');                                 // 'light' | 'dark' | 'high-contrast' | 'auto' | your own tokens
cube.drag = false;                                     // dragging the cube orbits the camera unless turned off
cube.setHome({position: [6, 4, 8], target: [0, 1, 0]}); // your own home view; shows the home button
cube.home();                                           // the home button and the Home key do the same
cube.roll(1);                                          // a quarter turn counter-clockwise about the view axis (-1 clockwise)
cube.dispose();                                        // engine.dispose() also disposes it
```

For less than a cube, `margoengine/viewcube/axes` (`@margoengine/viewcube/axes`) has an axis triad: X, Y and Z
balls on sticks and a smaller ball at each negative end, turning with the camera.

```ts
import {Engine} from 'margoengine/core';
import {AxisTriad} from 'margoengine/viewcube/axes';
const canvas = document.querySelector('canvas')!;

const engine = await Engine.create(canvas);
const triad = AxisTriad.attach(engine, {corner: 'bottom-left', home: true}); // every ViewCube option works
triad.view('right');                                   // a ViewCube in every other way
```

Options: `container` (default: the canvas's parent; made `position: relative` if it is static), `corner`
(`'top-right'` default, `'top-left'`, `'bottom-right'`, `'bottom-left'`), `size` (cube edge in CSS pixels, 80),
`duration` (seconds, 0.4), `projection` (a CameraProjection, or anything with `mode`), `labels` (face names, for
translation), `flip` (false; also a public field: clicking the view already shown turns to the opposite one, as
Blender's navigation gizmo and SolidWorks' "Normal To" pressed twice do; Autodesk's ViewCube keeps the view),
`drag` (true; also a public field: dragging the cube orbits the camera), `home` (none; a `{position, target}`, or
`true` for the camera as it is when the cube attaches: shows the home button), `roll` (false; shows the two roll
buttons), `theme` (none: the light colours; see Themes).
`@margoengine/controls` navigation profiles carry it: `ViewCube.attach(engine, {...BLENDER.viewCube})`. The toggle
also follows projection changes made elsewhere (Blender's numpad 5 through a profile) on the next frame.
`cube.element` is the widget root for your own styling.

[README continues: https://margoengine.com/llms/packages/viewcube.md]

=== @margoengine/selection (packages/selection/README.md) ===

# @margoengine/selection

GPU picking and visible mesh selection outlines.

Import `margoengine/selection` from the `margoengine` package, or `@margoengine/selection` from this package alone; the two are the same module. Neither is on npm yet: the [Install](../../README.md#install) section lists the two routes that work today (run in a clone, or install local tarballs).

Objects shown as an imposter of `@margoengine/lod` outline too: an engine plugin with `drawSelectionMask` (`SelectionMaskSource`) marks what it draws in the same mask, and a `LODSystem` does so for any object whose anchor or level is selected.

Visible core and PBR selection outlines using Jump Flood Algorithm distance fields or circular morphological dilation. `Selection.set` discovers glTF PBR/FBX buffers from their loader-owned mesh nodes; no separate outline registration is required.

```ts
import {Selection} from 'margoengine/selection';
import {Engine} from 'margoengine/core';
import {box} from 'margoengine/core';
const engine = await Engine.create(document.querySelector('canvas')!);
const mesh = engine.createMesh().setGeometry(box());
const selection = Selection.attach(engine, {algorithm: 'jfa', width: 3, color: [1,0.5,0]});
selection.set([mesh]);
engine.start();
// On teardown: selection.dispose(); engine.dispose();
```

`Picking.attach(engine)` enables faster `engine.pick(x, y)` in canvas CSS pixels:

```ts
import {Picking} from 'margoengine/selection';
import {Engine} from 'margoengine/core';
const x = 0;
const y = 0;
const engine = await Engine.create(document.querySelector('canvas')!);
const picking = Picking.attach(engine);
const mesh = await engine.pick(x, y);
```

The standard core PBR draw writes a second `r32uint` attachment in the same pass, with no extra draw calls. A pick copies a clipped 3×3 neighborhood from that frame when camera, mesh identities, geometry, transforms, visibility, materials and frame-graph revision match. Otherwise it renders a 3×3 micro frustum, rejecting each instance's bounding sphere before batching the survivors. The sphere test stays conservative under nonuniform scale, mirrored transforms and hierarchy shear. Zero means background; stored IDs are core slots plus one, so slot zero remains selectable.

The center wins. For an empty center, orthogonal neighbors win before diagonals, with a deterministic tie order. Coordinates and neighbors are bounded to the canvas. Readback remains asynchronous and one pick may be pending at a time. A reusable 768-byte staging buffer accommodates WebGPU's 256-byte row pitch. Device restoration recreates resources; removal or engine disposal frees them.

`Picking.attach(engine, {capture: false})` leaves the frame untouched (no second color target, no per-frame mesh snapshot) and renders the culled 3x3 pass for every pick; use it when picks are rare and frame rate matters more. Custom scene pipelines fall back to the micro pass; sections also use that pass so mutable core clipping uniforms stay current. Other mutable custom shader effects should render their changed state before picking. The cached ID texture costs four bytes per viewport pixel; the package remains optional and tree-shakable.

The cached ID texture is written by the colour pass itself, so its coverage matches the drawn pixels exactly. The separate 3x3 pass rasterises again with its own shader; 100 km from the origin its edges can differ from the colour by a pixel unless a `FloatingOrigin` (`@margoengine/cameras/origin`) keeps the scene near local zero ([limits](../../docs/limits.md), `npm run test:browser:far-origin`).

## Many points at once

A plain loop of `engine.pick`, awaited or under `Promise.all`, costs one readback a point and this package cannot merge them: core's queue answers overlapping picks one at a time and calls `onPick` for the next only when the last has finished, so a plugin never sees two at once. Merging them would be a core change.

`picking.pickMany(points)` answers many canvas CSS pixels from one GPU readback, where a loop of `engine.pick` waits for one
readback each. It answers what `engine.pick` answers, as `PickHit`s, in
order, with null for a miss or a point off the canvas. All points read the scene as it is at the call's turn in the pick
queue. Pass a `view` as the second argument to pick through it; with several views and no `view`, points outside the first
point's view are picked one at a time.

When the captured ID texture is current, the batch checks the scene once and submits all neighborhood copies in
one command buffer. Micro passes keep their per-point submissions so each reads its own camera and instance uploads.
Their sphere tests compute matrix rows only as each plane is reached, with unchanged arithmetic and culling results.

[README continues: https://margoengine.com/llms/packages/selection.md]

=== @margoengine/audio (packages/audio/README.md) ===

# @margoengine/audio

Web Audio listener, global and positional sounds and a frequency analyser for Margo Engine.

Pose writes read the three stored vector components directly. They preserve the existing parameter scheduling,
smoothing and clock-read order. This removes vector-iterator work; it does not establish a measured speedup.
For a self-contained offline example with no audio device or user gesture:

```ts
import {AudioListener, PositionalAudio} from '@margoengine/audio';

const context = new OfflineAudioContext(2, 4800, 48000);
const listener = new AudioListener({context, autoResume: false, smoothing: 0});
const sound = new PositionalAudio(listener);
const oscillator = context.createOscillator();
sound.setNodeSource(oscillator);
sound.setPosition(1, 0, -2).setDirection([0, 0, 1]);
oscillator.start();
const rendered = await context.startRendering();
console.assert(rendered.length === 4800 && rendered.numberOfChannels === 2);
listener.dispose();
```

Import `margoengine/audio` from the `margoengine` package, or `@margoengine/audio` from this package alone; the two are the same module. Neither is on npm yet: the [Install](../../README.md#install) section lists the two routes that work today (run in a clone, or install local tarballs).

Web Audio listener, global and positional sounds, encoded-file loading and a frequency analyser for Margo Engine.

Build from source with `npm run build` in `packages/audio`.

For the loading examples, serve `tests/fixtures/rain-foa.wav` at `/sounds/rain-foa.wav` (CC BY 4.0, attribution in `tests/fixtures/NOTICE.md`). Replace this shared sample with your app's engine, cue and step recordings.

```ts
import {AudioListener, Audio, PositionalAudio, AudioVoicePool, AudioAnalyser} from 'margoengine/audio';
import {Engine} from 'margoengine/core';
import {createMesh} from 'margoengine/materials';
import {box} from 'margoengine/core';
const timeline = {seconds: 0, playing: true, speed: 1};
const meter = document.createElement('div');
const x = 0;
const y = 0;
const z = 0;
const engine = await Engine.create(document.querySelector('canvas')!);
const truck = engine.createMesh().setGeometry(box());

const listener = AudioListener.attach(engine, {volume: 0.8}); // follows engine.camera every frame; resumes on the first click or key press

const engineSound = new PositionalAudio(listener, {
  mesh: truck, refDistance: 2, distanceModel: 'inverse', rolloffFactor: 1.2,
  coneInnerAngle: 90, coneOuterAngle: 220, coneOuterGain: 0.3, muteWhenHidden: true,
});
engineSound.setBuffer(await listener.load('/sounds/rain-foa.wav'));
engineSound.loop = true;
engineSound.fadeIn(0.5);

const music = new Audio(listener, {volume: 0.4});
music.setMediaElementSource(document.querySelector('audio')!).play();

// A sound on an editor timeline: starts at timeline second 4, follows play, pause, scrubbing and timeline speed.
const cue = new Audio(listener, {volume: 0.6, loop: false, timelineStart: 4});
cue.setBuffer(await listener.load('/sounds/rain-foa.wav'));
engine.onFrame(() => cue.sync(timeline.seconds, timeline.playing, timeline.speed));

// Footsteps and block sounds: 6 voices share one buffer; a 7th overlapping play steals the oldest voice.
const steps = new AudioVoicePool(listener, await listener.load('/sounds/rain-foa.wav'), {voices: 6, refDistance: 2});
steps.play([x, y, z], {volume: 0.7, playbackRate: 0.9 + Math.random() * 0.2});

const analyser = new AudioAnalyser(music, 1024);
engine.onFrame(() => meter.style.width = `${analyser.getAverageFrequency() / 2.55}%`);

// On teardown (engine.dispose() does this too):
engine.removePlugin(listener.name);
```

## Cancel a load, and clean up with `using`

```ts
import {AudioListener, Audio} from 'margoengine/audio';

using listener = new AudioListener({volume: 0.8}); // disposed at the end of the block
const buffer = await listener.load('/sounds/rain-foa.wav', {signal: AbortSignal.timeout(10_000)}); // rejects with an AbortError
using step = new Audio(listener).setBuffer(buffer);
step.play();
```

Errors carry a stable `code` (`error.code`): `disposed` for a sound used after `dispose()`, `state` for `play()` before a source is set, `unsupported` when Web Audio or `fetch` is missing, `failed` for an HTTP or decoding failure. Each message says what to do.

## How it works

=== @margoengine/mixer (packages/mixer/README.md) ===

# @margoengine/mixer

Import `margoengine/mixer` from the `margoengine` package, or `@margoengine/mixer` from this package alone; the two are the same module. Neither is on npm yet: the [Install](../../README.md#install) section lists the two routes that work today (run in a clone, or install local tarballs).

Audio mixing and effects on Web Audio, as a sibling of `@margoengine/audio`: a tree of buses with fader, mute, solo, sends and ducking; an effects chain (equaliser, filter, compressor, limiter, delay, convolution reverb); positional emitters; and deterministic offline rendering so a chain can be rendered and its numbers compared in a test. Nothing touches `AudioContext` at import time, and the package adds nothing to core.

```ts
import { Mixer, renderOffline, measure } from 'margoengine/mixer';

// Live: mix before the listener, so the camera-following AudioListener from margoengine/audio stays the last stage.
//   using mixer = new Mixer(listener.context, {destination: listener.input, buses: {...}});
// Offline (runs in a browser; the same calls work on a live AudioContext):
const buffer = await renderOffline({ seconds: 2, sampleRate: 48000, mixer: { effects: [{ type: 'limiter', ceiling: -1 }] } }, ({ context, mixer }) => {
  mixer.createBus('music', { gain: -6, effects: [{ type: 'eq', bands: [{ type: 'lowshelf', frequency: 120, gain: 3 }] }] });
  mixer.createBus('voice');
  const reverb = mixer.createBus('room', { effects: [{ type: 'reverb', seconds: 1.5, mix: 1 }], soloSafe: true });
  mixer.bus('voice').send(reverb, { gain: -9 });

  const tone = new OscillatorNode(context, { frequency: 220 });
  mixer.route(tone, 'music');
  tone.start(0);
  tone.stop(2);

  // Lower the music by 12 dB from 0.5 s to 1.2 s for a line of dialogue.
  const duck = mixer.bus('music').duck({ amount: 12, attack: 0.05, at: 0.5 });
  duck.release({ at: 1.2, seconds: 0.3 });
});
const { peak, rms } = measure(buffer.getChannelData(0));
```

## Buses

`new Mixer(context, {destination, gain, effects, buses})` makes a `master` bus and any buses you list. `mixer.createBus(name, {parent, gain, muted, solo, soloSafe, effects})` adds one that feeds its parent (default master). Each bus is `input -> effects -> fader -> duck -> mute/solo gate -> output`.

- **Gain** in dB: `bus.setGain(-6, {at, seconds})`. Changes move smoothly (about 20 ms) unless the context has not started or `seconds` is 0, so there are no clicks and an offline render starts at the right level.
- **Mute and solo**: `bus.setMuted(true)`, `bus.setSolo(true)`. While anything is soloed, only soloed buses, their ancestors (which carry the sound on), their descendants (which feed them) and `soloSafe` buses such as reverb returns stay audible. A solo-safe bus still plays through its parent, so put returns straight under `master`: under a group that no solo reaches, its sound stops at the group's closed gate. `audibleBuses(states)` is that rule as a pure function, one gate per bus.
- **Sends**: `bus.send(other, {gain, pre})` copies part of a bus to another (after the gate by default, so muting the bus mutes the send; `pre` taps before the fader). A send that would make a loop throws `RangeError`. `send.remove()` may be called more than once, and removing a bus with `mixer.removeBus` also disconnects every send to it. The function `mixer.route` returns undoes that route once, and does nothing after the source was routed again.
- **Ducking**: `bus.duck({amount, attack, at})` lowers a bus and returns a handle; `handle.release({at, seconds})` brings it back. Overlapping ducks hold the deepest one. You decide when to duck (when a voice starts); automatic audio-clock detection is available in the optional `mixer/sidechain` entry below.
- **Routing**: `mixer.route(source, bus)` connects an AudioNode, or anything with `getOutput()` such as `Audio` and `PositionalAudio` from `margoengine/audio`, to a bus after removing its other connections. Configure the sound's filters first.
- **Scheduling** uses AudioContext time: every `at` is `context.currentTime` seconds (default now), and `mixer.now` reads the clock.
- `bus.peak()` reads the current output peak (it adds an AnalyserNode on first use).

Invalid numeric fades are rejected before bus targets, gates, duck membership or existing automation
change. Times/durations must be finite and nonnegative; parameter values must fit finite float32.
Gain is checked before it reaches a node (-Infinity dB remains silence). Invalid duck releases
leave the handle active so it can be released correctly. An omitted or undefined release duration
keeps 0.4 s; gate fades keep their 0.01 s default.

## Effects

Effects are plain objects, so a chain can be stored as JSON: `bus.setEffects([...])`, or `createEffect(context, spec)` for one effect.

[README continues: https://margoengine.com/llms/packages/mixer.md]

=== @margoengine/physics (packages/physics/README.md) ===

# @margoengine/physics

Import `margoengine/physics` from the `margoengine` package, or `@margoengine/physics` from this package alone; the two are the same module. Neither is on npm yet: the [Install](../../README.md#install) section lists the two routes that work today (run in a clone, or install local tarballs).

Rigid-body physics for Margo Engine on its own Rust kernel (compiled to WebAssembly with SIMD, shipped inside the package): a fixed-step engine plugin with interpolation, colliders (compound and convex-decomposed ones included), joints (rope and spring included), ropes and chains, ray-cast vehicles, scene queries, collision events and a character controller.

Build from source with `npm run build` in `packages/physics`.

It exports `Physics` (the world: bodies, colliders, joints, queries and events), `PhysicsBody`, `PhysicsJoint`, `CharacterController`, `Vehicle` and `Rope`. The React components in `@margoengine/react/physics` are `<Physics>`, `<RigidBody>`, the collider components (`CuboidCollider`, `BallCollider` and others), `useJoint`, `usePhysics`, `useBeforePhysicsStep` and `useAfterPhysicsStep`. The solver comes with this package, nothing else to install: the kernel's WebAssembly is a blueprint inside the JavaScript, compiled by `await Physics.load()`.

```ts
import {Engine, PbrMaterial, box} from 'margoengine/core';
import {Physics, collisionGroups} from 'margoengine/physics';

await Physics.load();
const canvas = document.querySelector('canvas')!;
const engine = await Engine.create(canvas);
const physics = new Physics(engine); // registers itself with engine.use()

const floor = engine.createMesh().setGeometry(box(20, 1, 20)).setPosition([0, -0.5, 0]);
physics.addBody(floor, {type: 'fixed'});                 // box collider fitted to the geometry

const crate = engine.createMesh().setGeometry(box()).setMaterial(new PbrMaterial({color: '#c08040'})).setPosition([0, 5, 0]);
const body = physics.addBody(crate, {colliders: {shape: 'box', restitution: 0.3, density: 2}});
body.applyImpulse([0, 2, 0]);

// Hinge with limits and a motor.
const frameBody = physics.addBody(null, {type: 'fixed', position: [2, 1, 0], colliders: []});
const doorMesh = engine.createMesh().setGeometry(box(1, 2, 0.1)).setPosition([2.5, 1, 0]);
const door = physics.addBody(doorMesh, {colliders: {shape: 'box', halfExtents: [0.5, 1, 0.05]}});
physics.addJoint(frameBody, door, {type: 'revolute', anchorB: [-0.5, 0, 0], axis: [0, 1, 0], limits: [0, Math.PI / 2], motor: {targetVelocity: 1}});

// Queries return the core Mesh that was hit.
const hit = physics.raycast(engine.camera.position, [0, -1, 0]);
hit?.mesh; hit?.distance; hit?.point; hit?.normal;

// Events with the meshes involved.
physics.on('contactstart', ({meshA, meshB}) => {});
physics.on('intersectionstart', ({bodyA, bodyB}) => {}); // sensors

// Character controller on a kinematic capsule, driven once per fixed step.
const input = {x: 0, z: 1}; // from your keyboard or gamepad handling
const playerMesh = engine.createMesh().setGeometry(box(0.6, 1.6, 0.6)).setPosition([-2, 1, 0]);
const player = physics.addBody(playerMesh, {type: 'kinematicPosition', colliders: {shape: 'capsule', halfHeight: 0.5, radius: 0.3}});
const controller = physics.createCharacterController(player, {maxSlopeClimbAngle: Math.PI / 4, autostep: {maxHeight: 0.3, minWidth: 0.2}, snapToGround: 0.2});
physics.on('beforestep', dt => controller.move([input.x * 4 * dt, -9.81 * dt, input.z * 4 * dt]));

engine.start(); // each frame's delta drives the accumulator
// On teardown: physics.dispose(), engine.removePlugin('physics') or engine.dispose().
```

## Sediment transport and bed change

`@margoengine/physics/sediment` reads shallow-water depth and discharge and routes suspended and bedload sediment.
It contributes the Exner elevation change to the same TerrainBed. Water then runs over the updated surface.

```ts
import { TerrainBed } from '@margoengine/physics/earth';
import { ShallowWaterSolver } from '@margoengine/physics/hydro';
import { SedimentTransport } from '@margoengine/physics/sediment';
import { PhysicsWorld } from '@margoengine/physics/world';

const grid = { columns: 4, rows: 2, width: 16, depth: 8, centre: [8, 4] as const };
const terrain = new TerrainBed();
const sediment = await SedimentTransport.load();
const world = new PhysicsWorld({ rate: { num: 60, den: 1 } });
world.add(terrain, { ...grid, elevations: () => 0 });
world.add(new ShallowWaterSolver(), {
  bed: terrain.bed,
  depth: 1,
  velocity: () => [1, 0],
  sides: { maxX: 'open' },
});
world.add(sediment, {
  grid,
  mobileDepth: 0.1,
  grainDiameter: 0.0003,
  open: { maxX: true },
});
world.advance(120);
console.log(sediment.read(1, 0), sediment.budget, terrain.volume());
```
